regular EFI files are present, and the selected target is GPT with FAT.
Persistence suppresses the hybrid choice. Pure DD and DD-required images return

`ApplyIsoPolicy`, including reports whose `is_iso` transition the Linux UI
intentionally leaves untouched.

`GetImageWriteMode` resolves the original `SelectionDialog` row bit into a named
mode. This matters because DD is row two without ESP and row three with it.
Cancel, a missing choice and invalid/multiple row bits return no mode. The
Windows caller retains its existing localized dialog, flags and later boot
checks; it no longer duplicates the two dialog-building branches. The ESP size
constant moves to the already shared report header with the same value. No

`ImageModeDialog` implements the ISOHybrid dialog using Qt6 Widgets: original
message and choice captions, native question icon, exclusive radio buttons,
ISO selected first and OK as the default button, followed by Cancel. Enter
accepts, arrow keys change the radio choice, and Cancel/Escape/window close
return no operation. A fresh dialog always starts at ISO. There are no authored

The selection controller exposes choices only after analysis has completed.

or start writing. Native ISO extraction and ISO → ESP are not implemented by
this checkpoint. The separate Windows ISO-to-ESP-only prompt is also outside

## CP10c: native ISO/UDF tree extraction (2026-09-15)

Completed the paused ordinary-file extraction component. `WalkIsoFiles` and
`WalkUdfFiles` now supply shared traversal inside the existing `iso_scan.c`
module. Scan accounting is a named synchronous C visitor; native extraction is
another. This keeps the original accounting, selected image view, directory
limits and UDF iterator ownership in one place. The visitor has no Qt or GUI
dependency; reporting and cancellation retain their named host entry points.
No Windows build entries or platform conditionals were added for this split.

Linux's `ExtractIsoTree` retains the source descriptor and opens the selected
ISO/UDF view through that descriptor. It rechecks source identity before,
during and after copying, including pathname replacement and content changes
with restored mtime. A preflight walk rejects unsupported links/special entries
and incomplete/deep trees before creating output. The second walk copies into
a caller-owned private empty directory using descriptor-relative operations,
exclusive file creation and no symlink traversal. Files and directories are
flushed. A failed current file is removed; earlier completed entries remain and
the whole output is incomplete. Data buffers stay fixed at 1 MiB plus the
existing reader's 32 KiB cache.

The root `ldlinux.sys` exclusion is now a shared file property, used by both the
Windows extraction check and Linux. Nested loaders remain ordinary files.
There are no payload substitutions or configuration rewrites in this component.

**57 generated-image functional cases pass**, with independent inspection of
names, directory structure and complete contents. Coverage includes:

- ISO9660, Rock Ridge, Joliet and UDF; Unicode, spaces, nested/empty directories,
  empty files, chunk boundaries, and fragmented UDF short/long allocations.
- A UDF name differing from the ISO view, root-loader exclusion, preservation
  of nested loaders and unchanged configuration contents.
- Cancellation before analysis, after analysis and during copying/flushing;
  successful retry in the same process after a cancelled write.
- Source mutation/replacement, short writes, EINTR, zero/failed writes, failed
  reads, file/directory flush failures and close failures. These faults are
  exercised for both ISO and UDF, with exact partial counts and descriptor checks.
- Existing output preservation, a replaced parent directory, unsupported
  entries, invalid/truncated images and deep-directory rejection.

Fault injection exists only in the test executable through link-time wrappers.
The extractor has no testing switches and does not access devices or mounts.
The shared file-property suite now passes **703 checks**. Existing tree, analysis,
Widgets, mode-dialog and raw-writing regressions all pass after the refactor.

The full normal suite passes **44/44 CTest entries (53.13 seconds)**. The full
**ASan/UBSan/leak-check suite passes 44/44 (78.21 seconds)** with no sanitizer
findings. Both include the optional independent system-wimlib comparison.
Normal and sanitizer builds use CMake/Ninja with default parallelism. Existing
dependency warnings remain. Windows build/runtime validation is still deferred;
these Linux results do not qualify the Windows application. No new VM boot or

## CP10d: native FAT32 formatting in image files (2026-09-15)

`linux/platform/fat_format.c` adds one concrete native adapter,
`FormatFat32Image`. It quick-formats an explicit region of an existing regular
file with dosfstools `mkfs.fat`, passing the retained descriptor through
`posix_spawn` instead of reopening the caller's pathname. Structured arguments
specify offset, size, cluster size, label and volume ID, with two FATs and backup
boot metadata. No shell or new generic process framework is involved.
The [dosfstools 4.2 implementation](https://github.com/dosfstools/dosfstools/blob/v4.2/src/mkfs.fat.c)
was checked for offset/block units, argument validation, alignment and writes.

The adapter validates the file range and access flags before starting. Its
current subset uses 512-byte sectors, explicit power-of-two clusters from 512
through 32768 bytes, and already normalized uppercase ASCII labels. It checks
that the region can hold a standard FAT32 cluster count; choosing Rufus's
allowed/default cluster sizes and full label normalization remain caller work.
No alternative UI defaults or filename-based media choices were introduced.

Cancellation uses the existing named C job query. Diagnostics are capped at
4095 bytes while excess output is drained. Cancellation or a 120-second timeout
sends TERM, escalates to KILL after 500 ms when needed, and reaps the child.
After any started operation the target is flushed, including failure/cancel
paths; the result retains child status, signal and any flush error. Success
also requires unchanged target size, expected boot-sector fields and a readable
root through Rufus's existing `libfat`. Its FAT structures/readers are reused
unchanged. The caller retains descriptor flags and seek position.

**35 functional cases pass.** Real native formats cover 64 MiB/512-byte clusters,
128 MiB/1024-byte clusters, 512 MiB/4096-byte clusters and 2.25 GiB/32768-byte
clusters, including a volume at offset zero and partition-like regions at 1 MiB.
Tests independently decode geometry/label/ID, compare both FATs and backup boot
metadata, run `fsck.fat -n` on an exact sparse copy of the volume and use mtools
to list the original image at its offset. All bytes preceding and following
the requested region are checked against guards. Native track rounding is
reported explicitly; less than 63 sectors can remain unused inside the region.

Other cases cover a replaced pathname while its original descriptor remains
open, unsupported geometry/labels/access modes, non-regular descriptors, missing
tools, nonzero exits, signals, excessive/early-closed output, changed file size,
flush failure/EINTR, cancellation, forced termination, timeout and recovery.
They check descriptor ownership and that no child remains. Controlled fake
formatters and fault wrappers exist only in tests; timeout testing advances
the test clock rather than waiting two minutes. Tests use only disposable files,
with no device, mount, root prompt or production testing switch.

The full normal suite passes **45/45 CTest entries (56.02 seconds)**. The full
**ASan/UBSan/leak-check suite passes 45/45 (118.08 seconds)** with no sanitizer
findings, including all 57 ISO/UDF extraction cases and the optional independent
system-wimlib comparator. Both CMake/Ninja builds use default parallelism. The
new formatter/probe compile without warnings; existing upstream wimlib warnings
remain. Logs are `/tmp/rufus-cp10d-build-final.log`,
`/tmp/rufus-cp10d-tests.log`, `/tmp/rufus-cp10d-sanitizer-build.log` and
`/tmp/rufus-cp10d-sanitizer-tests.log`. These temporary logs are not durable.
Build/dependency paths are the same as CP10c. New test executables `fsck.fat`
and `mdir` come from the already required dosfstools and mtools packages.

**Next bounded checkpoint:** create one Rufus-compatible partition layout in a
disposable image using an established Linux facility, independently inspect the
table, and format only its recorded partition extent. Real-device formatting
through authorized services, mounting and extraction integration follow later.
This checkpoint does not create a partition table, erase old data or install a

## CP10e: shared placement and native GPT images (2026-09-15)

`src/partition_layout.c` extracts Rufus's first-partition offset and main-partition
length calculations from `drive.c`. Windows now calls those same functions;
its disk APIs, formatter and remaining partition choices stay in the Windows
implementation. The shared code preserves the modern 1 MiB start, legacy BIOS
track/cluster adjustment and main-length rounding order. Windows build manifests
register the new source/header. This is a small policy extraction, with no Qt
dependency or new platform conditionals.

Linux's `CreateGptImagePartition` uses native libfdisk through a retained regular
file descriptor. It creates one ordinary GPT "Main Data Partition" with the
Microsoft Basic Data type, 128 entries and Rufus's shared placement calculations.
The initial subset accepts 512-byte sectors and explicit geometry/cluster sizes.
It checks the prepared table, rechecks file size before writing, flushes every
attempted write and verifies the result through a fresh library context. Recovery
from a damaged GPT copy is rejected during that verification. The caller retains
the descriptor, flags and seek position; cancellation uses the existing C entry
point. No device, mount, privilege prompt or bootloader operation is involved.

The [libfdisk descriptor API](https://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/utils/util-linux/v2.41/libfdisk-docs/libfdisk-Context.html)
supports this image-only checkpoint without a loop device or helper process.
[UDisks partition creation](https://storaged.org/doc/udisks2-api/latest/gdbus-org.freedesktop.UDisks2.PartitionTable.html)
can adjust requested offsets and sizes, so its returned bounds must be checked
when integrating real devices. UDisks2/polkit remains the first choice for their
authorized operations. Linux CMake requires libfdisk development files through
pkg-config (`fdisk >= 2.35`); CI also installs the `sfdisk` test utility.

Integration caught two behavior differences. Rufus can produce an odd number
of 512-byte sectors, so the FAT32 adapter now accepts sector-aligned extents and
disables mkfs.fat's additional alignment for odd lengths. The explicit block
count remains in KiB; the filesystem may leave its final sector unused, without
changing the partition bounds. Replacing an existing GPT also reset libfdisk's
first-usable-sector override. In-memory header settings now preserve sector 34
on both initial creation and replacement.

**2,527 portable checks** compare the shared arithmetic with the original
formulas across sector, track, cluster and disk sizes, including legacy starts,
reserved tails and invalid/overflow boundaries. **27 native GPT functional
cases pass**, including **three GPT-to-FAT32 integration runs**. Tests decode
both GPT copies independently, check header/table CRCs, type/name/bounds and
protective MBR, and run `sfdisk --json` and `--verify`. They inspect all bytes
outside table metadata or the formatted partition, use `fsck.fat` and mtools on
the actual recorded extent, and recreate GPT without altering the FAT boot
sector. The separate formatter suite now passes **37 cases**.

Failure coverage includes invalid targets/options, pathname replacement,
cancellation before/after writing, target resizing, allocation/write/flush
failures, EINTR and damaged primary or backup GPT metadata. Test-only link
wrappers inject failures; production code has no fault switches. Descriptor
ownership and unchanged images before any attempted write are checked.

The full normal suite passes **47/47 CTest entries (45.04 seconds)**. The full
**ASan/UBSan/leak-check suite passes 47/47 (84.63 seconds)** with no findings.
Both include the optional system-wimlib comparison. The system libfdisk binary
itself was not rebuilt with sanitizers. CMake/Ninja builds use default
parallelism; authored checkpoint code builds without warnings, while existing
upstream wimlib warnings remain. Native tools tested here are util-linux 2.42.3
and dosfstools 4.2; the CMake wimlib provider remains upstream 1.14.5.

Logs are `/tmp/rufus-cp10e-build-final.log`, `/tmp/rufus-cp10e-tests.log`,
`/tmp/rufus-cp10e-sanitizer-build.log` and
`/tmp/rufus-cp10e-sanitizer-tests.log`; these temporary paths are not durable
artifacts. Windows project XML and source/object registrations were checked,
but Windows build/runtime validation remains deferred. No new VM boot or
physical USB qualification was performed. Changes remain local and uncommitted.

**Next bounded checkpoint:** qualify the existing tree extractor on a mounted

cleanup against actual filesystem behavior. Real-device orchestration, other

## Port-wide coding review (2026-09-15)

Reviewed the newly authored Linux adapters, Qt code, headers, test drivers,
functional fixtures and build support against the recorded coding preferences.
The scope includes the small upstream-wimlib reader extension. Copied/extracted
Rufus algorithms retain their original style. This pass changes 46 code/test
files; a hash comparison confirms all 528 files under `src/` captured before
this review remain unchanged, including pre-existing local modifications.

The fixes give image identity, target eligibility, sector alignment, extraction
paths, WIM input and progress boundaries meaningful local condition names.
Pointer, offset and division guards remain explicit; system-call failures retain
their original ordering and error codes. Repeated transfer limits, timeouts,
sector geometry and test descriptor offsets now have names. Numeric test fault
modes and UI actions use enums. Compressed test branches were expanded, and two
coherent groups were moved out of the long WIM extraction test entry point.
Device records explicitly default their native discovery fields to empty values,

## CP10h: file replacement and directory reuse (2026-09-15)

Reviewed both extraction branches in `src/iso.c` and `CreatePreallocatedFile`
in `src/stdio.c`. Windows uses `CREATE_ALWAYS`, mapped to `FILE_OVERWRITE_IF`,
and continues into existing directories after `_mkdirU`. For ordinary entries,
the last source file at an output path supplies its contents; colliding source
directories contribute children to the same output directory. This applies to
collisions produced by substitutions as well as native filesystem aliases.

Linux now follows that behavior through two small local output helpers. New
files retain the existing exclusive-creation path. On a collision, the helper
opens without following symlinks or truncating, checks for a singly linked
regular file, checks cancellation, then truncates the retained descriptor.
Nonblocking open avoids waiting on an unexpected FIFO. Directory reuse verifies
an actual directory without following links, including empty directories.
The private output root must still be empty when extraction starts. No custom
case-folding index, entry manifest or Windows compatibility framework was added.
The shared reader/traversal and Windows source are unchanged in this checkpoint.

Shorter and empty replacements remove the old tail. Once a file is created or
truncated, copy/flush failure removes the incomplete output; there is no rollback
of replaced data. Type rejection and cancellation before truncation leave the
existing entry untouched. Other completed entries remain after a failure. File,
directory and byte counts describe processed source entries, including those
whose outputs are later replaced, rather than unique final filesystem contents.

## CP10m: authorized native GPT/FAT32 preparation (2026-09-15)

Added a separate native-device operation to the production preparation helper and
Qt process controller. One `pkexec --disable-internal-agent` launch authorizes the
whole GPT/FAT32 job. The helper stays privileged through formatter cleanup; it does
not call separately authenticated UDisks operations or retry authorization. The GUI
stays an ordinary user. CMake generates an `auth_admin` policy restricted to the
configured helper path and `--device`, and supplies helper/policy installation rules.
Nothing is installed on the development host. Windows sources are unchanged.

The request captures the accepted UDisks service owner, object, identity and device
facts, plus the kernel disk sequence. Before writing, the root helper reads a fresh
snapshot from the real system bus, repeats the existing USB eligibility/use checks,
and validates its exclusive block descriptor against size, device number, sequence,
512-byte sectors and writable state. Raw writing and preparation now share the
existing UDisks use checks instead of maintaining two copies. The ordinary-file
operation remains unprivileged and is rejected in native launch mode.

After GPT creation, the helper refreshes the kernel partition table and checks the
kernel's partition-1 extent and disk sequence. It holds a non-exclusive partition
FD, releases the whole-disk exclusive claim, then calls stock mkfs.fat through the
inherited `/proc/self/fd/3`. The formatter's existing command construction, process
supervision, flush and Rufus FAT-reader verification serve both regular files and
native partitions. Partition I/O starts at zero; FAT hidden sectors still describe
the partition's disk offset. The helper closes the partition FD, reacquires the
whole disk and verifies its identity and both GPT copies, also attempting this
cleanup after formatter cancellation/failure. Busy or replaced targets are not
bypassed or retried. GPT placement and FAT32 preflight still precede any writes.

The kernel sequence provides an additional check against reusing a device number;
see the [kernel stable ABI](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.12/admin-guide/abi-stable.html)
and [block ioctl implementation](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/block/ioctl.c).
The current native path requires that facility and fails if it cannot obtain it.
The ownership handoff is explicit, not continuous exclusivity. These identity checks
are not evidence of physical hot-unplug or automount qualification during the gap.

Cancellation while the authentication dialog is open stops the still-unprivileged
pkexec process before a job request is sent. After elevation, cancellation uses
stdin EOF because the ordinary caller cannot signal a root helper. EOF also covers
actual caller death. The root worker uses the existing TERM/grace-period/KILL/reap
path and reports completion only after cleanup. No process relaunch or second prompt
is used. Cooperative cleanup still depends on blocked kernel I/O eventually returning.

Validation:

- Full normal CTest suite: **49/49 (52.78 s)**. Full ASan/UBSan suite with leak

## CP10n: extraction in the authorized device job (2026-09-15)

Committed CP10l/CP10m as `f63957a9`
(`[linux] add single-authorization GPT and FAT32 preparation helper`).

The same native request can now include an ISO source and Rock Ridge/Joliet options.
The existing helper performs source preflight, GPT creation, stock mkfs.fat,
private mounting, the existing ISO-tree extractor, filesystem flush, unmount and
exclusive disk reacquisition within its one authorization. This does not enable
application ISO START or claim that the resulting ordinary copied tree is bootable.

`CapturePrepareSource` captures device/inode/size/mtime/ctime. The helper checks
those accepted facts before reading source data and retains the source descriptor
through the job. This first path accepts caller-owned, owner-readable regular
images and rejects final-component symlinks; broader source permissions/descriptor
transfer remain separate work. Existing source checks detect changes and pathname
replacement, and shared UDisks checks refuse a source residing on the target.
Library opens use the retained inode; source validation does not claim a snapshot
against a concurrent writer.

`CheckIsoTree` exposes the extractor's existing preflight pass without opening an
output directory or allocating the copy buffer. It rejects unsupported entries,
incomplete trees and files above FAT32's limit before device writes. Planned byte
counts reject an obvious capacity shortfall; filesystem allocation and naming can
still fail during copying. `ExtractIsoTree` repeats its checks and continues using
the shared Rufus traversal, filename substitutions, native collision behavior,
root `ldlinux.sys` exclusion and bounded copying. Windows sources are unchanged.

The helper creates a private mount namespace before Qt starts threads and marks
mount propagation private. It releases the whole-disk claim, validates the retained
partition, and mounts the freshly formatted FAT filesystem at a root-only temporary
path with `nodev,nosuid,noexec`, UTF-8 names and the previously qualified short-name
policy. The mount's actual device and filesystem type must match. See the Linux
[mount namespace documentation](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/mount_namespaces.7.html)
and [mount flags](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mount.2.html).

New phases are mounting, extracting and finalizing. EOF cancellation reaches the
existing C extractor, including on GUI caller death. Cleanup flushes with `syncfs`
even after cancellation, closes descriptors, unmounts, removes only the empty
mountpoint and revalidates the reacquired disk/GPT. The result carries separate
flush and cleanup errors plus copied bytes. A cancellation with failed cleanup is
reported as failed. No recursive deletion, lazy detach or extra authorization hides
an unmount failure. A failed unmount can leave an empty `/run/rufus-*` directory
when the helper namespace exits and releases the mount; the operation remains failed.

Validation:

- Full normal CTest: **50/50 (53.59 s)**. Full ASan/UBSan CTest with leak checking:
  **50/50 (93.90 s)**. Both run as the ordinary user with disposable files/private
  D-Bus services outside the tracing/socket sandbox.
- Focused preflight/source/process/extraction suites pass. Read-only preflight
  reports planned bytes without output writes or descriptor leaks and refuses a
  too-large file for the supplied limit. Source tests cover accepted identity,
  later modification, changed metadata/inode/size, wrong owner, unreadable files
  and symlinks. Controller tests reject file-mode extraction and distinguish
  cancellation from failed cleanup. The final added controller cases also pass
  in a focused normal rerun and in the full sanitizer run.
- Both CMake/Ninja builds use default parallelism and have no authored-code
  warnings. Existing upstream libcdio/wimlib warnings remain.

- Normal and ASan/UBSan extraction guests both pass **11/11 Qt entries**: nine
  jobs plus setup/cleanup (156.47 s and 181.51 s respectively). Each independent
  D-Bus log records exactly **nine authorization requests**, one per job, with
  approval caching disabled. Neither guest reports sanitizer diagnostics.
- Guest cases cover changed source metadata, unsupported source entries,
  root-owned source refusal, cancellation during a FAT write, actual GUI caller
  death, mount failure, filesystem flush failure, unmount failure and recovery
  through a successful production job. The root observer verifies unchanged
  media for the initial refusals and private mount flags during both paused copies.
- Independent host checks validate both GPT copies, FAT32 geometry/metadata and
  backup boot sector, preserved surrounding bytes and `fsck.fat -n`. mcopy reads
  back every output file and empty directory; names and bytes match the generated
  source, including UTF-8/long names, substitutions and root-loader exclusion.
- Python/shell syntax, changed-file whitespace, no-lambda and local-documentation
  link checks pass.

The first guest run exposed a fixture assertion that assumed a fixed mount-option
string. Its root observer stopped before acknowledging the paused extraction,
which also stopped the authorization counter and caused dependent failures. The
observer now retains the mount record and checks each required flag independently.
That record confirmed the expected flags plus `relatime`. A follow-up also removed
an accidental `awk` dependency absent from the minimal guest: the parser uses Bash
`read`, checked against the retained record. Supervisor errors trigger guest shutdown. Production mount/cleanup behavior
was not changed to satisfy that assertion.

Reproduction uses `RUFUS_BUILD_VM_TEST=ON`, matching installed kernel packages,
mkisofs and mtools, with a new output directory:

```sh
cmake --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/rufus-test-deps/usr/lib ctest --test-dir /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --output-on-failure
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/rufus-test-deps/usr/lib python linux/tests/vm/helper.py --extract \
  --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --mkisofs /tmp/rufus-test-deps/usr/bin/mkisofs \
  --kernel 6.18.50-3-cachyos-lts --accel tcg /tmp/rufus-extract-guest
```

Temporary logs use `/tmp/rufus-cp10n-tests.log`,
`/tmp/rufus-cp10n-sanitizer-tests.log`, `/tmp/rufus-cp10n-focused.log` and
`/tmp/rufus-cp10n-process-final.log`. Guest artifacts are under
`/tmp/rufus-cp10n-extract-final` and `/tmp/rufus-cp10n-extract-sanitizers-final`,
with matching `.log` files, source fixtures, final copied files, disk images,
GPT/FAT inspection logs, manifests and real authorization evidence. No host disk,
mount or policy installation is involved. The earlier fixture failure is retained
under `/tmp/rufus-cp10n-extract-guest`. CP10n changes remain local and uncommitted.

**Next checkpoint:** qualify a narrow ordinary UEFI ISO through this full job and

## CP10o: UEFI boot after authorized ISO extraction (2026-09-15)

The production helper from CP10n now has a reproducible UEFI boot qualification.
This checkpoint adds VM fixtures and documentation; it makes no production backend
or GUI change. CP10n and CP10o remain uncommitted after `f63957a9`.

`helper.py --uefi` creates a generated ISO tree containing the installed systemd
UEFI loader at `EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`, the native Linux kernel, a small initramfs,
a path-based loader entry and payload checksums. The shared Rufus tree scanner
recognizes the fallback loader and complete tree, with no Windows, GRUB, symlink
or NTFS requirement. This source is a file-tree fixture without an optical boot
catalog or a distribution installer; it does not claim Arch/CachyOS compatibility.

The ordinary Qt caller uses the production `PrepareImageProcess` and helper for
source preflight, GPT partitioning, stock mkfs.fat, private mounting, extraction,
flush/unmount and disk reacquisition. It makes one real uncached authorization
request. The host independently verifies GPT/FAT metadata, surrounding bytes,
`fsck.fat -n`, every copied file hash and the directory tree.

A separate OVMF VM receives only the resulting emulated USB and fresh firmware
variables, with no direct kernel/initrd, source ISO, creation-guest disk or network.
The stock EFI loader loads its kernel/initramfs from the extracted filesystem.
Initial Linux userspace checks UEFI and the expected kernel release, mounts that
FAT32 partition read-only, verifies all payload checksums, unmounts and powers off.
A second boot uses a copy with the required marker removed; it must reach the
explicit missing-payload failure and exit with failure. Neither boot changes its
backing image, which is checked by hash.

Validation:

- Normal and ASan/UBSan CMake/Ninja builds pass with default parallelism and no
  warnings from the rebuilt guest test.
- Normal creation: **3/3 Qt entries**, one operation plus setup/cleanup, **32.916 s**.
  Sanitizer creation: **3/3**, **37.844 s**. Both independent D-Bus logs record
  **exactly one** authorization; no sanitizer diagnostics occur in either guest.
- Both resulting USB images boot through OVMF into Linux and pass payload checks.
  Both missing-marker copies fail as expected: **four boot checks passed**.
- Both independent filesystem checks pass: FAT32, 13 filesystem entries,
  47,831/126,945 clusters, 512 bytes per cluster. The 64 MiB disk retains the
  existing GPT Basic Data partition at offset 1,048,576, size 66,028,032 bytes.
  No ESP type change or bootloader installation was needed for this OVMF fixture.
- Both source trees also pass the final shared-scan assertions. The instrumented
  host scan runs outside the tracing sandbox so LeakSanitizer can operate.
- Python/shell syntax, changed-file whitespace and local documentation links pass.
  The CP10n **50/50 normal and 50/50 sanitizer** host-suite results remain the
  previous production validation; those suites were not repeated for fixture-only
  changes.

The first boot launches failed before firmware execution because QEMU's default
snapshot directory, `/var/tmp`, is read-only in the tool sandbox. The fixture now
sets QEMU's temporary directory to its own output directory. The already verified
normal and sanitizer USB outputs were then booted successfully with the corrected
launcher; the creation jobs did not need to be repeated for that host-only issue.

Reproduction and prerequisites are in the
[VM instructions](../linux/tests/vm/README.md#uefi-boot-after-authorized-extraction).
Inputs used here include systemd 261.3, Linux `6.18.50-3-cachyos-lts`, QEMU 11.1.1
with TCG and the normal x86-64 OVMF 4 MiB firmware pair. Source/loader/kernel and
firmware hashes, QEMU invocations, authorization evidence, copied files and serial
logs are retained under `/tmp/rufus-cp10o-uefi` and
`/tmp/rufus-cp10o-uefi-sanitizers`. Logs include
`/tmp/rufus-cp10o-build.log`, `/tmp/rufus-cp10o-sanitizer-build.log`,
`/tmp/rufus-cp10o-uefi.log`, `/tmp/rufus-cp10o-uefi-sanitizers.log`,
`/tmp/rufus-cp10o-boot-retry.log` and `/tmp/rufus-cp10o-boot-final.log`.
The initial launch failures remain in `uefi-boot-sandbox-failure/`; final
`results.json` records the successful boot checks. No host mounts, device writes,
policy installation or password collection are involved.

**Supported scope and next checkpoint:** the preparation/extraction mechanism can
boot this self-contained x86-64 EFI tree on OVMF with the existing GPT/FAT32 layout.
The loader uses filesystem paths, so the fixture does not exercise ISO label/UUID
references or configuration rewriting. EFI detection alone is not sufficient to
enable arbitrary ISOs. Next qualify one hash-recorded real distribution ISO and
its Rufus-compatible label/configuration requirements, then enable only the
qualified workflow in START with the existing Win32-compatible ISO/DD dialog.
BIOS/native installers, unknown installer versions, Windows media, Secure Boot,
other architectures/layouts and physical firmware remain outside this result.

## CP10p: real Alpine ISO through the authorized helper (2026-09-15)

The existing production helper now has a real distribution ISO boot qualification.
The fixture uses official Alpine standard **3.22.5 x86-64**, downloaded from the
[Alpine release directory](https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.22/releases/x86_64/)
and checked against the
[published SHA-256](https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.22/releases/x86_64/alpine-standard-3.22.5-x86_64.iso.sha256):

```text
8844f664dffbf50964ba33fe67658dd5d61c8f02d88e4febd17cf2c4334983c4
```

This checkpoint adds `helper.py --alpine`, its concrete guest test and image/boot
checks. It changes no production backend or Windows source. CP10n, CP10o and CP10p
remain uncommitted after `f63957a9`.

The native job prepares a 512 MiB USB using the existing GPT Basic Data/FAT32
layout, then extracts the original ISO in the same authorized helper. The FAT label
is `RUFUS TEST`, deliberately different from `alpine-std 3.22.5 x86_64`. The ISO
preflight accepts 122 files totaling 283,426,236 bytes. No Syslinux/GRUB installer
is selected or launched. The EFI executable, on-disk GRUB menu, kernel, initramfs,
modloop and packages retain their original bytes.

Independent host checks compare every copied file hash and directory, GPT/FAT
metadata and preserved surrounding bytes. bsdtar supplies the ordinary ISO tree.
Rufus's bundled reader additionally exposes two virtual El Torito files: a 2,048
byte BIOS range and the 1,474,560 byte EFI image. The fixture reads the pinned ISO's
boot catalog independently and verifies those ranges too, preserving this existing
reader behavior. The expected output has 122 files and nine directories.

The boot VM receives only the prepared USB and fresh OVMF firmware variables. It
has no direct kernel/initrd, source ISO, creation-guest disk, injected kernel
arguments or network. Alpine's own initramfs enables the serial login. The test
logs in to the live system, verifies release 3.22.5 and x86-64 UEFI boot, finds the
mounted USB FAT filesystem, checks hashes of the six original boot payload files,
and requires the squashfs modloop to be mounted. The system powers off normally;
the USB backing-image hash remains unchanged under QEMU's snapshot.

**Observed compatibility detail:** the on-disk `grub.cfg` uses paths, but Alpine
also embeds an original-label search in its EFI executable. This is visible in the
binary and in Alpine's
[image construction recipe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alpinelinux/aports/3.22-stable/scripts/mkimg.base.sh).
With the different FAT label, GRUB prints `error: no such device` before loading
the USB menu and successfully booting Linux on OVMF. The test retains that warning.
The successful fallback is observed behavior on this firmware, not a guarantee for
every machine. We do not introduce an Alpine-specific EFI binary patch for it.
The existing Rufus text-label replacement in `src/iso.c`/`src/parser.c` does not
rewrite this embedded configuration. Native Windows comparison remains deferred.

Validation:

- Normal and ASan/UBSan CMake/Ninja builds pass, using default parallelism with
  no warnings from the rebuilt guest test.
- Normal native creation: **3/3 Qt entries**, one job plus setup/cleanup,

- Both resulting USB images pass the full Alpine UEFI live-boot checks and clean

- Both full readbacks match all 122 files and nine directories. `fsck.fat -n`

- Source preflight, published-hash checks, Python syntax, CLI help, changed-file
  whitespace and local documentation links pass.
- No production changes were made for this checkpoint, so the previous CP10n
  **50/50 normal and 50/50 sanitizer** host-suite evidence was not repeated.

Fixture development exposed two reference-preparation assumptions: bsdtar omits
the reader's virtual boot images, and ISO directory permissions can prevent
removing the unpacked reference. The fixture now checks the virtual ranges and
makes only its temporary reference directories writable before discarding them.
The initial normal boot reached Alpine's live login, but the serial matcher did
not accept Alpine's extra carriage returns. Normalizing those line endings fixed
the test; only the normal boot stage was repeated on the already verified USB.
The subsequent sanitizer run passes the complete corrected command from start
to finish. Production media behavior was not changed for these fixture issues.

## CP10q: shared root Syslinux configuration (2026-09-15)

**Scope:** extract the root `syslinux.cfg` rule from Windows `iso.c` into the
existing shared `image_file.c` module and apply it after Linux tree copying.
`GetIsoSyslinuxConfig` returns concrete create/backup decisions and the bounded
CONFIG/APPEND text. Both platforms call it directly; there is no callback,
additional service, build system or installer framework. The original path bytes,
case, root-directory behavior and scanner-selected override are preserved.
The report no longer needs temporary mutation to emit the APPEND directory.
Windows retains its file operations, text-mode newline conversion and error paths.
Native Windows execution remains deferred to real Windows.

Linux keeps the scanned report alongside the retained image view, creates files
relative to its existing private output directory, checks source identity and
cancellation, and flushes the generated file and directory. Failed output is
removed; a successful backup and previously copied files remain. Source file/byte
counts retain their original meaning; `generated_bytes` reports config writes
separately, including partial writes if a subsequent operation fails.
Preflight still reports source totals, not final FAT allocation or generated bytes.
The existing helper runs this step within its single authorized creation job.

**Deliberate difference:** Windows ignores a failed rename to `syslinux.org` and
continues overwriting the original config. Linux uses a non-replacing rename and
stops if the backup cannot be made, including when `syslinux.org` already exists.
That preserves both original and backup instead of silently losing one. The user
confirmed that a small behavior difference is acceptable for a strong, concrete
reason with a coherent result, never merely for implementation convenience. This
preference is recorded in `AGENTS.md` and the port plan.

**Validation:** both complete host suites pass: normal **50/50** (53.83 seconds)
and ASan/UBSan with leak detection **50/50** (96.32 seconds). The existing portable
image-file test now includes golden config strings, keep/create/override states,
root and nested paths, spaces/UTF-8, maximum report-path length and report
immutability (**1,696 assertions** overall). The extraction test passes **121
ISO/UDF cases**, including 30 new config cases: source preservation, creation,
overrides, existing-backup/directory conflicts, source changes, cancellation and
failed backup/open/write/sync/close, with independent bytes and descriptor checks.

The mounted-FAT32 fixture adds three cases to its existing suite: keep an uppercase
root config through case-insensitive lookup, back it up on override, and preserve
both files on a case-insensitive backup collision. Its independent host readback
checks all names/bytes, fsck and surrounding GPT data. The real Alpine fixture now
expects its original 122 source files plus the generated root config, whose text
is independently specified. Neither the source boot files nor the EFI executable
are patched. Both normal and sanitizer mounted-FAT32 runs pass **19/19 cases**.
Normal Alpine creation passes **3/3 Qt entries** (63.670 seconds), with exactly
one uncached authorization, all source bytes unchanged and the additional
99-byte root config verified. Its subsequent OVMF boot passes release, USB boot
payload and modloop checks, then shuts down with the backing disk unchanged.
The sanitizer repeat also passes **3/3 Qt entries** (74.314 seconds), exactly one
authorization, the same independent readback and the subsequent UEFI boot checks.
Neither sanitizer VM reports ASan/LSan/UBSan diagnostics.
The original nonfatal EFI label-search warning remains visible.

Artifacts: `/tmp/rufus-cp10q-fat-config` and
`/tmp/rufus-cp10q-fat-config-sanitizers` contain the FAT case reports and independent
readback. `/tmp/rufus-cp10q-alpine` and `/tmp/rufus-cp10q-alpine-sanitizers` contain
the production-helper authorization/readback and UEFI boot evidence. Host suite
logs are `/tmp/rufus-cp10q-tests.log` and `/tmp/rufus-cp10q-sanitizer-tests.log`;
build logs use `/tmp/rufus-cp10q-build.log` and
`/tmp/rufus-cp10q-sanitizer-build.log`. No new-code build warnings were reported;
existing bundled dependency warnings remain. Older CP10o/CP10p reproducible
`system.raw` creation disks were removed to make temporary space; their verified
USB images and result/boot logs remain.

**Limits and next step:** this does not install Syslinux or qualify BIOS boot.
The unknown-version/native-installer decision is unchanged. Continue by sharing
Rufus's text token/label replacement with platform-specific I/O, then connect the
qualified GPT/FAT32 UEFI job to ISO START. Preserve the existing ISO/DD choices.

## CP10r: shared token matching and Linux config files (2026-09-15)

**Scope:** move the matching loop of Windows `replace_in_token_data` into
`src/config_text.c`, then add an independently testable Linux file adapter.
`SplitConfigToken` keeps the leading-space/tab rule, case-insensitive token,
required following separator, case-sensitive substring matching and four-match
limit. The Windows parser retains its existing encoding, file I/O, newline and
error behavior. Visual Studio and MinGW manifests include the new C module;
the portable component is included in the Windows test workflow. Parser CRLF
line endings are preserved. Real Windows execution remains deferred.

Linux's `ReplaceConfigTokenAt` uses Qt Core converters/UTF-16 validation and the
shared matcher. It reproduces the 1023 UTF-16-unit chunks, including long-line
continuations and split surrogate pairs. It accepts UTF-8 with/without BOM and
UTF-16LE with BOM; no match preserves the original bytes and inode. Changed files
retain encoding/BOM, owner/group and ordinary permission bits. Native reads and
writes use bounded transfers with cancellation. The input descriptor stays open;
identity and metadata are rechecked before a same-directory atomic rename.
Writes, file flush, close and checks must pass first. Failures clean the unique
temporary file and preserve the original; cleanup failure is reported too. After
rename, a directory-flush error reports failure with `modified=true`.

**Deliberate differences and constraints:** Windows's in-place replacement can
leave truncated output on write errors, and its fixed `filename~` temporary name
can overwrite an image file of that name. Linux uses a unique temporary file and
atomic rename to preserve those files. Linux uses UTF-8 for unmarked text rather
than guessing a Windows code page. Malformed Unicode and embedded NUL/EOF control
markers fail explicitly instead of losing bytes. CR removal operates on actual
U+000D, preserving characters such as U+010D whose low UTF-16 byte is also 0x0D.
Whole-file edits have an explicit 8 MiB input/output limit to bound memory in the
future authorized job; unsupported inputs are not silently skipped. These bounds
must inform configuration preflight before application ISO writing is enabled.

**Validation:** the normal full suite passes **52/52** (53.54 seconds).
The portable matcher has **111 assertions**. Native file tests pass **36 Qt
entries**, covering encodings/BOMs, Unicode parameters and deletion, CRLF/bare CR,
four-match/chunk boundaries, unchanged content/inodes, invalid or incomplete text,
size/expansion bounds, link/special-file rejection, cancellation, short/interrupted
I/O, partial/zero writes, file/directory flush, close, rename, input/path changes,
cleanup failure and descriptor counts. Malformed UTF-16 tests initially exposed
permissive decoding of odd bytes and unpaired surrogates; explicit complete-unit
checks and Qt's UTF-16 validation now reject both. The validation API was checked

## CP10s: ISO label and Red Hat config integration (2026-09-15)

**Scope:** share the ordered label/Red Hat substitutions and connect CP10r's adapter
to source preflight, extraction and the existing authorized creation job. The
original `replace_char` algorithm moves from `parser.c` to `config_text.c` unchanged.
`GetIsoConfigPatches` supplies the seven label passes, then the optional seven

heuristic. The existing helper supplies its actual requested/verified FAT label.

`\x20` expansion. No binary bootloader patch is introduced.

Before GPT writes, config preflight reads bounded source contents and runs the
same transformations without destination writes. It rejects malformed/unsupported
text, input/output beyond 8 MiB and final configs exceeding the filesystem's
per-file limit. Extraction repeats this check, copies each file, then patches it
through retained directory descriptors. Source file/byte counts retain their
original meaning; `patched_files` reports changed configs. Root Syslinux config
generation still follows all source files. The GUI remains unprivileged and the
same helper covers partitioning, formatting, mounting, copying, editing and cleanup
with one authorization.

ordering, 1023 UTF-16-unit chunks, four-match limit and per-pass encoding round
trips. Linux commits all passes once per config. Windows may retain earlier edits
when a later pass fails; Linux preserves the original and fails the job, avoiding
partially applied boot configuration. CP10r's explicit encoding/size constraints
and Unicode-preserving CR handling remain. Unsupported configs are rejected before
partitioning; they are not silently copied with a success/boot claim. Identical
labels with no Red Hat pass leave config bytes alone, including unmarked binary
bytes, matching the original no-op behavior.

## CP10t: FreeNAS and EFI Syslinux config fixes (2026-09-15)

**Scope:** share the two remaining non-persistence `fix_config` workarounds and use
them in Linux extraction. `GetFreeNasConfigPatch` supplies the original `set` token
and `cd9660:/dev/iso9660/` → `msdosfs:/dev/msdosfs/` references, retaining literal
label spaces and the original bounded buffers. Windows retains its allocation,
text I/O and logging. Linux includes the FreeNAS pass after the label/Red Hat
passes in both preflight and the atomic text commit. Even identical labels require
the reference change, so malformed GRUB configs are checked in that case too.

`GetEfiSyslinuxConfigName` shares the original directory/name/report predicates:
copy `/EFI/BOOT/isolinux.cfg` only when the scan found no EFI Syslinux config.
Replace only the first three basename characters with `sys`, preserving the
remaining case (`ISOLINUX.CFG` becomes `sysLINUX.CFG`). Windows retains
`CopyFileA(..., TRUE)` at the original call site. Linux copies from the already
patched file through retained directory/file descriptors, using the existing
1 MiB buffer and write loop, then flushes and closes the new config. The shared
GRUB and isolinux classifications are disjoint and tested, preserving their
original ordering. Root Syslinux config generation still comes after the source
files. Copy/generated bytes are accounted separately from original source totals.

**Deliberate error-handling difference:** keep an existing regular destination,
as Windows's non-overwriting copy does. Reject links, special files and directories.
For other copy errors Windows ignores the return value and continues; Linux stops
the job and removes a newly created incomplete duplicate, preserving the source
config. This prevents a missing/partial boot config from being reported as successful
creation. A later source directory conflicting with a generated file still fails
when that directory is visited, retaining completed configs; this checkpoint does
not add a full output-name collision manifest. No extra privileges or prompts are
introduced; all work stays inside the existing authorized helper.

## CP10u: Read-only ISO preparation preflight (2026-09-15)

**Scope:** add the preflight component that the confirmed ISO START job will
use. `CheckIsoWriteImage` accepts the captured source identity and proposed

helper and requests no authorization. `PlanGptImageLayout` exposes the existing
geometry calculation; the descriptor-based planner and writer still repeat it
and validate the actual target. The arithmetic and partition layout are unchanged.

The check retains the caller-owned image, scans through that descriptor, applies
shared Rufus policy, checks the actual original-case x64 fallback EFI file in
the selected ISO/UDF view, and calls the existing extraction/config preflight
with the FAT32 file limit. The header check uses Rufus's `FindPeArch`, Qt endian
readers and at most 1 MiB of prefix storage. It checks PE32+, the EFI application
subsystem and header bounds, without adding a full executable parser. Its
diagnostic result includes the analysis, original mode choices, partition extent,
source totals, fallback path and any failure reason.

preflight rejects unfinished content/tree analysis, Windows/other unsupported

while Secure Boot and unused embedded-EFI analysis remain pending; those report
bits are not cleared. This avoids treating a pending trust check as either
successful validation or proof that the ordinary file tree is unusable.

trust, complete FAT allocation fit, boot configuration dependencies or arbitrary
distribution compatibility. EFI header presence alone must not become the GUI's

## CP10w: shared label normalization and FAT32 cluster choices (2026-09-16)

units on both platforms, preserving replacement of each non-ASCII unit,

dot without changing the application's locale. Localized UI size formatting

Source inspection also identified two related problems in the original Windows
label wrapper: `utf8_to_wchar` allocates only the input's length, but the size
fallback can require more space; the final copy then uses the original UTF-8
length instead of the destination's capacity. The extracted normalizer writes
to a separate fixed-capacity output, and the Windows wrapper passes the actual
destination capacity. This is a defensive correction based on source inspection;
no Windows runtime validation has been performed. The existing Windows build
manifests register the shared source, and the standalone test is included in the

the smallest supported allowed choice is selected. Discovery refresh preserves
the user's choice when the device identity has not changed; selecting a new
device or image restores the applicable default.

Geometry-only validation no longer reads libfat's mutable sector-size setting.
This lets the form calculate choices while the image worker is scanning an
embedded FAT image. Actual formatting still checks that setting before using
libfat. The adapter opens no target and requests no authorization.

## CP11a: shared UEFI:NTFS layout and native file tables (2026-09-16)

**Scope:** first step toward Windows 11 installation media. The source trace is
in [the Windows installer notes](linux-windows-installer.md). It records the
filesystem choices, special large-WIM/FAT32 route, UEFI:NTFS condition and existing
boot payload. This checkpoint implements partition metadata, not NTFS formatting,
boot-payload writes, Windows ISO creation or a new GUI choice.

Two small functions in the existing shared `partition_layout.c` preserve
`CreatePartition`'s trailing-partition arithmetic: round the requested size up to
a track and position it backwards from the available end, rounded down to a
track. Windows calls these in its existing layout builder; Linux calls them
before the existing main-extent calculation. Invalid/overflowing geometry returns
zero before unsigned subtraction or addition can wrap. No Win32 compatibility
layer, framework or new build system was needed.

The native GPT options now accept an optional UEFI:NTFS payload size and return
both extents. Libfdisk writes two Microsoft Basic Data partitions, named
`Main Data Partition` and `UEFI:NTFS`. Only the latter has bit 63 (no drive letter),
matching the original Windows layout; it is deliberately not an ESP or read-only
partition. In-memory validation and fresh-context readback check both entries,
including their attributes. Existing flush, cancellation, retained-descriptor
and damaged-GPT handling remain in use. The source payload is unchanged.

The new layout accepts regular files only. An explicit block-device request for
it returns `ENOTSUP` before writes; the helper supplies zero payload size and
continues its existing one-partition workflow. Native two-partition discovery,
formatting, mounting and extraction will be qualified together within the same
authorized helper, retaining the one-prompt requirement.

112.38 s). The shared placement suite now has **2,746 checks**, including original
MBR/GPT tail placement across track/sector sizes, rounding and overflow/empty
geometry. The native GPT file test has **50 cases**, using the bundled payload's
actual size for its new layout. It independently decodes both headers, tables,
CRCs, type GUIDs, names, unique IDs, extents and attributes, and checks the tables

metadata. Faults cover second-partition allocation, attribute setting/mismatch,
incorrect placement, insufficient space, overflow, cancellation, failed flushes
and damage to either GPT copy. The existing FAT32 extent integration also passes.

4K-sector refusal case**. They explicitly prove that the unqualified UEFI:NTFS
block request makes zero writes, and requalify ordinary GPT writes, descriptor

Physical USB and Windows runtime validation remain deferred.

## CP11b: native NTFS formatting on partition files (2026-09-16)

**Delivered:** `linux/platform/ntfs_format.cpp` quick-formats an existing,
partition-sized regular file through native `mkntfs`. It supplies explicit
512-byte sectors, 4–64 KiB clusters, geometry, UTF-8 label and partition-start
metadata. That last option does not offset writes: the borrowed file represents
only the partition and I/O starts at byte zero. Requests for block descriptors,
wrong capacities, incompatible flags or invalid options fail before launch.
Indexing is disabled as in Rufus's default settings. The formatter chooses the
volume serial; the adapter reads and returns it without rewriting NTFS metadata.

**Reuse:** the original NTFS allowed/default cluster calculation is now in
`src/format_policy.c`, called by Windows and Linux. Fourteen golden rows cover
size thresholds and sector filtering, alongside the existing label/FAT cases
(**265 checks, zero failures**). The adapter uses the bundled Syslinux NTFS
boot-sector structure and zero-field check. Readback checks signatures, geometry,
size, full primary/backup boot-sector equality and initial MFT/MFTMirr headers.
It is not a full filesystem validator or custom MFT parser. Label/version/flags
are independently checked by native tools in the tests, not decoded by our code.

FAT's existing child runner moved into `format_command.c` and is shared by both
formatters: descriptor inheritance, bounded output, 120-second timeout,
TERM/KILL cancellation, reaping and flush after any started child are preserved.
Only the child receives `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, allowing Unicode NTFS labels without
altering the GUI's locale. FAT callers retain their existing result/API shape.
No new authorization, UI controls or formatter framework were added.

**File tests:** `rufus_ntfs_format` passes **44 cases**, including real formats
at every supported cluster size, Unicode/shell-metacharacter/empty/max-length
labels, odd sector boundaries and a 6 GiB volume. Native `ntfsinfo`, `ntfslabel`
and optional `ntfsck -n` independently check output. Failure cases cover refusal
without mutation, retained descriptors after pathname replacement, cancellation,
timeout, nonzero/signal exits, closed/noisy diagnostics, sync errors/EINTR,
false-success, shrinking files and corrupted boot/backup/MFT mirror data.
Descriptors, child cleanup and unchanged caller locale are checked throughout.
The existing **39 FAT32 cases** pass through the shared runner.

**Regression:** both CMake builds pass. Full CTest passes **56/56 normally**
(67.96 s) and **56/56 with ASan/UBSan and leak checking** (121.07 s).
The existing GPT USB fixture also passes normally and with sanitizers: its
11 requests on 512-byte media, 4K-sector refusal, exclusive-ownership conflict,
CLI handoff, mounted-volume refusal and reacquisition all remain valid.
Windows runtime validation is still deferred. Ubuntu CI now installs `ntfs-3g`
for the new tests; it has not run remotely. The local native tools are
ntfsprogs-plus 1.0.0, not an independently tested ntfs-3g installation.

**Large-file functional test:** `linux/tests/vm/ntfs.py` formats a 6 GiB file,
attaches it to an offline QEMU USB guest and mounts it with kernel NTFS3.
The guarded guest creates a Unicode-named file of **5 GiB + 512 bytes**, writes
distinct beginning/end markers, unmounts, remounts read-only and checks length,
markers and zero-filled blocks at 2/4 GiB. Host tools recheck clean metadata
after shutdown. **Normal and sanitizer-built formatter runs both pass** these
guest and host checks. This qualifies large offsets and persistence, not the complete
ISO extraction of an oversized WIM. It directly boots a Linux test kernel;
UEFI:NTFS firmware boot and Windows Setup remain unqualified.

The first sanitizer VM attempt exceeded the original 120-second guest deadline
while the kernel allocated/zeroed the large gap. The fixture now reports its
write/readback stages and permits 300 seconds for emulated USB I/O; the production
formatter retains its 120-second timeout. The failed attempt's image/log remain
available separately from the final run.

Reproduction uses the build commands above, the ordinary/sanitizer CTest builds
and the new recipe documented in `linux/tests/vm/README.md`. All mutations target
disposable files or their emulated guest USB. No host mounts, physical media,
installed policies or privilege prompts are involved.

**Next:** bounded writing/readback of the bundled UEFI:NTFS image, followed by
firmware handoff to a generated EFI payload on NTFS. Then qualify two-partition
discovery, native formatter handoff, mount/extraction/cleanup in the existing
single-authorization helper before enabling Windows ISO creation in Widgets.
WIM splitting, WUE options, Secure Boot and actual Windows 11 installation each
remain separate qualification steps.

## CP11c: bounded UEFI:NTFS payload and firmware boot (2026-09-16)

**Delivered:** `WriteUefiNtfsImage` verifies the existing GPT against Rufus's
two-partition plan, writes the retained bundled image at its reported offset,
flushes, compares every payload byte and checks GPT again. It copies only the
source image, preserving track padding as the Windows implementation does.
The main filesystem, GPT and intervening gaps are untouched. This entry point
accepts regular files only; the caller supplies the trusted bundled source and
retains exclusive ownership. Production resource packaging and block-device
handoff are still pending. No Windows source or firmware binary changed.

**Reuse:** `WriteRawImageToExtent` adds target offset/extent bounds to the existing
raw writer's copy/flush/verify loop. It checks capacity with subtraction before
adding offsets, retains the 2 MiB buffer, handles short I/O/EINTR/cancellation,
and flushes partial writes. Existing whole-image and block-device entry points
continue to use offset zero. `CheckGptImagePartition` exposes the existing
libfdisk readback checks with descriptor validation and seek restoration.
No new copy loop, NTFS parser, bootloader implementation or callback framework
was introduced.

**Tests:** **41 bounded-copy/UEFI:NTFS cases** independently compare complete
before/after file contents, including all bytes outside the payload. Cases cover
unaligned regular-file extents, multiple buffers, short I/O/EINTR, extent overflow,
insufficient capacity, wrong geometry, one-partition GPTs, damaged GPT copies,
size mismatches, read-only/append descriptors, refused block requests, cancellation,
partial writes, flush failures, corruption, changed source and post-write table
or target changes. The existing **39 raw-write**, **50 GPT** and **44 NTFS
formatting** cases also pass. Truncation during flush reaches EOF during payload
readback and correctly returns EIO; it does not report success or roll back.

Both CMake builds pass. Full CTest passes **57/57 normally** (68.19 s) and
**57/57 with ASan/UBSan and leak checking** (117.43 s). No new sanitizer findings
occurred. Existing bundled-source/compiler warnings remain. Windows runtime
validation and remote Ubuntu CI execution are still deferred.

**Firmware functional test:** `linux/tests/vm/uefi_ntfs.py` prepares a 256 MiB
ordinary-file disk using the actual GPT, NTFS formatter and bounded writer.
Native tools independently inspect NTFS; the existing independent parser/sfdisk
checks both GPT copies and partition attributes. The payload must exactly equal
the bundled FAT image, and its remaining partition padding must stay zero.

A guarded Linux guest mounts the main NTFS partition and copies a generated EFI
tree. Bytes outside that partition remain identical. A separate offline VM boots
only the written USB through fresh x64 OVMF, with no direct kernel/initrd, source
ISO or injected boot arguments. The serial log confirms:

`OVMF → UEFI:NTFS 2.8 → bundled NTFS driver 1.9 → EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI → Linux`

The generated loader is the installed systemd-boot EFI executable. Its booted
Linux guest checks actual UEFI boot, the expected kernel, NTFS mounting and all
seven fixture file hashes, including a Unicode filename/content. It unmounts
and powers off normally. A second disk missing the required payload marker must
reach that check and explicitly fail. Snapshot boots must leave both backing
images unchanged. **Normal and sanitizer-built creation paths pass** positive
and missing-payload boot checks. The firmware's serial rendering of the label's
emoji is imperfect; native label readback and Unicode file hashes remain exact.

Secure Boot is disabled for these tests. This validates the firmware/storage
chain, not Windows Setup, ISO extraction into NTFS through the production helper,
other architectures, BIOS boot or physical USB. The preparation guest uses `cp`;
the production helper must use the existing shared ISO reader/extractor once its
NTFS mounting stage is implemented. No host mounts, device writes, installations
or privilege prompts were used for this checkpoint.

**Next:** integrate two-partition discovery and the native NTFS formatter handoff
into the existing authorized helper, with a disposable USB checkpoint before
adding NTFS mount/extraction/cleanup. Keep the single authorization through the
whole job. Then connect shared Windows image decisions, qualify Windows 11 media
and boot/install Setup onto a disposable VM disk.

## CP11d: native NTFS preparation in the authorized helper (2026-09-16)

**Delivered:** the existing preparation helper accepts an explicit NTFS device
request, creates Rufus's two-partition GPT, rereads it in the kernel and checks
both child extents and identities before formatting the main partition. It uses
the native mkntfs adapter with explicit geometry, cluster size and Unicode label.
The formatter generates its own serial. The boot-partition reservation comes
from the bundled image's size at CMake configuration; the helper does not write
that payload yet. NTFS requests containing an ISO source, file targets or a
caller-selected serial are rejected. The GUI remains on its qualified FAT32 path.

**Access decision:** inspection and native tests showed that mkntfs's block open
does not request O_EXCL. The helper therefore retains its exclusive whole-disk
descriptor throughout NTFS formatting, cancellation, flush and readback. It does
not need FAT's claim-release/reacquire window. The existing child runner receives
only the retained main-partition descriptor, with no force option on block
devices. A provider requiring a conflicting claim fails without a weaker retry.
Both child identities, the whole disk and saved GPT metadata are checked. This
continues to use one helper/polkit request for the job; no additional password
handling, authorization cache or process framework was added.

**File/protocol checks:** **46 NTFS cases** now include block-request/type and
missing-device refusals on regular-file fixtures. **51 GPT cases** include 64 KiB
clusters for the two-partition NTFS layout. The process tests check the NTFS
request boundary and Unicode roundtrip. Existing FAT, extraction, raw-write and
Widgets tests remain passing. Full CTest passes **57/57 normally** (67.51 s) and
**57/57 with ASan/UBSan and leak checking** (117.75 s). Both CMake builds pass;
existing bundled-source warnings remain. No Windows source changed in CP11d.

**Native functional tests:** `helper.py --ntfs` reuses the nine real, uncached
authorization scenarios: dialog cancellation, changed sequence/identity,
ordinary-file rejection after elevation, active formatter cancellation, caller
death, native success, mounted-target refusal and no-agent failure. Each job
makes exactly one request. The fault-linked helper checks a second exclusive
disk open is busy immediately before launching the slow formatter; cancellation
and caller death still reap the child and release the job. The production helper
then formats the native partition while retaining its disk claim.

The root observer mounts the completed NTFS partition read-only with NTFS3 and
attempts native formatting through the actual descriptor adapter. mkntfs refuses
the mounted `/proc/self/fd/3` target; the helper also refuses it via UDisks. The
entire disk hash remains unchanged. Host readback independently verifies both
GPT copies/entries/attributes, NTFS geometry, Unicode label, backup boot sector
and clean metadata with ntfsinfo/ntfslabel/ntfsck. Every byte outside the main
partition and GPT preserves its sentinels, including the complete reserved boot
partition. **Normal and sanitizer NTFS USB runs pass all nine scenarios** and
independent disk readback, without sanitizer diagnostics. The existing **FAT32
helper also passes all nine scenarios** and independent disk readback.

The standalone GPT USB fixture also passes its **11 native cases**, FAT formatter
conflict/handoff, mounted-volume refusal, reacquisition and separate 4K-sector
refusal. Its two-partition request now succeeds on the emulated block device.

**Test setup observations:** an exploratory NTFS run completed its guest tests
and disk checks but its final executable-hash assertion noticed a concurrent
rebuild. The final run uses unchanged executable inputs. The first sanitizer
attempt timed out constructing its 3 GiB guest system image, before booting;
the fixture now allows 120 seconds for that setup operation. Production timeouts
are unchanged. Failed-attempt artifacts remain available for inspection.

**Next:** package and write the bundled boot payload through the retained device
descriptor, then qualify NTFS mount/extraction/cleanup in this same authorized
helper. Follow with shared Windows filesystem/image decisions and a real
Windows 11 Setup VM. Preparation alone does not create bootable Windows media.
Secure Boot and real Windows validation remain separate. No host disk writes,
mounts or policy installations were used.

**Delivered:** the preparation helper embeds the unchanged Rufus
`res/uefi/uefi-ntfs.img` using Qt's CMake resource compilation. Before modifying
GPT, Qt materializes that resource into a private temporary native file so the
existing descriptor-based writer can read it. A scoped Qt owner closes/removes
the file on success, failure, cancellation and caller EOF. Requests cannot
supply an alternate payload. The resource size must match the GPT plan.

After native NTFS formatting, the same helper writes, flushes and reads back the
boot payload through its retained whole-disk descriptor. It checks the stored
GPT before and after. The Qt process controller requires the new `bootloader`
phase before accepting successful NTFS preparation. The whole-disk exclusive
claim remains held; the job still needs only one uncached authorization.
NTFS ISO extraction requests remain rejected until the next checkpoint.

**Reuse:** `WriteUefiNtfsImage` now accepts the authorized block descriptor and
delegates to `WriteRawImageToDeviceExtent`. This adds explicit device-extent
validation to the existing raw copy/flush/readback loop. It checks target
identity, capacity, writable state, sector alignment, range and offset limits;
there is no second copy loop or new process/resource framework. Only the bundled
payload bytes are written, preserving the partition's track padding as Windows
does. No Windows source changed in CP11e.

**File-based checks:** eleven synthetic block-extent cases cover exact and padded
extents, disk-end writes, empty/undersized/out-of-range extents, arithmetic limits,
misalignment and 4 KiB sectors. They compare the entire output and unchanged
source, including zero-write refusal. Existing raw-write, GPT, NTFS and bounded
UEFI:NTFS cases remain passing. Full CTest passes **57/57 normally** (94.80 s) and
**57/57 with ASan/UBSan and leak checking** (121.09 s). Both CMake builds pass with
the existing bundled-source warnings.

**Native functional checks:** `helper.py --ntfs` now makes fourteen separate,
uncached authorization requests for fourteen jobs. Five new payload scenarios
cover cancellation after a 4 KiB partial write, caller death at the same point,
flush failure, corrupted readback and success. A guest-only linked probe verifies
that another exclusive whole-disk open fails and hashes every byte outside the
payload before and after each case, including the NTFS filesystem, GPT and boot
padding. The root observer checks that all helper resource temporaries were
removed. The production helper then completes preparation independently of the
fault probe. Existing authorization rejection, identity, formatter cancellation
and mounted-target checks remain in the run.

Normal and ASan/UBSan simulated-USB runs pass all fourteen jobs, with no sanitizer
diagnostics. Independent host readback checks both GPT copies, native NTFS
metadata and every surrounding sentinel. The written 1 MiB payload matches the
bundled image byte for byte, with SHA-256
`72683fa1250eeea772d3399277b434d4e55ba8dd0dc926e52d817e701fc2eb9e`.

**Next:** extend this same authorized helper through NTFS mounting, ISO extraction

## CP11f: shared NTFS extraction, new kernel driver and NTFS-3G fallback (2026-09-16)

**Delivered:** the NTFS device request now accepts the same retained ISO source
as FAT32. Before disk writes, the helper validates the source/tree, planned size
and mount support. It then creates GPT, formats NTFS, writes/verifies the embedded
UEFI:NTFS payload, mounts the main partition, copies using the existing extractor
and runs the common flush/unmount/reacquisition path. The process controller
requires all phases through finalization for successful extraction. It continues
to use one authorized helper for the whole job. No Windows code changed here.

**Provider decision:** the user's preference is recorded in AGENTS.md and the
plan: use ntfsprogs-plus utilities and prefer the new kernel `ntfs` read/write
driver, with NTFS-3G as fallback when that support is unavailable. The installed
formatter remains ntfsprogs-plus 1.0.0. `ntfs3`, used in earlier qualification,
is a separate driver. Because the old limited driver also used the name `ntfs`,
automatic selection requires kernel 7.1 or newer and successful filesystem
context creation. A backport on an earlier kernel version uses the fallback.
No alternative driver is tried after a mount, device or filesystem error.

The fallback executable is NTFS-3G's `lowntfs-3g`, using its `ignore_case` mode
for Windows-style lookup and an explicit UTF-8 locale. A normal QProcess keeps
it in the foreground, without a detached daemon or another authorization. The
same helper waits for mount readiness, checks device/type/writable state, then
unmounts and reaps the process. Failed shutdown is reported. Driver-specific
code covers mount selection and the FUSE lifetime; file copying, config patches
and normal cleanup remain shared. The optional executable path is configured
through CMake's `RUFUS_NTFS_3G` setting.

**Claims and cleanup:** formatting and boot-payload writing retain the whole-disk
claim. Mounting requires handing that claim to the filesystem driver; this reuses
FAT's retained partition identity and saved GPT checks. The mount exists only in
the helper's private namespace, with `nodev,nosuid,noexec`. Every success/error
path uses the common flush/unmount and whole-disk reacquisition. A failed unmount
is not hidden by lazy detachment or recursive removal. NTFS-3G is stopped/reaped
even when unmount fails, so namespace exit cannot leave its daemon behind.

**Native functional evidence:** normal runs on kernel 7.2.5-1-cachyos and
6.18.50-3-cachyos-lts both pass nine extraction jobs. The root observer confirms
`ntfs` for the first and `fuseblk` for the fallback, checks mount isolation and
flags, and verifies no remaining NTFS-3G process or boot-resource temporary.
The jobs cover unchanged-disk source refusals, cancellation during a real file
write, caller death, mount/startup failure, flush failure, unmount failure and
production-helper success. Every job makes exactly one uncached polkit request.

Independent readback mounts the finished volume read-only through `ntfs3`,
exports its file tree and confirms the disk hash is unchanged. The host checks
every filename, byte and empty directory, including mixed case, Unicode and
Rufus's filename substitutions. It also checks native NTFS metadata, Unicode
label, both GPT copies, exact bundled boot bytes and surrounding padding. Guest
packages and binaries are hashed. No host package installation or mount is used.
The ASan/UBSan fallback run also passes all nine jobs and independent readback,
without sanitizer diagnostics. The existing FAT32 extraction guest passes its
nine jobs and independent GPT/FAT/tree checks. These runs instrument the helper
and Qt controller; packaged utilities and guest kernels are their native builds.

**Protocol review:** a regression test reproduced acceptance of an unexpected
`finalizing` phase before any stage in a request that has no mounting phase.
The cleanup transition now also requires that finalization belongs to the
request's phase list. This preserves the intended mount-failure cleanup sequence
for both FAT32 and NTFS. The new case fails before the correction and passes
after it. The reviewed CTest suites pass **57/57 normally** (68.73 s) and
**57/57 with ASan/UBSan and leak checking** (119.28 s). Both CMake builds pass with the existing
bundled-source warnings; Python/shell syntax and whitespace checks pass.

**Next:** qualify ISO extraction of files larger than 4 GiB, then connect shared
Windows filesystem/image decisions and the Widgets workflow before testing real
Windows 11 Setup. Existing large-file NTFS filesystem tests do not alone qualify
the complete large-ISO extraction path. Secure Boot and Windows customization
remain separate. Changes are local and uncommitted.

**Artifacts:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/` contains `cp11f-kernel/`,

a Linux adapter bug, not a change to upstream Windows behavior.

## CP11o — Native Setup WIM update adapter (2026-09-17)

**Scope:** add the Linux WIM update boundary needed by the remaining Windows
customization paths. This checkpoint does not enable another GUI choice or run
another Windows customization/installation test. The single privacy qualification
from CP11n remains the agreed limit.

`OpenWindowsSetupWim` opens the extracted `boot.wim` with native write access,
chooses image 2 with Rufus's image-1 fallback, and clears outputs on failure.
It refuses symlinks, hardlinks and non-regular targets. The private target path
must remain stable under the calling helper. `UpdateWindowsSetupWim` accepts
the upstream command structures directly and uses `wimlib_update_image` followed
by `wimlib_overwrite`, preserving Rufus's recompression and automatic threading.
Linux requests FSYNC to report flush failures before success. Zero commands
leave the file untouched. There is no new WIM parser/writer or dependency patch.

Cancellation is checked before opening, before commit and through library
progress. A rename callback occurs after commit, so it cannot turn a completed
update into an abort result. The caller frees the WIM after the operation,
including on failure. Upstream handles append/rebuild recovery; failed writes
or power loss are not claimed to be transactional. The enclosing helper will
retain its existing authorization and final flush/unmount responsibilities.

**Validation:** CMake/Ninja builds the adapter and component target normally and
with ASan/UBSan. `rufus_windows_wim` passes **15 Qt checks** in each build:
**1/1 CTest suite**, 0.24 s normally and 0.82 s with sanitizers, including leak
detection and halt-on-error. The tests use generated text payloads in small WIMs,
with no Windows system files, real ISO, VM or USB. They verify selected-image
updates, case-insensitive replacement, other-image/boot-index preservation,
single-image fallback, cancellation at four stages, cancellation after rename,
missing inputs, injected fsync failure, malformed/read-only archives, unsafe
target types, invalid arguments and unchanged bytes for no-op/pre-commit refusal.
Successful WIMs are reopened, their files read back and all file data verified
by upstream wimlib. Existing upstream build warnings remain; the new adapter and
test have no new warnings.
