## CP11p — Native offline SYSTEM registry adapter (2026-09-17)

**Scope:** provide the native hive-editing operation required by Rufus's
remaining Windows customization path. This uses Hivex's C API and the existing
shared `bypass_name` array. The helper and GUI are not connected to this adapter
yet; no additional Windows customization/installation qualification is run.

`PrepareWindowsSetupHive` requires the existing Setup key, creates LabConfig
only if absent and sets Rufus's three little-endian DWORD values. It uses
case-insensitive, single-value replacement to preserve other entries and child
keys. The source is retained through a regular-file descriptor and opened into
Hivex's editable memory copy. It is never committed back to the source path.
A separate output is exclusively created, committed through its descriptor,
flushed and closed. Existing output files or links are refused. Errors or
cancellation remove our output; any cleanup failure is logged. The caller must
keep these paths private and only pass a successful result into the WIM update.
Commit has no cancellation callback, so cancellation is checked around that
operation. No root request, hive mount or Windows API emulation is introduced.

**Dependency:** CMake locates the distribution Hivex development package through
pkg-config; Linux CI now installs `libhivex-dev`. The local machine lacked it,
so the Arch `hivex-1.3.24-8` package was extracted into the existing dependency
directory. Its SHA-256 matches the configured repository metadata:
`d9b071912cc9131502d76c4d4cda5234bc2530c8d016b7535b5cafe949703bf5`.
Only local pkg-config path metadata was relocated; library bytes are unchanged.
No system package install, configure-time download or non-CMake build was added.

The 8,192-byte fixture is upstream Hivex 1.3.24's `images/minimal`, pinned to
commit `7996d79cf910758fcb29554e83f44c94560f170d`, with its provenance, original
README and LGPL-2.1 license under `linux/tests/fixtures/hivex`. Tests add synthetic
keys/values to temporary copies; they do not use a real Windows SYSTEM hive.

**Validation:** the CMake/Ninja component builds pass normally and with
ASan/UBSan. `rufus_windows_registry` passes **17 Qt checks** in both builds:
**1/1 CTest suite**, 0.02 s normally and 0.05 s with sanitizers, including leak
detection and halt-on-error. The distribution Hivex binary is not instrumented;
the adapter, tests and independent wimlib registry reader are. That separate
reader validates the written hive and the three values. Tests also cover
case-insensitive replacement without duplicate values, unrelated values and
subkeys, missing Setup/LabConfig, corrupt input, source/destination links,
non-regular sources, existing outputs, partial commit, flush/close failures,
cancellation before/during/after editing, unchanged source bytes and descriptor
cleanup. All temporary hives are removed automatically.

An initial test compile exposed wimlib's private C `swap` macro to Qt headers.
The independent reader now stays in a small test-only C source; the production
adapter uses only Hivex's public API. Final builds have no new adapter/test
warnings; existing upstream dependency warnings remain.

## CP11r — CA 2023 bootloader integration (2026-09-18)

**Status: implemented and verified locally.** The original CA 2023 checkbox is
enabled for eligible Windows 11 images, with Rufus's text, default, compatibility
tooltip and persisted selection. The existing helper uses native wimlib to read
the selected Setup image's immediate `Fonts_EX` files and two `EFI_EX` loaders.
It reuses the shared `efi_archname` order and answer-file writer. The original
Windows sources/build and the single-authorization lifecycle are unchanged.

The font mapping removes uppercase `_EX`, without descending into subdirectories.
Only the first existing fallback EFI loader is replaced; absent fallback loaders
are not created. Root `bootmgr.efi` can be replaced or created. CA-only selection
leaves `boot.wim`, SYSTEM and upgrade wrappers unchanged. When hardware bypass
is also selected, finish CA reads/copies before the WIM update consumes the
handle, then retain the existing registry/answer-file fallback behavior.

**Behavior decision:** fail creation on CA extraction/copy errors instead of
Win32's warning/skip behavior, so partially applied selected bootloader changes
are never reported as ready. Each file uses `QSaveFile` atomic replacement with
direct-write fallback disabled and an explicit checked native `fsync`. Copying
uses bounded buffers and supports short writes/cancellation. Checked parent
descriptors prevent following target-directory links; unsupported source entries,
unsafe mapped names, non-regular destinations and destination hardlinks are
refused. This is not a transaction across the media: earlier replacements can
remain after a later failure. The same helper performs final flush/unmount on
all paths. See the detailed contract in `linux-windows-installer.md`.

- The helper's Python tests verify GPT/FAT layouts using disposable regular files.

## CP11u — Rufus copy percentages and weighted progress (2026-09-18)

**Status: implemented and verified locally; installed preview helper still
needs updating before the next progress-display USB test.** The user's physical
USB run exposed a missing reporting path: the GUI showed only “Copying ISO
files...” while the helper was writing. A read-only disk-counter sample showed
90.5 MiB written in three seconds (about 30.2 MiB/s). That observation proves
activity, not successful completion or bootability. The user later requested
the GUI for a screenshot; it was launched without changing the installed helper.

**Shared behavior:** move Win32's allocation and float arithmetic out of `ui.c`
into `src/progress_policy.c`, with both frontends calling it. Keep the existing
Windows UI inputs, refresh throttling and build systems; register the shared
source in their current manifests. Invalid non-finite percentages are ignored.
The copy status displays the original one-decimal operation percentage. The bar
separately uses Rufus's weighted ranges: for default quick NTFS ISO creation,
copying occupies 16–97%; with Windows customization it occupies 16–56.5%, leaving
the next range for customization. Small FAT32 uses 9–98%; large FAT32 retains
its original format/copy weighting. There is no arbitrary 99% cap.

The native ISO/UDF copy loop counts 2,048-byte blocks, rounding each file's tail,
against the original shared scan denominator, including skipped root
`ldlinux.sys`. It forwards counters through the existing C reporting adapter,
50 ms Qt coalescer and authorized helper; JSON uses decimal strings to preserve
all 64 bits. Forced first/final reports preserve boundaries. The controller
rejects out-of-phase, decreasing or changing-total reports and displays the
weighted position. Copy completion alone cannot produce READY: flush, unmount,
helper cleanup and successful exit must finish first. Progress updates do not
flood the log. Native formatting and customization still advance at phase
boundaries; finer callbacks, ETA and throughput text are separate work. Their
missing callbacks are not replaced with elapsed-time estimates.

parallelism. All **seven focused suites** pass normally (**24.90 s**) and with

setup/cleanup), and **229 extraction cases**. Coverage includes per-file block
rounding, intermediate samples, skipped entries, full-width counters, malformed
reports, visible 50.0% text with the expected weighted bar, cancellation,
removal and copy-complete-but-cleanup-pending behavior. A final readability

## CP11v — Completed READY and unplugging contract (2026-09-18)

**Status: implemented and verified locally.** The user requires completed
READY to mean that all creation writes are synced because the USB may be
unplugged immediately. Idle READY remains an empty bar, as in Windows Rufus.

**Windows source audit:** `src/format.c` performs finalization, calls
`RemountVolume()`, optionally runs the NTFS check and closes both logical and
physical handles before posting `UM_FORMAT_COMPLETED`. In `src/drive.c`,
`RemountVolume()` calls `FlushDrive()` (`FlushFileBuffers`) and refreshes the
volume's mount. It leaves the ordinary main volume accessible; it is not a USB
eject or power-off operation. The completion handler in `src/rufus.c` sets the
bar to its maximum, displays MSG_210 (READY), beeps and flashes the taskbar.
MSG_233 is “Finalizing, please wait...”. The original normal/paused/error bar
colors are defined in `src/ui.h`. Special alternate ESP/ext mounts and raw-image
rescans have their own cleanup paths; no general device eject was found.

**Native contract:** the existing ISO helper calls `syncfs`, closes the directory,
unmounts its private write mount without lazy detach, waits for the NTFS-3G
provider when used, removes its empty mountpoint and releases its descriptors.
Only after worker termination does it send the final result and exit. The GUI
requires both a successful result and clean helper exit. Raw writes already
wait for device `fsync`, verification and worker/descriptor release. Linux
[`syncfs`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/sync.2.html) waits for I/O
completion and reports filesystem writeback errors. No backend sync change was
needed. A sync or cleanup failure remains FAILED, including cancellation with
failed cleanup. Win32 does not propagate every `FlushDrive()` failure; retain
our stricter behavior because silently showing READY would violate this user's
explicit requirement.

The private Linux unmount closes the application's write session before READY;
it does not eject/power off the USB or remove it from discovery. Do not remount
it read/write for a desktop drive-letter analogy: that could introduce new
writes after our completion boundary. The device remains connected and may be
mounted again by the user. Removing it after READY must preserve the completed
result. This contract covers our creation writes; later user/application writes
constitute another session.

**GUI changes:** use Rufus's green/amber/red progress palette, a full green READY
on success and its original finalization text while sync/cleanup is pending.
Request Qt's completion beep and desktop alert once per successful creation,
after I/O ownership is released. Ordinary discovery refreshes and post-success
unplugging must not repeat the alert. Desktop settings determine whether the
requested sound/attention indication is presented. No success dialog or extra
authorization was added.

READY or completion alert before the boundary; then full READY, green palette,
CLOSE enabled, one notification and expected unplugging without FAILED.
Existing cancellation, unmount-error and progress checks continue to pass.
Qt beep/alert calls are intercepted only in the test executable, keeping tests

regular-file I/O; no physical USB, VM or Windows customization qualification

## CP11ac — Archive binding investigation and native WIM splitting (2026-09-21)

**Archive decision:** Win32's archive picker in `GetEditions` reads editions from
its selected archive, while the shared answer generator emits only `/IMAGE/INDEX`.
Microsoft documents an explicit `InstallFrom/Path`, including relative paths,
but the current Linux image-internal path does not establish a drive/working
folder in WinPE. The separate configuration-set mechanism is not sufficient
evidence for changing the existing embedded-answer flow. Keep the single
conventional archive restriction for silent creation. Do not add a misleading
picker, guess drive letters or rename image contents. This remains a parity gap,
deferred until a defined source/launch contract is available; ordinary creation
eligibility is unchanged. Sources and reasoning are recorded in the
[archive investigation](linux-windows-installer.md#archive-binding-investigation-cp11ac).

The next useful planned capability is native FAT32 WIM splitting. This checkpoint
qualifies the public upstream API before adding extraction integration. It adds
`test_wim_split` through Linux CMake, and updates the existing reader's documented
capabilities. It adds no production wrapper, GUI option, Windows source/build
change, new library or additional patch to upstream wimlib. The pinned 1.14.5
source and existing reader extension are sufficient.

**Split coverage:** small generated ISO9660 and UDF containers hold two editions
sharing six distinct 128 KiB resources. Uncompressed, LZX and pipable WIMs split
into native `install.swm`, `install2.swm`, etc. Native library readback verifies
all twelve image/file combinations, UTF-8 edition metadata and WIM integrity.
The complete original WIM/reader/filesystem chain is released before readback;
source ISO hashes remain unchanged. Each case uses a disposable output directory
and removes its files at cleanup.

The normal multi-part target is 256 KiB, so the test needs no large ISO or disk.
A separate call exercises Rufus's original 4094 MiB argument and FSYNC flag on a
small WIM; it does **not** qualify a greater-than-4-GiB input or a FAT32 volume.
The original aggregate progress formula is checked for monotonicity, and every
completed part is synced. Read failure, read cancellation, cancellation after
part one and fsync failure propagate as native errors. The first-part cancellation
leaves a completed part, confirming that callers must clean partial output.

The tests also confirm two upstream limits: the requested part size is not a
strict maximum when a resource is larger, and solid archives return UNSUPPORTED
without producing parts. These are requirements for integration, not reasons to
silently change filesystem or transcode the input. The existing NTFS path stays
available; any future conversion of solid images requires its own plan.

**Validation:** all **six selected suites** pass normally (**9.34 s**) and with
ASan/UBSan/leak detection (**32.52 s**). These include 15 new split checks,
15 existing Setup-WIM checks, 134 reader-contract checks, 146 bounded-extraction
probes, 22 Windows-image probes and 95 reader/metadata probes. The latter retain
coverage for fragmented UDF and independent ordinary-file metadata comparison;
the new split fixtures themselves use generated contiguous ISO/UDF content.
Leak detection ran outside the process sandbox. External system-comparator
libraries are not sanitizer-instrumented. Existing upstream wimlib warnings
remain; the new test compiles without warnings.

The initial test build needed a C++ enum conversion for wimlib's compression-type
argument; that was corrected before execution. The C adapter header is included
with C linkage. All new runtime cases passed on their first run, then the final
full runs also exercised release of the input chain before output readback.
CMake/Ninja builds used default parallelism and selected test/probe targets only.
No host GUI/helper was rebuilt for installation, installed or launched.

**Artifacts and cleanup:** retain `cp11ac-before.tar.gz`, incremental review
patch, source checksums, build settings, source-reference record and build/test
logs under the parent `.rufus-test-artifacts`. Tests cleaned all generated
containers, source trees and split outputs. Only the two active build directories

## CP11ad: checked native WIM splitting in ISO extraction (2026-09-21)

**Scope:** connect the qualified upstream splitter to native extraction without
enabling FAT32 creation prematurely. `ISO_EXTRACT_OPTIONS.split_install_wim`

wimlib still performs splitting with Rufus's 4094 MiB target and FSYNC flag.

destination filesystem, enforces the actual FAT32 per-file limit, and publishes

copy. Source identity and cancellation are checked through split/publication.
Failures remove only this call's staged/published files; cleanup failures are
reported and leave the target incomplete. Existing names are never overwritten.
Every part and the final parent directory are synced before success.

Extractor preflight requires one conventional archive and reserves the numbered
SWM namespace against existing source entries, including later tree entries.
It rejects solid/multipart resources and individually oversized resources before
writes. Other files obey FAT32's limit. This does not predict all metadata/header
or total-space overhead; the actual output checks remain necessary. The internal
option can split small archives for component use; creation policy must select
it only for Rufus's large-WIM FAT32 case. Nested/nonstandard layouts are deferred.
Logical processed source bytes/files are retained, with separate actual split
byte/part counters. Copy progress uses Rufus's compressed-resource arithmetic.
Review caught a possible backwards final progress update on cancellation; the
adapter now returns its last reported block count on failure, covered by a new
extractor regression case.

input, real FAT32, physical USB or Windows boot qualification is added.

## CP11ae: helper split selection and space reservation (2026-09-21)

**Scope:** connect the native split path to fresh helper preflight and account for
its output space. GUI exposure remains deferred until the real FAT32 boundary
checkpoint. Win32 source/build, upstream wimlib, the reader extension and the
single-authorization lifecycle are unchanged.

**Policy:** the original Windows source enables the large-WIM FAT32 exception
through **Alt+E**, `allow_dual_uefi_bios`. This is separate from Ctrl+Alt+E expert
mode and S Mode. The request protocol now carries the boolean preference as
`enhancedInstall`, only for a native request with an image source. Default false
requests omit it and keep their prior shape; an older helper rejects the added
field rather than silently ignoring it. The shared filesystem/partition policy
receives that preference. Fresh preflight additionally requires one conventional
known Windows 10/11 UEFI install.wim for this first split route. The helper derives
and passes `splitInstallWim`; the client does not supply a trusted split decision.
Default large-WIM FAT32 requests remain rejected. NTFS and small WIMs keep ordinary
copying. Nested/multiple archives remain unavailable for this split route.

**Space:** `PlanIsoWimSplit` uses the existing upstream split algorithm, aborting
at the first BEGIN_PART callback before output opening. This supplies the actual
planned part count and resource-byte total without a payload copy or duplicate
algorithm. A deliberately invalid descriptor output path also prevents a host
file from being created if the callback contract changes. The reservation is
source bytes plus one overhead allowance per part. Each allowance is the greater
of original non-resource bytes and the 2 MiB gap between Rufus's 4094 MiB target
and 4 GiB. Invalid resource totals and arithmetic overflow fail.

This is a conservative, enforced budget, not an exact serialized-size or complete
filesystem/customization allocation model. Actual parts must fit the reservation
and the independent FAT32 per-file bound; unexpected expansion fails and removes
this split's files. `required_bytes` includes that reservation while the existing
source byte counters retain progress semantics. Preflight rejects a reservation
larger than the partition before writes. The extractor rechecks `f_bavail` on the
mounted target before creating entries, dividing into blocks to avoid overflow.
Directory/cluster overhead, config growth and customization temporary space still
rely on runtime I/O/ENOSPC handling; this does not claim to model them fully.

**Validation:** all **11 selected suites** pass normally (**43.99 s**) and with
ASan/UBSan/leak detection (**102.41 s**). The initial five focused suites also
passed; the final run adds the existing reader and GUI regressions. New coverage:

- Actual output exceeding its reservation, and missing/invalid/unreadable mounted

- Nine additional creation-preflight cases exercise enhanced/default/NTFS/small

  layouts. This suite now has **106 Qt checks**.
- Protocol roundtrip/type/scope checks keep enhanced installation separate from
  Windows customization fields and reject it without a native image source.
  The process suite now has **34 Qt checks**.

Policy tests inject the large-WIM scan flag on small valid generated archives;

small-input upstream split test remains. The helper's new enhanced-device route

## CP11ag: Qt enhanced-installation preference (2026-09-21)

**Scope:** expose the separately qualified enhanced-installation path in Qt with
the original Alt+E shortcut. No new splitter, helper protocol field, privilege
flow, upstream-library patch or Win32 change is introduced. The existing Qt
selection controller owns the preference because it affects filesystem choices
and the next ISO request. The request passes through the existing preflight,

**Win32 comparison:** `src/rufus.c`'s Alt+E branch toggles
`allow_dual_uefi_bios`, persists `EnableWindowsDualUefiBiosMode`, shows a timed
status and refreshes partition/filesystem choices. It is inside the
`!op_in_progress` guard. `SetFileSystemAndClusterSize(NULL)` retains the last
selected filesystem if it is still available; cluster size returns to default.
The Qt toggle follows that selection/persistence behavior and uses the same
setting name in the existing Rufus/Linux QSettings file. New image selection
still uses the shared image preference. Large-WIM Windows images default to
NTFS; users must enable Alt+E and select FAT32 explicitly. Disabling Alt+E while
such a FAT32 plan is selected returns the form to NTFS. The source label remains
unchanged until the existing plan-time label normalization.

**Intentional difference:** Win32 names the status “Dual UEFI/BIOS mode” and can
select MBR/dual boot. Linux keeps its supported GPT/UEFI target and reports
“Enhanced installation mode enabled (UEFI only)” for the same 3.5 seconds. BIOS/MBR
installation is not implemented, so repeating the Windows text or enabling that
target would misrepresent the result. The separate Ctrl+Alt+E expert setting and
S Mode selection are unchanged. Both key combinations disable auto-repeat.

The controller rejects Alt+E changes while analyzing or during any active ISO/raw
creation flow. This includes preflight, options/confirmation, authorization,
writing and cancellation; the current request and persisted preference remain
stable. At START, only the preference is copied into the ISO request, not a
trusted instruction to split. Fresh client/helper validation retains the existing
Windows-version, source-layout, part-size and free-space restrictions. NTFS and
small WIM paths retain ordinary copying; raw/DD writing remains separate.

ASan/UBSan/leak detection (**75.68 s**). The final Widgets/mock-D-Bus suite now has
**84 Qt checks**, including ten new cases/data rows plus expanded shortcut checks:

- Real Alt+E and Ctrl+Alt+E key events remain independent; enabled/disabled state

- Large-WIM selection offers FAT32 only with enhanced installation, preserves

- Four large/small-WIM × FAT32/NTFS paths pass fresh preflight, choose zero Windows

- Paused analysis/preflight and held active creation test busy-state refusal;
  confirmation, cancellation and the retained request are checked too. An
  unsupported Windows 7 image is refused before helper authorization.

Generated small WIMs use the existing linker-wrapped scan flag to exercise the

## CP11ai: VM supervisor interruption and exit records (2026-09-21)

**Scope:** close CP11ah's concrete supervisor gap without recreating its Windows
fixture. Python's default SIGTERM action bypassed `run_vm`'s cleanup, so an
interrupted runner could leave its separately started TPM alive without a
process-status record. The exact source and timing of CP11ah's interruption
remain unknown; this checkpoint does not claim to identify them.

`windows_setup.py` now installs a scoped SIGTERM handler that unwinds through
cleanup, then restores the caller's handler. Status 143 remains a failure.
It appends `process-status.jsonl` at VM startup/exit and before/after cleanup,
including child PIDs, exit codes, timestamps and the active exception. Normal
VM exit is recorded before cleanup begins. SIGTERM/SIGINT are blocked only while
stopping/reaping the children and then unblocked; pending interrupts are
delivered afterward instead of being discarded. A second interrupt cannot skip
TPM cleanup while a slow VM is stopping. The existing five-second termination
grace and SIGKILL fallback are retained. Cleanup still attempts both children
if status-file writing fails. No signal handling can cover SIGKILL or host loss.

**Checks:** the new CMake-registered `rufus_vm_supervision` test uses Python
children and a temporary Unix socket, requiring no VM tools, root, ISO or disk.
Its seven unittest methods cover **ten scenarios**: normal VM exit, nonzero VM
exit, signaled VM exit, timeout, TPM startup failure, missing VM executable,
SIGTERM, SIGINT, a repeated interrupt while a child ignores termination, and a
first interrupt arriving during otherwise successful cleanup.
Each scenario checks that child exit status is retained and neither process
survives the runner. The repeated-interrupt case exercises forced killing after
the grace period. The last case confirms a pending interrupt is actually delivered
after cleanup, not discarded into a successful return. Interrupts and errors must
not become successful returns.

The final CTest suite passes in **13.82 s**. The initial nine-scenario direct run
also passes in **8.23 s**.
The initial sandbox run could not bind its temporary Unix socket (`EPERM`);
the confirmed restriction was resolved by running with local socket access,
without changing the test assertions. Python syntax checks pass. The Linux GUI
build passes using CMake/Ninja's default parallelism; warnings remain in reused
wimlib code. No C/C++ behavior changed, so its previously passing component and
sanitizer suites were not repeated for this Python/CMake checkpoint.

Two additional **diskless QEMU/TPM** runs pass: QMP quit returns 0, while SIGTERM
to the supervisor returns 143 after cleanup. Both produce complete status records
and reap QEMU/TPM. The interrupted run records a still-running VM before cleanup
and exit code 0 afterward because QEMU handles termination itself; this does not
turn the supervisor's interrupted run into a successful test. These runs use
128 MiB RAM, no guest OS, network, USB, source ISO or installation disk.

**Artifacts/cleanup:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts` retains the incremental
`cp11ai-review.patch`, baseline tarball, source checksums, build/test logs,
diskless smoke recipe and its actual process/QEMU/TPM logs. All temporary process
and TPM state is removed. No large fixture was created, and the source ISO was
not opened. Production, Win32 and upstream-library source are unchanged.
Existing uncommitted work is preserved; this checkpoint is uncommitted.

**Next:** return to native Syslinux installer/payload compatibility and small
FAT-image qualification, as described in the port plan. Do not enable BIOS in
the GUI until its later layout integration and representative boot test pass.
No additional Windows installation or customization matrix is scheduled.

**Scope:** qualify a native installer/payload pair before adding BIOS support to
the helper or GUI. `linux/probes/syslinux` is a standalone CMake build of ten
unmodified upstream Syslinux 6.04-pre1 installer/libfat C files. It uses upstream
`bin2c.pl` to embed the release payloads, without invoking Make/Autotools or
rebuilding the BIOS code. No Windows, Qt or production-helper source changed.

The published release archive checksum was verified over HTTPS. Its `.sys` and
`.bss` payloads exactly match Rufus's bundled v6 resources. CMake checks that
equality and pins both hashes plus `ldlinux.c32` from the same release. A small
incorrect-module fixture confirms that configuration rejects a different payload.
All **2,093** extracted regular files still match the verified archive after the
build. The archive's PGP signature was not authenticated. Source licenses and
notices remain in the retained release tree; see the
[probe's provenance and recipe](../linux/probes/syslinux/README.md).

**Functional checks:** the native x86-64 executable installs into unmounted
regular FAT32 files through host mtools. Three cases cover root installation
with 512-byte clusters, `/boot` installation with 1024-byte clusters, and a FAT
region at a 1 MiB byte offset. Tests verify the preserved BPB, exact companion
module, loader length, existing config/boot-fixture/ordinary-file contents,
bytes outside the volume and temporary MTOOLSRC cleanup. A fourth case rejects
a valid 4096-byte-sector FAT16 image without changing its complete SHA-256.

The installer changes the primary VBR but leaves its backup unchanged, matching
Rufus's installer behavior. Each test verifies that fact, then updates the backup
only in a separate check copy and requires clean `fsck.fat -n`. This isolates the
known backup mismatch; it does not repair the actual booted volume or claim a
clean unmodified fsck result.

Both volume-at-zero cases boot under QEMU/SeaBIOS with TCG and 64 MiB RAM. They
load the installed Syslinux 6.04-pre1 code and companion module, read the config,
and execute `BOOT fixture.bs`. The existing raw-boot fixture prints its serial
marker and exits QEMU with the expected debug-exit status. Tests require the
Syslinux banner followed by that marker, plus an unchanged complete backing-image
hash afterward. These are volume boots; the offset case is not booted and no MBR
or representative distribution boot is claimed.

All four cases pass in one CTest entry: **2.39 s** initially, **2.29 s** after the
final CMake rebuild. The first test attempt reached the boot fixture but failed
an extra console-marker assertion; that early `SAY` message was not emitted to
serial. The test now requires the actual loader banner, configured fixture
handoff and exit status. It does not require that unsupported observation.
Packed-member compiler warnings remain in upstream code. No sanitizer run is
claimed for this native-installer probe.

The four existing shared Syslinux suites pass in **0.32 s**. Two additional
generated ISOs use the release's real `isolinux.bin` or a synthetic loader with
no banner, both with its real companion module. Shared scanning detects
`6.04/pre1` in the first; the second keeps `DETECTED=0`, an empty detected suffix,
numeric `SELECTED=1540` (6.04), an empty selected suffix and `INFERRED=1`.
Unknown detection is not replaced by the host installer's banner.

**Integration decision:** native installation is viable for this exact pair.
Its fixed embedded payloads, suffix-free `--version`, movement of both files
with `--directory`, 512-byte-sector/32-bit-offset constraints and internal
mtools child commands prevent treating it as an arbitrary host-tool replacement.
Next, bind the pair to shared selection and test Rufus's root-loader/config
redirect behavior. Preserve image modules and unsupported-version diagnostics;
unknown-image compatibility is not established just by the numeric fallback.
Descriptor ownership, process supervision, postchecks and final sync stay within
the existing one-authorization helper when integration is added. MBR and a
representative distribution boot remain later checkpoints before enabling BIOS.

**Artifacts/cleanup:** the parent `.rufus-test-artifacts` retains `cp12a-*`
build/test/tool logs, selection output, payload-guard result, provenance, baseline,
incremental patch and source checksums. The 5 MiB source archive and 28 MiB
extracted dependency remain for the next checkpoint. All disposable volumes,
check copies, ISO trees and QEMU overlays were removed. Peak test volume size
was 128 MiB plus its check copy; final free space remains about **119 GiB**.
No physical device, mount, root authorization, Windows ISO or customization
test was used. This checkpoint and earlier work remain uncommitted.


## CP12b: native Syslinux pair selection and extracted-ISO boots (2026-09-21)

**Scope:** connect CP12a's exact native pair to shared Rufus selection and test
its root installation against real extraction output. The new Linux-only
`CheckNativeSyslinuxPair` component checks the selected 6.04/pre1 build or inferred
numeric v6 fallback, FAT32, 512-byte sectors, representable/aligned byte offsets,
and the exact companion module size/SHA-256. It does not modify image facts,
replace an unknown detected version, launch an installer or write media. It is
built by the Linux CMake project but not called by the GUI/helper yet.

The standalone selection probe calls the existing shared config, version and
fallback functions, then the new pair checker and shared root-config policy.
Its **23 cases** cover the matching detected and inferred selections; wrong
numeric versions, missing/different suffixes; absent, truncated and different
same-size modules; FAT16/NTFS and unsupported sectors; unaligned/unrepresentable
offsets and accepted representation boundaries; absent configs; preservation of
an existing root config; and openSUSE's override/backup choice. The pair check
must preserve every byte of the input report. The maximum-offset checks do not
claim an actual large-offset installation.

**Functional qualification:** four tiny generated ISOs pass the real shared
scanner and `ExtractIsoTree`, then native installation on a 64 MiB FAT32 file.
They cover a nested `/isolinux/isolinux.cfg`, that layout with an unknown loader
banner and matching companion, an existing `/syslinux.cfg`, and the openSUSE
`/boot/x86_64/loader/isolinux.cfg` override. Extraction skips source root
`ldlinux.sys`, creates the shared `CONFIG`/`APPEND` redirect when needed, preserves
an existing chosen root config, and saves `syslinux.org` for an override.

Every extracted file is independently read back from FAT, including all original
modules, configs, backup and ordinary data. The matched root companion is also
checked. All four boot in QEMU/SeaBIOS through real `menu.c32`, `libcom32.c32` and
`libutil.c32` to the relative `BOOT fixture.bs` entry. This checks working-directory
and module lookup behavior as well as reaching the fixture. The expected serial
banner, fixture marker and debug-exit status are required; complete backing-file
hashes remain unchanged after snapshot boot. The VBR/BPB/normalized-copy fsck
checks reuse CP12a's recipe. A conflicting root companion is rejected separately
before making media or invoking the native installer.

**Native difference:** image-mode Win32 Rufus patches the loader's base directory
and leaves image modules in their extracted locations. The unmodified native
root installer also creates a matching root `ldlinux.c32`. This supplies the
verified bootstrap companion before the shared redirect changes directories,
while retaining upstream installer/loader code and the image's module set. An
existing root module must match too; do not blindly overwrite it with a host
version. This extra bootstrap file is explicit and covered by readback/boot tests.
The four layouts do not establish arbitrary config search paths, competing
`extlinux.conf`, other module sets or a representative distribution boot.

**Validation:** the final three standalone CTest entries pass in **8.44 s**:
selection **0.20 s**, four extracted-ISO boots **6.00 s**, and the earlier FAT
qualification **2.23 s**. The first four-layout run also passed in **6.18 s**.
The selection component/shared policy probe passes ASan, UBSan with halt-on-error
and leak detection in **0.60 s**. The tracing sandbox initially prevented
LeakSanitizer from inspecting processes; running this read-only test outside it
resolved that restriction without disabling assertions or leak checks. The native
upstream installer and QEMU are not claimed as sanitizer-qualified here.

The six relevant main-build suites pass: ISO extraction, shared image-file rules,
and four Syslinux suites. The image-file executable had been removed from the
temporary build and was initially reported missing; it was rebuilt and its test
then passed. Existing upstream wimlib warnings remain visible during dependency
rebuilds. The new component/probe builds without new warnings. No Windows runtime
or customization test was added, and no Win32 or shared Rufus source was edited.

**Artifacts/cleanup:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp12b-*` retains the baseline,
incremental patch, source checksums, build/test/sanitizer logs and initial/final
boot/readback evidence. Test ISOs, extracted trees, FAT/check images and QEMU
overlays are removed between cases and on assertion failures. The source release
and small build directories remain for the next checkpoint. No physical USB,
mount, privileged installer or Windows ISO was used. Free space remains about
**119 GiB**. All work remains uncommitted.

**Next:** controlled native-installer execution on disposable files, including
retained-descriptor handling, mtools child-process supervision, cancellation,
failure cleanup and final sync, with complete source/layout eligibility before
writes. Then integrate MBR placement and qualify a representative distribution
boot before exposing BIOS in Qt. The pair checker alone is not full preflight.

## CP12c: native installer process handling (2026-09-21)

**Scope:** extend the existing command runner with an explicit installer entry
point, exercised by a standalone regular-file worker. The upstream installer,
shared Rufus policy and Win32 code are unchanged. The GUI/helper do not invoke
this route yet. Source-layout preflight is the next bounded checkpoint.

The worker supplies a retained descriptor, private working directory and complete
environment with a selected mtools PATH. Only the standard streams and target
descriptor survive exec. It enables child-subreaper adoption before starting;
the runner rejects missing adoption, ignored SIGCHLD and automatic child reaping.
Cancellation/timeout signal the installer process group, and all adopted children
are reaped before final descriptor sync. The leader's PID remains reserved until
group cleanup starts. An otherwise successful installer with leftover children
fails. Unrelated children retain their exit status. Existing FAT/NTFS callers
keep their single-process behavior and pass their regression suites.

**Validation:** 21 process scenarios cover normal/failing/signalled exit,
retained-file replacement, unrelated children, an orphaned writing grandchild,
TERM-resistant cancellation, closed/noisy output, timeout, clock failure,
pre-cancellation, worker/argument rejection, missing executable and sync
failure/EINTR. Each started call checks that final sync occurs after child
cleanup, with no descriptor leak, altered target flags or moved file position.
Three actual native cases cover root install, a guarded 1-MiB-offset install
after pathname replacement, and cancellation inside a substitute mcopy with a
writing grandchild. Successful installs preserve BPB/guards, read back the exact
companion and pass fsck on a separate normalized-backup-VBR copy. Cancellation
leaves the private upstream MTOOLSRC for the owner to remove after reaping.

All four standalone CTests pass in **11.51 s**: process/native cases **2.75 s**,
selection **0.20 s**, four extracted-ISO boots through the new worker **6.24 s**,
and earlier native FAT cases **2.32 s**. FAT/NTFS formatter suites pass in
**4.86 s**. The new worker also passes the 24 process/native cases with ASan,
UBSan halt-on-error and leak detection, using the normal upstream installer.
LeakSanitizer runs outside the previously confirmed tracing-sandbox restriction.
The new source builds without warnings. Whole-tree `git diff --check` still
reports pre-existing CRLF whitespace in `src/parser.c`; this checkpoint does not
edit that file.

**Limits:** these trusted tools must remain in their process group and the worker
must own their reaping. Cleanup waits for actual exit, including a process stuck
in kernel I/O; the timeout is not permission to sync while a writer survives.
The worker currently accepts only disposable regular files. This is not complete
source/target preflight or a privileged device-installation API. Independent
postchecks remain in the qualification harness pending the concrete adapter.

**Artifacts/cleanup:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp12c-*` contains the baseline,
incremental review patch, source checksums and build/test/sanitizer evidence.
All temporary FAT disks, check copies, extracted ISOs, tool directories and
private installer files were removed. About **119 GiB** remains free. No physical
USB, mount, root operation, Windows ISO or customization test was used.

**Next:** read-only source-layout eligibility, including root `extlinux.conf`
precedence and every companion the root installer could replace. Combine these
checks with independent post-install verification in a file-image adapter before
device/helper and MBR integration, then qualify a representative distribution
boot. BIOS remains disabled in Qt until those requirements are met.

## CP12d: native Syslinux source-layout eligibility (2026-09-21)

**Implemented:** `CheckNativeSyslinuxSource` walks the retained analysis view with
the existing shared ISO/UDF walker and range reader. It checks the selected and
root `ldlinux.c32` companions against CP12a/b's pinned set, compares initial config
lookup using shared root-redirect/EFI-copy decisions, and rejects differing
routes before a target is opened. Critical-path collisions, incompatible file
types, renamed paths, unsupported redirect tokens and an occupied required
config backup also fail. Traversal stores only watched boot paths and ancestors;
module size is checked before reading its bounded content. Analysis/version facts
are never rewritten, including unknown detection with inferred v6 selection.

**Behavior:** Win32 patches the loader's start directory, whereas the native
installer starts at root. Both search `extlinux.conf` before `syslinux.cfg` in
each directory. Extra configs are accepted when the effective initial route is
the same, including the generated EFI copy; differing routes identify both paths
in the diagnostic. The comparison also preserves a root-config edge case in
Win32 source: it passes the full root filename as the start directory, leaving
the fallback directories ahead of root. Windows runtime validation remains
deferred, and no Win32/shared Rufus source was changed.

Trailing-dot names and trailing spaces need special treatment because kernel
VFAT and mtools have different filename rules. The kernel ignores trailing dots
and rejects trailing spaces; critical variants are refused instead of normalized
into a replacement candidate. An exploratory mtools check disproved an initial
assumption that it resolved these names identically to the kernel. Its log is
retained; no mounted-kernel alias qualification is claimed. See the
[probe notes and source reference](../linux/probes/syslinux/README.md#cp12d-initial-source-layout-eligibility).

**Validation:** 46 read-only source/fault/view cases pass: 36 layouts, eight
fault/identity checks and two UDF checks. Cases cover matching/conflicting root
companions, wrong size/hash, missing modules, case collisions, directories at
reserved paths, a real Rock Ridge symlink, generated/preserved/backed-up configs,
lookup differences, cancellation, read errors and source replacement. A UDF-only
rename proves that a missing UDF companion is not silently read from ISO9660.
Input hashes, report bytes and descriptor counts are checked. The final source
CTest passes in **0.83 s**. The same final cases pass ASan, UBSan halt-on-error
and leak detection outside the known tracing-sandbox restriction.

Eight extracted-ISO BIOS volume boots pass after source eligibility and the
supervised native installer. The four added layouts cover a selected-directory
syslinux.cfg, root extlinux.conf, an ignored fallback and EFI config duplication.
They read back all extracted files and the native companion, preserve BPB/guard
expectations, check fsck on the separately normalized VBR copy, and verify that
snapshot boot leaves the backing file unchanged. The last focused source/boot
run passed in **12.76 s**, including **11.98 s** for the eight boots. The earlier
full five-entry standalone run passed in **18.23 s**, including CP12a/b/c tests.

Seven relevant main-build suites pass: ISO extraction, the shared file reader,
image-file rules and four Syslinux suites. The reader executable was initially
missing from the temporary build; rebuilding it resolved the Not Run result and
its test passed. New C++ code exposes existing pedantic zero-length-array warnings
in bundled libcdio headers; the original headers were not changed or suppressed.

**Scope/next:** this is initial loader/config-route eligibility, not a parser for
all config commands or a certification of every referenced module. General
extraction preflight, retained source/target checks, independent post-install
verification and actual distribution qualification remain required. Next combine
these pieces in a concrete regular-file adapter, then address device/helper
ownership and MBR placement. BIOS remains disabled in Qt.

**Artifacts/cleanup:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp12d-*` retains the baseline,
incremental patch, source manifest and build/test/sanitizer evidence. All disposable
ISOs, FAT/check disks, extracted trees and tool directories were removed; roughly
119 GiB remains free. No physical USB, root operation, Windows ISO or Windows
customization test was used.

## CP12e: native Syslinux file-installer adapter (2026-09-21)

**Implemented:** `InstallNativeSyslinuxImage` combines CP12d source eligibility,
retained source/target validation, CP12c process-group execution, sync and explicit
temporary-directory cleanup. It only accepts a privately owned regular-file FAT32
image already populated by checked shared extraction. The root loader must be
absent, and an existing root companion must match the pinned pair. Tools run with
the retained descriptor and a complete controlled environment. Source identity,
target identity/size and formatted geometry are rechecked after execution.

**Reuse:** bundled libfat supplies FAT lookup/traversal. The existing formatter's
read-only volume check is exposed without copying its BPB conditions. Rufus's
Syslinux patcher reconstructs the expected installed loader, empty ADV and VBR
from the actual sector map and compiled, hash-pinned payloads. Full byte comparison
checks the boot code and original BPB; backup VBR and companion checks complete
the readback. File-size/cluster bounds keep reads and allocations bounded; cycles,
short/extra chains and overlapping loader/module allocation are rejected. The
pinned payload has 192 extent slots, enough for its worst-case fragmented map.

**Shared fix:** UBSan exposed unaligned integer dereferences in the original
`src/syslinux/libinstaller/syslxint.h`. The six 16/32/64-bit x86 accessors now use
memcpy, retaining their byte behavior and the patching algorithm. No platform
branches or Windows build changes were added. A 24-case packed-field test checks
every byte alignment, exact little-endian bytes and surrounding guards. Native
GCC 16.2.1 `-O2` assembly confirms single loads/stores, without memcpy calls.
Windows application/runtime testing is still deferred; this is not a claim that
a Windows failure was observed. The external upstream installer remains unchanged.

**Validation:** all six standalone suites passed in **23.54 s**: the new 32-case
adapter suite, prior process/selection/source suites, eight extracted-ISO BIOS
boots and the earlier native FAT cases (including two more volume boots).
Faults cover preflight rejection with unchanged target hashes, false success,
corrupt boot code/BPB/backup/loader/module, malformed FAT chains, changed source
or target size, read/sync errors, cancellation before/during/after the child and
failed directory removal. Every worker checks descriptor leaks/flags/position,
unchanged analysis facts, child reaping, source content and temporary cleanup.
Successful images also undergo independent companion readback, BPB/guard checks
and fsck on the separate normalized-backup copy. Boot tests read back all copied
files and require unchanged backing hashes after snapshot boot.
After final review, the adapter and eight-boot suites pass again in **17.78 s**
(5.36 s and 12.42 s respectively).

All 32 adapter cases and 24 packed-field cases pass ASan, UBSan halt-on-error and
leak detection without suppressions. Leak checks run outside the previously
identified tracing-sandbox restriction. The native installer itself remains the
normal upstream executable. Four focused main-build suites pass in **5.51 s**:
ISO extraction, FAT formatting, image-file rules and the packed-field test.
The first regression attempt saw the packed-field executable before its build
completed; rebuilding and rerunning resolved that Not Run result. Build issues
while connecting the adapter (a renamed private formatter call, the old global
NONE enum collision and the test's missing stddef include) were corrected before
qualification. Existing bundled-header packed/zero-array warnings remain visible.

**Limits/next:** copied-tree integrity and general extraction preflight remain
caller responsibilities; this is not a whole-filesystem checker or config parser.
Use a newly created, exclusively owned image, not an arbitrary existing/mounted
volume. The executable and tools are trusted job inputs, not authenticated by
their version banner. Next integrate/boot an MBR whole-disk image, then address
native-installer packaging and device/helper ownership inside the same authorized
job. BIOS remains disabled in Qt. No further Windows customization qualification
was run or scheduled.

**Artifacts/cleanup:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp12e-*` contains baseline
archives, the incremental patch/manifest, build/test/sanitizer logs and packed
helper assembly. Disposable ISOs, FAT/check disks, extracted trees and fault

The final disk check shows approximately **119 GiB** free on the project disk

## CP12f: Syslinux MBR whole-disk images (2026-09-23)

**Implemented:** the existing partition component now provides file-only planning,
creation and readback for one active FAT32 LBA MBR partition. It reuses Rufus's
partition-placement functions, the existing native descriptor checks and libfdisk
for table creation/verification. MBR boot code comes directly from the same
440-byte ms-sys header used by Windows; it also equals the pinned upstream
6.04-pre1 MBR. No Win32/shared source or boot payload changed in this checkpoint.
The normal 1-MiB start and Rufus track/cluster rounding are preserved. The caller
supplies the disk signature; legacy-BIOS fixes and extra partitions are excluded.

The writer preserves descriptor flags/position, checks exact capacity and access,
flushes after every attempted write, then verifies boot bytes, marker, signature,
reserved/unused entries, active flag, type and extent. Partial writes/EINTR are
handled; cancellation or write/sync/readback failure cannot succeed. Non-DOS
labels are rejected before writes, preventing a partial GPT conversion. DOS
replacement removes old table entries; clearing old filesystem/partition metadata
elsewhere remains part of complete disk preparation, before device integration.

**Validation:** 57 MBR planner/create/check calls pass, including the 2-TiB planner
boundary without creating a huge file, different track/cluster settings, replaced
DOS tables, rejected GPT conversion, invalid access/geometry, retained descriptor
after pathname replacement, cancellation, partial/interrupted writes, sync errors
and corruption of code/signature/active/type/extents/reserved/unused fields.
Independent raw-byte decoding and sfdisk inspection verify actual output; hashes
check preservation outside sector zero and rejection without repairs/writes.
Descriptor counts, offsets, flags and flush counts are checked. The final suite
passes in **21.28 s**, and all 57 calls also pass ASan/UBSan halt-on-error with leak
detection outside the known tracing-sandbox restriction.

Two new whole-disk fixtures (65/129 MiB; 512/1024-byte clusters; nested/root config)
compose MBR creation, the existing native FAT formatter, shared extraction copied
through mtools and CP12e's installer adapter. Both boot in QEMU from MBR through

copied files, loader/companion, BPB, MBR and alignment gaps. As before, fsck runs
on a separate copy with only the known backup-VBR mismatch normalized; the booted
disk remains unchanged, including its hash after snapshot boot. The eight prior
volume boots now use the native formatter too, and still pass. The ten-boot run
passes in **16.79 s**, with **3.74 s** for the two new whole-disk boots.
The final two-boot rerun after review passes in **3.71 s**.
GPT partition and FAT formatter regressions pass; the initial three-suite
partition/MBR/format run took **29.48 s**. No hardware or Windows ISO was used.

**Scope/next:** this qualifies ordinary MBR/LBA boot on generated fixtures, not

ownership to the existing one-authorization helper job. A representative

## CP12h: Syslinux MBR device preparation (2026-09-23)

**Implemented:** MBR creation/readback now accepts a caller-owned exclusive block
descriptor, checking expected device number, capacity, native sectors, access
flags and read-only state through the existing target validator. File mode still
requires a regular file. `PrepareSyslinuxMbrTarget` explicitly clears the disk
before the table-only writer: the first 8 MiB, last 1 MiB and up to 8 MiB at the
new partition start, matching `ClearMBRGPT`/`ClearPartition` on Win32. Overlapping
prefixes are combined; small test media are clamped without out-of-bounds writes.
The shared partition header now owns the unchanged `MAX_SECTORS_TO_CLEAR` value;
`rufus.h` includes it. No Windows algorithm or build configuration changed.

Clearing uses bounded 64-KiB transfers with partial-I/O/EINTR handling and
cancellation between chunks. Every attempted clearing stage is synced, even on
failure/cancellation. Readback must confirm zeroes before creating the MBR; its
existing flush and independent table/boot-code verification remain. `started`
stays true if clearing happened but MBR creation failed before its first write.
Descriptor flags/position stay owned by the caller. This removes normal GPT
copies and stale filesystem data at the new start; it is not secure erasure or
a scan/removal of arbitrary old signatures elsewhere in the disk.

**Deliberate Linux difference:** Windows logs a warning and can continue when
clearing the backup GPT or new partition prefix fails. Linux stops, retaining
the partial-write state, because an old backup table or stale filesystem header
can make the new layout ambiguous. Both successful clearing and failure paths
are tested. The table-only writer still rejects an existing GPT without writes;
only the explicit preparation operation authorizes clearing larger regions.

**Validation:** 26 new preparation/readback calls pass in **5.49 s**, covering
2/9/65-MiB bounds, two-partition GPT conversion, retained pathname replacement,
invalid access, cancellation before/during/after clearing and before table write,
partial/interrupted/zero/failed writes, tail failure, readback corruption/failure,
resize, sync failures/EINTR and table-creation failures after clearing. Successful
output has independently decoded MBR bytes, zeroed ranges and untouched middle
bytes. The existing 57 MBR calls pass in **21.25 s**, and the GPT suite in **5.66 s**.
All 83 MBR/preparation calls also pass ASan/UBSan halt-on-error with leak detection
outside the tracing sandbox (**30.94 s**), without sanitizer exceptions.
The final bounds review clamps the tail length before subtracting its offset;
the 26 preparation calls pass again normally (**5.60 s**) and with sanitizers
(**6.84 s**), as do both USB guests built from the final code.
The shared partition-layout suite and staged Syslinux package regression pass;
the latter retains its two whole-disk boots and payload checks (**5.22 s**).
An initial new-test failure was its reused single-stage sync-count assertion;
the preparation suite now explicitly checks both clearing and table sync counts.

The final initramfs qualification uses kernel **6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts** with TCG

## CP12i: MBR formatting and mount handoffs (2026-09-23)

**Implemented:** `PrepareDeviceTarget` accepts an explicit `Table::SyslinuxMbr`
selection, retaining GPT as the default for existing callers. The MBR path saves
and compares its 512-byte sector zero; it does not reserve/check the disk tail
as if it contained backup GPT metadata. The existing native formatter, kernel
partition checks, private mount, sync/unmount and exclusive-claim reacquisition
are shared. MBR/NTFS is refused until a separate supported layout needs it.
Table selection is an internal caller decision following verified creation,
never a fallback inferred from a damaged GPT. No Windows code changed.

Snapshots are published only after all required reads succeed, so a failed
snapshot cannot leave partially initialized metadata valid for mounting.
Mounting verifies the saved bytes before releasing the whole-disk claim, in
addition to the existing checks after reacquisition. Device identity, capacity,
sector size and disk sequence checks remain in place. Cancellation and failed
formatting still attempt reacquisition without retrying a busy claim or asking
for authorization again. A sync error remains separate from cleanup success.

**Validation:** the small QEMU guest uses kernel **6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts**, TCG,
512 MiB RAM and one **64-MiB** ordinary file attached as USB storage. It runs the
production device backend, real `mkfs.fat`, kernel FAT mounting, `syncfs`, unmount
and native block ioctls. The existing UDisks fixture supplies properties over a
private real D-Bus; no production authorization bypass or fake block I/O is used.
This does not qualify actual UDisks, polkit, desktop automount or hot-unplug.

All **13 cases** pass: unsupported MBR/NTFS, failed snapshot, changed MBR after
formatting, busy reacquisition, formatter cancellation, changed primary/backup
GPT, successful GPT, MBR change before mounting, mount failure, sync failure,
MBR change while mounted and full-volume MBR success. Each checks descriptor
counts; cleanup verifies removal of the private mountpoint and retained exclusive
ownership. Linker-wrapped faults are confined to the guest executable. Its
root/PID/DMI/fixture guards reject ordinary host launches before opening a disk.

The final case writes **65,026,560 bytes**, filling every free FAT cluster through
the disk's final sector, then succeeds at sync, unmount and claim reacquisition.
Independent host readback decodes the MBR with `sfdisk`, verifies Rufus's exact
boot payload/table bytes, reports a clean filesystem with `fsck.fat -n`, and
reads every file byte back through mtools. The last disk sector must contain
file data. This specifically proves that valid MBR filesystem tail writes are
not mistaken for damage to a backup GPT.

The final normal run passes in **21.78 s** and the ASan/UBSan build in **25.16 s**,
with leak detection, halt-on-error and no sanitizer exceptions. The private
fixture exits normally so its sanitizer shutdown also runs. Existing GPT image,
FAT formatting and one-request helper suites pass in **12.61 s** total. Both
earlier MBR preparation guests also pass all eight requests in **20.34 s**,
including unchanged rejected 4K media. The production helper builds successfully.
The initial guest setup lacked its D-Bus root-user policy/account environment;
it stopped before formatter tests. The minimal guest now supplies those files
and a UTF-8 locale and forwards child diagnostics to the serial log.

**Scope/next:** this completes the table-aware format/mount component. The
native Syslinux installer still needs qualification on a retained block
descriptor, followed by the complete one-authorization helper job and a

## CP12l: Real Alpine BIOS qualification (2026-09-23)

**Finding/fix:** Alpine 3.22.5 detected as Syslinux 6.04/pre1 was initially
rejected because its rebuilt non-root `ldlinux.c32` differs from the upstream
binary. Windows Rufus selects its core loader by version and suffix, without
requiring byte identity for preserved distribution modules. Linux now applies
that selection rule to known versions while preserving the distribution's
non-root companion. Unknown/inferred versions, root companions the native
installer would replace, and installed payload verification still require the
exact qualified pair. Other versions/suffixes remain unsupported. This is a
Linux source-check correction, with no distribution hash allowlist or Windows
source/build change; it does not establish compatibility of every rebuilt module.

The source companion is **115416 bytes**, SHA-256
`eb5da0d2b08bda3d3055a37bcf4fca700edbf916378b97fdb4a7eb3fefaf561e`.
The native root companion remains **122656 bytes**, SHA-256
`d3472c02263acf9cd1da5db51e263c5484bad13ea68618c403d9cb01ca070aee`.

[Alpine standard 3.22.5 x86_64 ISO](https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.22/releases/x86_64/alpine-standard-3.22.5-x86_64.iso),
SHA-256 `8844f664dffbf50964ba33fe67658dd5d61c8f02d88e4febd17cf2c4334983c4`.

The helper copies **283426236 bytes** and completes the existing phase/progress,
result/exit, claim-release and descendant-cleanup checks. The creation guest
uses 2 GiB RAM to hold the source and instrumented helper in its initramfs.

Independent readback checks the MBR/layout, alignment gap, exact file inventory,
and hashes of **122 source files plus the generated root configuration and
native companion**. The native loader is also present and passes the production
adapter's exact verification. BPB/backup-VBR checks and fsck on a normalized copy
pass. A separate SeaBIOS VM boots the whole USB without an attached ISO or

with only a serial-console argument added. Alpine reaches BIOS userspace,
mounts the FAT media and squashfs modloop, verifies six original boot files,
and powers off cleanly. Snapshot boot leaves the verified backing disk unchanged.

Normal and ASan/UBSan plus leak-detection creation/readback/boot runs pass in
**121.43 s** and **127.75 s**, respectively, using TCG. The native upstream

## CP12m: Qt Syslinux creation (2026-09-23)

**Implemented:** Qt now offers MBR/FAT32 for the qualified native Syslinux
version/geometry, alongside GPT/UEFI when regular EFI files are present. Hybrid
images default to MBR as in Win32; explicit partition choices persist within the
session. BIOS-only sources use MBR. The existing Rufus ISO/DD dialog retains ISO
as its recommended default and omits GPT-only ISO-to-ESP in MBR mode. DD remains
usable without native installer tools. Other Syslinux versions remain unavailable
for MBR. Unknown detection is not rewritten: START still requires source-layout
and exact companion eligibility before confirming an inferred native selection.

Filesystem choices use the BIOS policy and actual MBR extent, and only FAT32 is
enabled on this route. Windows options and the saved enhanced-install preference
cannot leak into a Syslinux request. Confirmation identifies MBR/FAT32/BIOS. The
existing controller emits `prepare-syslinux-device-v1` to one helper, retaining
source/device identity and all cancellation/cleanup/completion gates. A shared
fixed-path tool check is used by both the GUI and helper; the GUI checks before
confirmation and again before authorization. A missing installer, mcopy or
mattrib fails without launching the authorization process. No executable path
is supplied by the request, and no system-installer fallback was introduced.

The existing shared Win32 progress allocation already fits FAT32 ISO creation:
copying 50% maps to **35061/65535**, the first finalization step to
**64879/65535**, and successful helper exit to the full green READY state.
The native installer remains in finalization after private unmount; copying 100%
or receiving a successful result alone never completes the GUI operation.

**Real-input finding:** Alpine's default label truncates at eleven characters to
`ALPINE-STD `, which the earlier Linux validator rejected because of the trailing
space. The Linux label adapter now removes FAT padding after the unchanged
shared Rufus normalization, using `ALPINE-STD` for confirmation, formatting and
configuration patches. Win32 refreshes the effective label after formatting
specifically for those patches. FAT labels are space-padded; the
[dosfstools validator](https://github.com/dosfstools/dosfstools/blob/master/src/common.c)
also distinguishes forbidden leading spaces from that padding. Invalid leading
spaces and the existing other validations remain rejected. NTFS normalization
and original Windows code are unchanged. This avoids simply accepting padding
and then inserting a label that cannot be resolved into boot configurations.

**GUI parity follow-up:** the user noticed our long idle status sentence.
Win32 `src/rufus.c` uses `PrintStatus(..., MSG_205, short_image_path)` and the
English resource is `Using image: %s`. The Linux lower bar now uses that short
message for usable selections. Pending-check/preflight explanations remain in
the existing log and tooltip. A usable partial scan shows empty READY instead
of INCOMPLETE; blocked/incomplete scans and real errors retain their diagnostics.
The checked Alpine screenshot confirms the short bar and unchanged form layout.

**Deliberate qualification limit:** the MBR target says **BIOS (or UEFI-CSM)**.
Windows uses **BIOS or UEFI** for dual-capable Linux images. CP12l qualified this
MBR path in BIOS, so the Linux UI does not yet advertise MBR/UEFI boot from copied
EFI files. GPT/UEFI remains selectable. Qualify MBR/UEFI before extending that
label; convenience is not the reason for this restriction.

**Validation:** all **96** QtTest entries in the Widgets creation suite pass,
including twelve new cases for known/unknown sources, partition switching,
BIOS-only images, missing tools and tool removal, incompatible unknown modules,
unsupported versions, explicit DD, progress/cancellation, and real Alpine
selection/preflight. The protocol fixture checks the decoded MBR operation and
reports an independently expected MBR extent. It never opens the target or

ends before authorization. It checks the default label, 283426236 copy bytes,
partition extent, short status bar and empty READY. The original ISO hash is
unchanged.

The twelve new GUI cases also pass with **ASan/UBSan and leak detection** in

Widgets CTest suites pass in **29.27 s**. The three ISO-preflight/protocol/helper
suites passed earlier after the tool-check extraction. Five actual production
helper jobs, independent readback, fsck and generated MBR/Syslinux boot also pass

fixture; sandbox socket restrictions required running the host Qt tests outside
that restriction. Fixture issues with the optional companion path, generated
copy-byte expectations and updated device identity were corrected. The aborted

## CP14: Initial device selection (2026-09-23)

**Win32 comparison:** `GetDevices` in `src/dev.c` orders drives by increasing
capacity, restores the requested drive number when present and otherwise selects
the first entry. `WM_DEVICECHANGE` preserves that choice while idle; active
formatting defers refresh. Qt previously kept the initial target blank and
displayed discovery order.

**Change:** Qt now sorts eligible devices by capacity and selects the smallest
on the first populated list. Empty startup, initially excluded devices and an
initial discovery error do not consume that first selection. Equal capacities
retain discovery order. Later refreshes preserve a healthy selected identity,
including a manually selected larger device when a smaller device arrives.
The existing selection operation computes format defaults if an ISO was loaded
before discovery. No eligibility, authorization, layout or formatter policy changed.

**Deliberate refresh difference:** Linux still clears a target after removal,
replacement, capacity/path/identity changes, ambiguity or discovery failure.
Unlike Win32's fallback, it requires explicit reselection even after recovery:
a recycled path or new UDisks service must not silently replace the target of
an old selection/confirmation. Discovery also must not reset cancellation or
the completed READY result. The change is limited to initial selection and
display order; preflight identity checks, active-job invalidation and sync/cleanup
requirements remain in place.

**Validation:** the initial test run reproduced six failures against the old
selection/order behavior. The final normal build passes the affected window,
UDisks and write-Widgets suites: **29, 35 and 100 cases**, respectively, with two
optional real-ISO selection cases skipped. Image-analysis Widgets and enlarged
window checks passed earlier in the same checkpoint and needed no test changes.
All five CTest entries also pass with ASan/UBSan and leak detection enabled.
The sanitizer configuration additionally skips the unknown-Syslinux-version
success case because its qualified companion is unavailable; that case passes
in the normal build.
New checks cover initially empty/error discovery, filtering before selecting,
capacity ordering, preserving the user's choice, ISO-before-device format
defaults, no device open/helper start/write during selection, explicit reselection
after service recovery, reappearance during write cancellation, and full READY
with one notification after unplug/replug. Existing identity, write-confirmation,
ISO/DD, synchronization and error checks remain active. Test development also
corrected assertions for the window's precreated hidden dialog and the generated
EFI fixture's expected partial scan; no production behavior was changed for those.

**Evidence and scope:** parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp14-*` retains the baseline,
incremental patch, builds, normal/sanitizer logs and checksums. Tests used private
D-Bus sockets and small generated images; no physical USB, system installation,
user ISO, additional Windows customization qualification or new VM was involved.
Temporary fixtures clean themselves up; existing normal/sanitizer builds remain
for continued development. The next checkpoint is filesystem display/default
marker parity, as recorded in the plan.

## CP14a: Filesystem names and default markers (2026-09-23)

**Source comparison:** `SetFileSystemAndClusterSize` in `src/rufus.c` adds
“Large ” to FAT32 when the device exceeds `LARGE_FAT32_SIZE` (32 GiB), or when
the Windows forced-large option is enabled. It assigns `default_fs` to the first
capacity-supported format **before** applying image restrictions. `SetFSFromISO`
can select another format without moving the marker. Cluster labels already
follow `SetClusterSizeLabels` and `SetClusterSizes`, including the unit switch
above 8192 bytes and the independent default-cluster marker.

**Change:** moved the unchanged 32-GiB threshold to the shared format-policy
header; Windows still receives it through `rufus.h`. Qt uses it for the FAT32
display name. The selection record retains a separate native device/layout
default before image filtering, and the GUI appends “(Default)” only to that
format. Manual changes and ISO preference do not move it. A Windows image that
excludes FAT32 on a FAT32-capable target shows plain “NTFS”, even if NTFS is the
only offered item. Changes of target recompute names/markers, and invalidation
clears them. Creation requests still carry the same filesystem identifiers and
cluster values; the image policy and formatting backends are unchanged.

**Capability difference:** Windows can mark FAT16 on small media. Linux only
implements FAT32/NTFS creation, so it uses the first native-supported format
instead of presenting an unimplemented format as its default. This is distinct
from assigning a marker to whichever item survives the image filter. The
forced-large Windows option remains unavailable; Linux's label follows capacity
and does not imply switching away from the native FAT32 formatter.

**Tests:** five new generated-ISO cases reproduced the missing names/markers
before implementation. They cover small media, immediately below/at/above
32 GiB, FAT32's 2-TiB exclusion, manual selection, return to the original target,
target removal and text fitting in the combobox. Advertised capacities are
metadata only: no large disk files are allocated and these cases never press
START. The existing enhanced-Windows-selection case now also checks that an
NTFS requirement does not acquire the hidden FAT32 default marker, and that
enabling FAT32/WIM splitting restores the marked FAT32 entry without changing
the selected NTFS format. This remains a component test, not another Windows
customization qualification.

The normal image-analysis, window, enlarged-window, native-format-options and
shared-format-policy CTest entries pass. The corrected write-Widgets suite also
passes, including all five new cases. Test development corrected the expected
return selection when NTFS had been chosen automatically for a FAT32-ineligible
target; only an actual manual change creates the existing saved preference.
No production selection-policy change was needed. The separate enlarged-scale
run passes all eight test entries, including setup/cleanup, with every longer
filesystem label fitting the combobox's style-reported text area.

The final write-Widgets totals are **105 passed / 2 optional real-ISO skips**
normally and **104 passed / 3 skips** under ASan/UBSan with leak detection. The
sanitizer build additionally lacks the qualified Syslinux companion for its
unknown-version success case; that case passes normally. Sanitized image-analysis
and window suites also pass. No new sanitizer findings occurred.

**Scope and artifacts:** no physical USB, user-provided ISO, host installation
or additional VM/customization qualification was used. Native Windows runtime
testing remains deferred. Generated fixtures remove themselves; no new build
tree or dependency was retained. Parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp14a-*` retains
the baseline, incremental patch, build/test logs, hashes and link checks. The
next checkpoint audits formatting controls before image selection and after
rejected-image/target changes.

## CP14b: Plain FAT32 and idle format defaults (2026-09-23)

**User decision and backlog:** Linux now displays “FAT32” at every supported

Windows formatter switch is not a separate Linux mode. CP14a's “Large FAT32”
label and its size-only bookkeeping are removed; default markers and all
capacity/cluster checks remain. The Windows large-format constant is restored

`SetFileSystemAndClusterSize` fill the filesystem/cluster lists from the selected
device. `EnableControls` then disables them while image mode has no selected
image; they are populated, not editable. The failed/cancelled image scan path
calls `PopulateProperties` again. Qt now displays its supported native defaults
in those disabled fields before image selection and after rejection. Rejection
discards the image report/source and rebuilds device format choices, retaining
a valid manual filesystem preference. If no target remains, both lists clear.
Partition/target and volume-label defaults remain a separate follow-up; existing
filesystem metadata discovery is not claimed by this change.

START and format-control enablement retain their existing usable-image, device
and helper gates. DD-only controls, scan/write locking and READY-after-cleanup
remain unchanged. The change neither enables blank-device formatting nor makes
an unsupported format selectable.

**Tests:** before implementation, the new initial-device case and four rejected
image cases reproduced empty lists. The latter exercise missing and corrupt
images after generated ISO selection, using both the default FAT32 and a manual
NTFS choice. They verify disabled restored fields, the selected cluster size,
empty READY, disabled START and zero helper starts/device opens. Existing
capacity-label cases now expect plain FAT32 on both sides of 32 GiB, retaining
the format/default checks at FAT32's upper capacity limit. No large disk files
are allocated for the synthetic capacities.

All **seven** normal CTest entries pass: native-format options, shared format
policy, image-analysis Widgets, window, enlarged window, write Widgets and UDisks
discovery. Separate enlarged-scale runs of the new initial-device case and the
filesystem-label/rejection cases also pass. The tests use private D-Bus sockets
and generated image files; no physical USB or user ISO is involved.

ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes the image-analysis, window and write-Widgets

## CP14d: Existing labels and capacity proposals (2026-09-24)

**Source comparison and implementation:** `GetDriveLabel` uses the first Windows
drive letter/volume, optionally overriding its label with `autorun.inf`.
`SetProposedLabel` preserves manual edits, otherwise prefers the loaded ISO label,
then the device label, then `SizeToHumanReadable(..., FALSE, TRUE)`. Qt now carries
UDisks filesystem labels separately from physical identity and follows those
selection priorities. An accepted new ISO clears the manual-edit flag; rejected
scans preserve it. Raw DD labels remain empty. Device/partition content updates
refresh automatic labels without replacing the selected identity or changing an
active job's label.

Linux uses the first filesystem by partition offset, or a whole-disk filesystem,
because Windows drive-letter ordering has no equivalent here. An unlabeled first
filesystem does not borrow a later label. Non-filesystem/container partitions,
foreign partition tables and missing offsets do not supply a label. Discovery
uses only existing UDisks metadata, including unmounted volumes; it neither
mounts nor opens devices. The optional `autorun.inf` extended-label path remains
unsupported and is documented in the GUI audit.

The small Qt capacity formatter follows Rufus's decimal-unit proposal and
rounding, including the original float tolerance at the five-percent boundary.
It uses Qt's existing next-power-of-two function. On-disk label normalization
and original Win32 code are unchanged.

**Validation:** all six normal CTest entries pass: image-analysis Widgets,
window, enlarged window, UDisks target access, write Widgets and discovery.
Nine new capacity rows cover bytes, fractional units, the eight-unit switch,
nominal rounding/boundary, binary-versus-decimal capacities and terabytes; they
also pass at 2× scaling. Seven discovery rows cover filesystem selection, and a
live private-bus test covers label updates, changed partition association,
identity preservation and manual edits. A generated Windows-shaped ISO test
checks ISO/manual/device precedence, rejected selection and accepted reload
without starting a helper or opening the target. Normal write Widgets reports
110 passed and two optional real-ISO skips; discovery reports 45 passed.

ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes the same five functional suites (excluding
the separate enlarged-window entry), with no findings. The rebuilt sanitizer
configuration includes the qualified Syslinux companion, so its write suite now
has the same two optional real-ISO skips as the normal build. No extra real-image
or customization qualification was added.

**Environment and scope:** `/tmp` builds had been cleared since CP14c. Both builds
were recreated with the retained upstream wimlib/Syslinux sources and local
mkisofs binary; no host installation or new dependency download was needed.
No physical USB, user ISO or additional Windows customization qualification was
used. Disposable test files clean themselves up. Parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp14d-*` retains the baseline, incremental patch, build
