## CP14e: Existing-filesystem preselection (2026-09-24)

**Win32 comparison:** `PopulateProperties` supplies the detected filesystem to
`SetFileSystemAndClusterSize` unless a saved user selection takes precedence.
Image loading separately applies `SetFSFromISO` and shared filesystem policy.
The existing filesystem is a preference, not the meaning of the “(Default)”
marker and not permission to offer unsupported formats.

**Implementation:** extend CP14d's single volume lookup to return filesystem
type/version alongside the label. NTFS and explicitly identified FAT32 can be
preselected before image loading, subject to native geometry. Other types,
including FAT16/exFAT or an unknown FAT version, fall back to existing supported
defaults. Explicit manual choices retain precedence. A metadata refresh updates
format choices only when idle without an image; it cannot replace physical
identity, modify an active job or reset a loaded image's custom cluster size.
Original Windows code and shared image/format algorithms are unchanged.

**Tests:** seven window rows cover NTFS, FAT32, FAT16, unknown FAT, exFAT,
unknown media and FAT32-ineligible capacity, including rejection, device changes,
disabled controls and independent default markers. These also pass at 2× scale.
The existing multipartition tests verify that type/version and label come from
the same filesystem. A private-bus test covers automatic FAT32-to-NTFS refresh,
cluster defaults, identity preservation and a retained manual choice. Generated
ISO checks verify image policy overrides detected NTFS and that subsequent
metadata refresh preserves a manually selected filesystem and cluster size.

The initial discovery test used the generic fixture's unaligned capacity; it was
corrected to a sector-aligned synthetic target. The added custom-cluster check
initially requested 8 KiB clusters on a 64 MiB FAT32 fixture; native geometry
correctly rejected that request. It now uses supported NTFS geometry. Neither
correction weakened production validation. Initial logs are retained alongside
the corrected runs.

All eight relevant normal CTest suites pass after the fixture corrections:

reports 110 passed and the same two optional real-ISO skips; discovery reports
46 passed. No real-image/customization qualification was added.

**Scope:** no physical USB, user ISO, host install or additional Windows
customization qualification. Capacity boundaries are metadata only, with no
large image allocations. Existing normal/sanitizer builds and retained native

## CP15a: Native FAT16 regular-file formatting (2026-09-24)

**Reuse boundary:** extend the existing native FAT formatter, not its process
runner or the bundled FAT reader. FAT16 and FAT32 share request fields, label and
descriptor validation, retained-fd execution, diagnostics, timeout/cancellation,
flush, post-process identity/size checks and libfat root-directory readback. The
existing FAT32 function names and request layout remain compatible. New FAT16
entry points accept regular files only; no device or GUI route is enabled.
Original Windows and bundled libfat code are unchanged.

FAT16-specific code checks conservative cluster-count bounds, requests its
reserved/root-directory geometry and validates the appropriate total-sector,
volume ID and label fields. Clusters range from 512 bytes to 64 KiB, subject to
geometry. mkfs.fat's alignment can enlarge the reserved/root areas; odd-sector
requests retain the existing no-alignment handling. Readback verifies actual
FAT16 cluster counts rather than trusting the filesystem-name string. Bounds
can reject marginal geometries before starting the formatter; qualification
does not imply every theoretically valid geometry or any bootloader support.

**Functional checks:** 61 FAT16 format/readback cases pass using guarded sparse
files. They include 16/32/64/128/512 MiB and 2 GiB volumes, 64 KiB clusters,
whole-file and offset extents, odd offsets/sizes, empty/full labels and literal
shell punctuation. Independent BPB/FAT-copy checks, fsck.fat and mtools agree
with native readback. Corrupt signatures, sector/cluster sizes, reserved/root/FAT
geometry, FAT12-sized cluster counts, hidden sectors, volume IDs and labels are
rejected by read-only checks without launching a child.

Failure coverage includes invalid geometry/labels/descriptors, retained-fd
behavior after path replacement, missing or failed formatters, false success,
file-size changes, sync failure/EINTR, cancellation before/during execution and
timeout. Every probe checks guards, caller descriptor flags/position, descriptor
leaks, bounded diagnostics and child reaping. Failure/cancellation after a child
starts still flushes the target. Test operations never open physical devices.

The existing 39 FAT32 formatter cases pass unchanged. Eight additional normal
CTest entries pass: native format options, shared format policy, GPT image
planning, Syslinux MBR image/preparation, ISO preflight, preparation helper and
write Widgets. Seven ASan/UBSan suites with leak detection also pass, including
both formatters and simulated creation. No sanitizer findings occurred. The
write-Widgets suite retains its two optional real-ISO skips; no extra Windows
customization qualification was introduced.

**Scope/artifacts:** Linux remains CMake-only. Existing build trees and tools
were reused with Ninja's default parallelism. Disposable sparse files and
extracted verification volumes clean themselves up; no large fixture is
retained. No user ISO, physical USB, host installation or new dependency was
needed. Parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp15a-*` retains the baseline, incremental
patch, build/test logs and hashes. CP15b will connect shared FAT16 policy to

through Syslinux 6.04-pre1 to the generated `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK` fixture marker;
boot leaves the backing hash unchanged. The normal FAT32 five-job helper regression
also passes independent readback and BIOS boot. The creation guest uses emulated
USB storage; the separate BIOS boot uses the existing IDE-attached disk fixture.
This does not claim physical USB or a complete distribution boot qualification.

Guests use installed kernel `6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts` and QEMU TCG; `/dev/kvm` was
unavailable. No network, host block devices or filesystem sharing are attached.
UDisks discovery is a private guest fixture; partition I/O, mkfs.fat, kernel vfat,
extraction, native installation and helper cleanup are real. This does not repeat
interactive polkit qualification. The sanitizer boundary remains CP15h's normal
upstream executable plus instrumented adapters/helper/libfat/Rufus patcher.
ASan/UBSan and leak detection report no findings there; upstream executable
alignment/leak findings remain unresolved and unsuppressed.

**Component regressions:** seven suites pass normally and with ASan/UBSan:
34 format-option cases, 25 native-pair/config selection cases, 34 installer cases
per FAT type, 119 ISO preflight cases, 41 preparation-process cases, and 127 write
Widgets cases with two optional real-ISO skips. The initial sandboxed normal
Widgets run could not start its private D-Bus service; its unrestricted rerun
passes. Python compilation and scoped whitespace checks pass.

**Scope and cleanup:** GUI MBR/Syslinux selection remains FAT32-only for this
checkpoint; FAT16 Qt exposure is CP15j. No user ISO, physical USB, Windows
customization test, host installation or download. All seven guest runs remove
their disks, extracted/copied trees, kernel and initramfs after exporting logs,
input hashes, QEMU commands and results. Both build trees return to
`RUFUS_BUILD_VM_TEST=OFF`. Parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp15i-*` retains only
small evidence, baseline archives, changes and source/binary hashes.


## CP15j: FAT16 MBR/Syslinux selection in Qt (2026-09-24)

**Implementation:** remove the FAT32-only gate from native MBR cluster choices,
passing the selected FAT type to the existing partition planner. Syslinux scheme
eligibility accepts either supported FAT format, so a small FAT16-only target can
still offer MBR. It keeps the existing version/geometry checks and exact-pair
preflight before authorization. The confirmation text uses the selected format
for both BIOS-only and BIOS-or-UEFI targets. Existing requests already carry the
explicit filesystem and CP15i's distinct FAT16 protocol operation.

**Rufus behavior:** the original shared filesystem/cluster policies remain in
use. FAT16 receives the target default marker where it is the first supported
format; compatible images still prefer FAT32 when available. Partition and target
changes retain allowed manual preferences. A successful ISO reload reapplies the
image preference and default cluster, as Win32 does; the initial new capacity test
incorrectly expected the manual choice to remain through that scan and was fixed.
No product behavior was changed to satisfy that incorrect test. ISO stays selected
and recommended in the ISO/DD dialog; DD bypasses native formatting/installation.

**Validation:** normal and ASan/UBSan builds pass format options, preparation
process, image-mode dialog and write Widgets suites. The 34 format-option cases
now check FAT16 choices against independently calculated GPT and MBR extents,
including capacity/cluster boundaries. The write suite passes 141 cases, with two
optional real-ISO skips. New/extended cases cover known and unknown compatible
Syslinux sources with each FAT type, FAT16-only small targets, the last supported
sector below 4 GiB and rejection at 4 GiB, both directions of the GPT/MBR switch,
manual selection, scan reload and target changes, explicit helper requests,
confirmation text, custom clusters and `Formatting FAT16...`, cancellation during
formatting/copying, authorization/sync/cleanup/layout failures, and DD without
native tools. Both FAT formats retain the exact shared progress values: 35061 at
half-copy and 64879 after the first finalization slot, then MAX_PROGRESS/READY
only after helper exit. Successful unplugging preserves READY and emits no extra
completion notification. All writes use the existing single helper launch.
The first sanitizer Widgets run reached the old 60-second suite limit near its
last cases with no assertion failure. The expanded suite now allows 90 seconds;
individual operation timeouts are unchanged. Its final rerun passes, and the
73 MiB of fixtures left by the timed-out process were removed.

The Widgets child checks the real protocol but never opens a target; destructive
FAT16 MBR creation, ownership and boot evidence remain CP15i's generated guests.
No new VM, physical USB, real user ISO or Windows-customization qualification was
run. Both VM build options stay OFF. Test-owned files clean themselves up; parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp15j-*` retains baseline, patch, hashes and small logs.
FAT16 is complete for the currently supported ISO routes; exFAT begins at CP16a,
with standalone/non-bootable creation integrated separately.

## CP16a: native exFAT formatting on regular files (2026-09-24)

**Implementation:** `ExfatFormatOptions` and the file-only adapter reuse
`RunFormatCommand` for retained-descriptor passing, bounded diagnostics, explicit
child locale, cancellation/timeout, reaping and sync. Native exfatprogs does the
formatting with explicit 512-byte sectors, cluster size and Unicode label.
`-C` checks metadata writes, `-K` prevents discard, and `-P none` leaves partition
creation with Rufus. No full-format flag is passed. Unsupported flags cause a
failure without retrying weaker options. No original Windows code changed in
this checkpoint.

The adapter requires an exact-size, O_RDWR buffered regular file, starting at
byte zero. The native tool has no offset/length option, so this is a partition
image, not a bounded region of a whole-disk file. Current limits are 16 MiB to
below 256 TiB, sector-aligned, with power-of-two clusters from 512 bytes to 32 MiB
(the original Rufus exFAT range). These are range checks, not a complete native
layout feasibility prediction; compatible size/cluster combinations and shared
default policy are the next checkpoint. Labels retain case and valid Unicode,
including surrogate pairs and trailing spaces, with the native 11 UTF-16-unit
limit; forbidden characters, controls and invalid UTF-16 are rejected.

**Readback reuse:** libblkid probes the retained inode through a separate read-only
file description so its seeks cannot move the caller's offset. It validates the
primary boot checksum and supplies filesystem type and the raw UTF-16 label.
Small local checks compare requested size, cluster and zero partition offset,
and require matching primary/backup boot regions. This is post-format verification,
not a full filesystem checker. Upstream libblkid 2.35/2.38 readers identify exFAT
without validating the boot checksum; the 2.39 implementation adds that check.
The build still accepts 2.35+ for compatibility with existing Linux builds, but
the exFAT adapter returns ENOTSUP before writes when the runtime library is older
than 2.39. A fault test verifies this boundary. CI build dependencies now name
`libblkid-dev` explicitly. CI execution itself was not run here.

**Validation:** 64 normal and ASan/UBSan cases pass with exfatprogs **1.4.3** and
libblkid **2.42.4**. Native success cases cover all 17 cluster sizes, empty/Unicode/
maximum-length/trailing-space labels, literal shell-looking labels, an odd sector
count and replacement of the original pathname. Independent test readback checks
boot metadata, checksum, root label, absence of an MBR table, filesystem bounds
and preserved free tail data; `fsck.exfat -n` and `dump.exfat` also pass. An unrelated
neighbor file remains untouched. Reject-before-write cases check bad sizes,
clusters, labels, access flags, pipe targets, old libraries and cancellation.
Failure injection covers corrupt primary, backup and both copies, wrong native
label/cluster, false success, target shrinkage, missing tools, nonzero exits,
signals, bounded noisy output, forced cancellation, timeout, readback and sync
errors, and interrupted sync. Caller descriptor/status flags, position, locale,
child reaping and descriptor counts are checked. Failures after a command starts
may leave partial media; they never report success.

The first sandboxed sanitizer run stopped because LeakSanitizer cannot inspect
processes under that sandbox. The unrestricted file-only rerun, including the
final old-library test, passes with leak detection enabled and no findings.
Normal FAT16, FAT32 and NTFS formatter regression suites also pass. Native tools
and the system libblkid remain distribution binaries, not sanitizer builds.
The optional exFAT CTest skips on providers lacking mandatory capabilities; a
skip does not qualify those providers.

**Scope and cleanup:** no device authorization, block formatting, mounts, GUI
exFAT selection, ISO extraction or boot support is added. Device integration must
qualify partition-offset metadata and the existing exclusive-claim handoff first;
non-bootable creation remains a separate product step. No user ISO, physical USB,
VM, Windows customization test, host installation or large download was used.
Both VM build options remain OFF. Temporary sparse volumes clean themselves up;
parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16a-*` retains small logs, baseline, patch and hashes.

## CP16b: shared exFAT cluster policy and native geometry (2026-09-24)

**Shared policy:** extract the original exFAT block from Win32's
`SetFileSystemAndClusterSize` into `GetExfatClusterSizes`, alongside the existing
FAT16/FAT32/NTFS helpers. Win32 calls it directly; no platform conditionals or
Linux geometry enter that policy. Preserve the allowed 512-byte through 32-MiB
range, capacity limit below 256 TiB, defaults of 4 KiB below 256 MiB, 32 KiB below
32 GiB and 128 KiB thereafter, and the original sector/default adjustment.
Seventeen golden rows cover the thresholds, sector filtering, fallback defaults
and invalid inputs. The complete shared suite passes 469 checks. Windows runtime
validation remains deferred to real Windows as requested.

**Native preflight:** `NativeExfatClusterSizes(diskSize, volumeSize)` preserves
the whole-disk default and filters allowed choices using the actual volume size.
The file adapter now uses the shared range policy instead of its own maximum
cluster/volume constants. The small `checkGeometry` calculation follows
exfatprogs 1.4.3's FAT sizing and checks the cluster-count limit and space for the
allocation bitmap, standard upcase table and one root directory cluster. It
allocates nothing and performs no I/O. Invalid ranges are checked before any
subtraction/division; intermediate calculations use 64-bit unsigned values within
the shared capacity limit. Requests with insufficient metadata space return
ENOSPC before launching the formatter; excessive counts return EINVAL.

This calculation is limited to our native invocation: one FAT, standard upcase
table, unpacked bitmap, 512-byte sectors, zero partition offset and 1-MiB
alignment. `-b 1048576` now makes the previously implicit native alignment explicit.
The CLI has no dry-run option, so this small preflight is needed to filter choices
before destructive work. exfatprogs still builds and writes all metadata; libblkid
and CP16a's checks still perform final readback. This is not a new formatter or a
general-purpose exFAT layout API. Partition-offset/device geometry will be
qualified separately before that API accepts block devices.

**Validation:** all 81 file-format/failure cases and 17 native policy rows pass
normally and with ASan/UBSan/leak detection. The new policy cases cover volume
versus whole-disk size, alignment/minimum size, large-volume small-cluster limits,
and overflow-sized inputs without creating huge fixtures. Actual formatting and
independent `fsck.exfat -n`/`dump.exfat` readback cover the 8/16/32-MiB-cluster
metadata-fit boundaries (one sector below, exactly at, and one sector above),
and both sides of Rufus's 256-MiB and 32-GiB default transitions. Rejected cases
leave the original file hash unchanged and never start a child. At exact fit the
last cluster contains the root directory, so free-tail preservation is checked
only in cases where those bytes are actually free. Native readback also checks
FAT/heap alignment. Extreme TiB limits are arithmetic tests, not full-format or
physical-device qualifications.

The full normal Linux CMake build passes. Normal format-options, FAT16, FAT32
and NTFS formatter regression suites pass. The focused shared-policy/exFAT
sanitizer run uses unrestricted process inspection because LeakSanitizer cannot
run under the normal sandbox; there are no findings. Distribution exfatprogs and
libblkid remain uninstrumented, as in CP16a. Existing upstream wimlib header
pedantic warnings remain in the full build.

**Scope and cleanup:** GUI choices, authorized jobs and boot-mode support stay
unchanged. No USB, VM, user ISO or additional Windows-customization test was used.
The 32-GiB logical test files are sparse (only metadata is written), run one at a
time, and are removed immediately. All disposable volumes were removed. Both
VM build flags remain OFF. Small evidence is retained in parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16b-*`; device formatting is the next bounded checkpoint.

Sources: [original native layout calculation](https://github.com/exfatprogs/exfatprogs/blob/1.4.3/mkfs/mkfs.c#L995)
and [native format limits and standard table size](https://github.com/exfatprogs/exfatprogs/blob/1.4.3/include/libexfat.h).

## CP16c: exFAT block formatting and claim handoff (2026-09-24)

**Implementation:** `FormatExfatPartition` accepts a retained partition descriptor
and expected device number. Before and after the native command it checks block
type, identity, exact capacity, 512-byte sectors, writable access, the kernel
read-only flag and sysfs partition/start information. Whole disks are refused.
`partitionOffset` describes expected metadata, never a seek offset; file-only
calls still require zero. Offsets must be whole-MiB aligned and the complete
extent must fit the signed offset range. This keeps CP16b's layout calculation
valid for the GPT starts currently produced by Rufus. Unaligned starts and 4K
logical sectors remain explicitly unsupported, rather than receiving altered
metadata. The native CLI reads the partition start from sysfs and writes both
boot copies; our existing readback checks that exact offset.

**Ownership reuse:** exfatprogs 1.4.3 opens writable targets with O_EXCL. Extract
FAT's existing begin/finish handoff into two private `PrepareDeviceTarget`
operations, shared by FAT16, FAT32 and the new GPT-only exFAT method. Preserve the
retained non-exclusive partition fd, use/identity checks, partition-table snapshot,
whole-disk claim release, supervised native command, partition close and claim
reacquisition with descriptor/table verification. Reacquisition is attempted even
when formatting fails or is cancelled. A competitor retaining the claim causes
failure; no retries, force flags, new process/authorization lifetime or extra
privilege prompts are introduced. NTFS retains its existing claim behavior.
The FAT entry point now explicitly refuses other filesystem types, avoiding a
fallback to FAT32 for a newly accepted exFAT target. Mount support and mounting
explicitly reject exFAT until a corresponding copy path is implemented. The GUI
and helper protocol do not yet expose exFAT jobs. Windows sources are unchanged
in this checkpoint.

**Guest qualification:** the existing private-UDisks/QEMU handoff fixture gains
`--exfat`. It reuses production GPT creation, real kernel partition nodes/sysfs,
real exfatprogs and the production preparation target; no host device is passed
to QEMU. Nineteen cases pass normally and under ASan/UBSan with leak detection:
11 direct partition cases (zero/wrong device, wrong capacity/start, unaligned
start, read-only descriptor, native BLKROSET state, whole-disk refusal, file-only
API refusal, insufficient metadata space and native refusal while the whole-disk
claim is held), seven handoff cases (snapshot failure, changed primary/backup GPT,
busy reacquisition, cancellation, sync failure and success), and unchanged refusal
on an actual emulated 4096-byte-sector device. The latter checks a full host-side
disk hash. Direct refusals check the boot region, started flag, retained position
and claim. Handoff cases check descriptor cleanup, claim release/reacquisition,
error propagation and final sync. Success preserves every byte outside the main
partition, including alignment gaps and both GPT copies.

Independent host readback checks GPT CRCs/geometry with the existing parser and
`sfdisk`, copies the partition to a temporary file, and checks native exFAT boot
copies/checksum/label/cluster/size/partition offset with CP16a's reader, `fsck.exfat
-n` and `dump.exfat`. No offset patching is used. Both 13-case FAT16 and FAT32
handoff regressions pass, including real kernel mounting, full-volume writes and
cleanup. File-format regression coverage expands to 84 cases (nonzero file offset,
unaligned offset and overflowing extent are new), plus the existing 17 native
policy rows. These pass normally and with sanitizers; normal FAT16/FAT32/NTFS,
format-options and shared-policy component suites also pass. The full normal
Linux build passes; existing upstream header pedantic warnings remain.

Guests use installed kernel `6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts`, QEMU TCG (no `/dev/kvm`),
a 64-MiB emulated removable disk and no network. The native tools/system libraries
remain distribution binaries; sanitizer coverage is for our adapters, shared
runner and preparation backend. This is formatter/ownership qualification, not
an exFAT kernel mount, copied-file or boot qualification. Real desktop automount
and physical hot-unplug remain separate checks.

Reproduction (from the repository root; use a new output directory each run):

```sh
cmake -S linux -B /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build -DRUFUS_BUILD_VM_TEST=ON
cmake --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --target test_mbr_handoff_guest udisks_fixture partition_image_probe
python3 linux/tests/vm/mbr.py --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --kernel 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts --accel tcg --exfat /tmp/rufus-exfat-guest
cmake -S linux -B /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build -DRUFUS_BUILD_VM_TEST=OFF
```

**Cleanup and next step:** every runner removes its emulated disk, copied
partition, guest kernel and initramfs/staging trees, including on failure. Small
logs, commands, hashes and results remain under parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16c-*`. Both VM build flags return to OFF. No physical USB,
user ISO, Windows customization test, host installation or download was used.
Next is a complete non-bootable GPT/exFAT helper job, followed by GUI exposure as
a separate checkpoint.

Upstream evidence: [exfatprogs exclusive open and sysfs discovery](https://github.com/exfatprogs/exfatprogs/blob/1.4.3/lib/libexfat.c#L404)
and [native partition-offset selection](https://github.com/exfatprogs/exfatprogs/blob/1.4.3/mkfs/mkfs.c#L1555).

## CP16d — Non-bootable GPT/exFAT helper job (2026-09-24)

**Scope:** connect CP16c's qualified partition adapter to a complete job using
the existing Qt process client, pipe protocol and authorized helper. Add the
distinct `format-exfat-device-v1` operation. It is device-only and rejects ISO
sources, enhanced installation, Windows settings, bootloader options, formatter
paths and supplied volume serials. Native exfatprogs generates the serial. The
request retains the existing target identity/use and disk-sequence checks.
Older FAT/NTFS operations retain their meanings; decode rejection preserves the
previous destination object. No Windows source changes are required.

**Before writes:** plan the ordinary one-partition Rufus GPT, validate label and
native metadata space, then check runtime libblkid and the trusted formatter's
help for every required option. The help query uses a clean C locale, a
three-second deadline, cancellation and a 16-KiB retained-output limit. Missing,
incompatible or unresponsive providers fail before changing the partition table;
there is no weakened-option retry. `mkfs.exfat` is now discovered for production
builds as an optional provider, independently of BUILD_TESTING. Missing exFAT
tools do not prevent existing FAT/NTFS builds. Generic GPT planning accepts up to
32-MiB clusters so exFAT's 128-KiB default and larger choices can reach the helper;
individual filesystem adapters still enforce their own restrictions. New GPT
file cases verify 128-KiB and 32-MiB layouts, preserved bytes and rejection at
64 MiB. Shared Rufus placement arithmetic is unchanged.

**Execution and completion:** reuse production GPT creation and the existing
formatter claim handoff. Report checking, partitioning, formatting and finalizing.
After native formatting/readback and partition sync, flush the reacquired whole
disk, retry EINTR and recheck its identity/use before success. Cancellation during
this final flush still waits for it. Sync failures remain failures. The client
requires all four stages, a valid filesystem extent, zero sync/cleanup errors
and process exit. It cannot skip straight to finalizing by applying the existing
mount-cleanup exception to a job without a mount stage. `started` remains true
after GPT writes even if formatting fails. No mounting, copying, eject or extra
authorization is added; the worker destroys the target before publishing its
outcome and the helper joins the worker before exiting.

**Validation:** all focused tests pass normally and under ASan/UBSan with leak
detection: 16 provider preflight cases, 84 existing exFAT file cases, 17 native
cluster-policy rows, 54 GPT image cases and 42 Qt preparation-process cases
(including fixture init/cleanup). Provider tests cover each missing capability,
missing tool, old library, unexpected exit, oversized help, timeout and
cancellation, with child/descriptor cleanup. Normal FAT16/FAT32/NTFS formatting,
format-options and both FAT helper regressions pass. The full normal Linux build
passes; existing upstream flexible-array/pedantic warnings remain.

`mbr.py --exfat-helper` runs 11 complete client/helper jobs in an offline QEMU
TCG guest, normally and with sanitizers:

- Missing/old formatter, invalid label, insufficient metadata space and wrong
  disk sequence all fail with a byte-for-byte unchanged whole-disk hash.
- Formatter failure and cancellation preserve the partial-media state and
  release/reacquire ownership before exit.
- Final whole-disk sync failure, cancellation and EINTR recovery are injected
  only in a guest-specific helper probe; production has no fault controls.
- Success uses the production helper with real exfatprogs. Independent host
  readback checks both GPT CRCs/geometry, native exFAT boot copies/checksum,
  offset, size, Unicode label and 128-KiB clusters, plus `fsck.exfat -n` and
  `dump.exfat`.

The guest uses real kernel USB/partition nodes and a private UDisks fixture.
Its root-only authorization stand-in counts exactly one launch per job and
briefly delays launcher exit after the helper result. The production Qt client
must remain active during that delay, then report exactly one final result.
Every case checks phase order, no copied bytes, released claims, descriptor and
child cleanup, and no private mount directories. This qualifies the job lifetime;
it does not test desktop polkit prompts, physical automount/hot-unplug, exFAT
kernel mounting or bootability. The installed kernel is
`6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts`; providers are exfatprogs 1.4.3 and libblkid 2.42.4.
Native system utilities/libraries are distribution binaries; our code is
instrumented in the sanitizer run.

Reproduction is documented in [the VM guide](../linux/tests/vm/README.md#non-bootable-gptexfat-helper-qualification-cp16d).
All disposable 64-MiB disks, copied partitions, kernels and initramfs/staging
trees were removed. Small logs, manifests, hashes and the scoped source patch
remain in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16d-*`. Both VM build flags return to
OFF. No physical USB, user ISO, host installation or Windows customization test
was used. **Next: CP16e, Qt non-bootable GPT/exFAT selection and behavior parity.**

## CP16e — Non-bootable GPT/exFAT in Qt (2026-09-24)

**Scope and source comparison:** expose CP16d's complete non-bootable format job
through the existing Widgets/controller lifecycle. Compare Win32 SetBootOptions,
SetPartitionSchemeAndTargetSystem, SetProposedLabel, EnableControls and the boot
selection handler in `src/rufus.c`, ToValidLabel in `src/format.c`, and the shared
filesystem/progress policies. Boot selection now places Non bootable before Disk
or ISO image and initially selects image mode. Switching retains the selected
ISO/DD image, disables SELECT and hides image-specific choices. Switching back
restores the image route. The proposed label comes from the device unless the
user edited it. Busy jobs reject mode/settings changes.

**Supported route:** GPT/exFAT only, with BIOS or UEFI as on Win32's non-bootable
form. Quick format remains selected; unsupported full format, bad-block checks
and extended label/icon creation remain disabled. Windows also offers MBR/SFD
and other filesystems, and normally falls back to MBR without a preference.
This narrower Linux list is a temporary qualification boundary, not complete
non-bootable parity. Native GPT cluster filtering now accepts exFAT, preserves
Rufus's whole-disk defaults and rejects metadata that cannot fit the rounded
partition. It does not allocate media, open devices or request authorization.
No exFAT choice is added to ISO extraction or Syslinux.

**Controller reuse:** the existing creation controller accepts the source-free
exFAT plan. Its asynchronous worker checks device identity/use, disk sequence,
geometry, normalized label and installed providers before destructive
confirmation, then repeats those checks before starting the one authorized
helper. It never opens the retained ISO for this job. The request has no image,
Windows options, Syslinux installation or caller-specified serial. Win32 applies
FAT-style ToValidLabel normalization to exFAT, so the GUI reuses that shared
algorithm and shows its effective result in confirmation. The native adapter's
Unicode-capable interface is retained. Enhanced Windows install preferences
cannot reset the non-bootable cluster selection or enter its request.

**Progress and completion:** use InitProgressState with BT_NON_BOOTABLE and the
original ten exFAT filesystem steps, with no copy/customization slots. The native
formatter has no intermediate progress callbacks; the existing phase changes
advance to shared operation boundaries. The first of two finalization slots
is 15/16 (61439/65535). Full READY still requires successful device sync/cleanup,
helper exit, the confirmed partition extent, an entirely formatted partition
and zero copied bytes. Failure/cancellation stays below full completion and
never sounds the success notification. Unplug after success preserves READY
and does not repeat the notification.

**Tests:** 14 new functional Widgets rows cover the initial controls, retained
ISO/DD selections, normalized confirmation, 128-KiB cluster request, exclusion
of Windows preferences, one helper launch, result-before-exit waiting, complete
READY/unplug behavior, denied authorization, sync/cleanup errors, wrong extent,
short filesystem result, omitted finalizing, cancellation in formatting/final
sync, and providers disappearing before confirmation or before authorization.
Five window rows cover the too-small/too-large boundaries and the 4/32/128-KiB
defaults. A geometry component case independently checks every offered cluster
against its actual GPT extent and refuses Syslinux/exFAT.

Normal and ASan/UBSan runs with leak detection pass the format-options (35),
preparation-process (42), image-analysis Widgets (46), window (57), scaled-window
(3), and complete write-Widgets (155 passed, two optional skips) suites. Qt totals
include fixture initialization/cleanup. The skips are existing opt-in read-only
real Windows/Alpine ISO selections, whose environment variables were unset;
all new exFAT cases ran. No new Windows customization qualification was added.
The Widgets fixture uses private UDisks/D-Bus properties, regular files and a
protocol-only child; it verifies that the backing file stays unchanged. Actual
native disk creation/readback remains the separately recorded CP16d guest proof.
The tests run outside the ptrace/socket sandbox for private D-Bus and LeakSanitizer,
without root, physical device access or host polkit prompts.

The first run caught a stale identity in the resized test fixture; rebuilding
its identity from the fixture's own UDisks properties fixed the test. Another
case caught an unwanted cluster reset when toggling the Windows-only enhanced
setting; the production controller now leaves non-bootable geometry alone.
The initial expected progress value used the wrong filesystem step count; it
was corrected against the original exFAT allocation. The full final suites pass.
The full normal Linux build passes with the existing upstream header warnings.

A rendered offscreen form was inspected and retained as parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16e-exfat.png`; it shows the short device-count footer,
disabled SELECT, editable formatting fields and empty idle READY bar. Logs,
source baseline/patch and hashes are retained beside it. Temporary regular-file
and generated-ISO fixtures are automatically removed. No VM disk, source ISO,
physical USB, host installation or download was needed; both VM build flags
remain OFF. **Next: CP16f, non-bootable GPT/FAT16 and FAT32 completion, before
exposing those filesystem choices.** MBR/SFD and non-bootable NTFS remain later
bounded steps.

## CP16f — Non-bootable GPT/FAT16 and FAT32 backend (2026-09-24)

**Scope:** complete source-free FAT formatting through the same authorized
helper, before exposing additional Qt choices. `format-fat16-device-v1` and

contracts. Reject regular-file targets, image sources and boot/customization
settings. FAT keeps the requested serial; exFAT retains its native serial rule.
Existing native FAT geometry/tool checks run before GPT writes. Formatting uses
the already qualified partition descriptor handoff and metadata verification.
The small final whole-disk sync/recheck operation is now shared with exFAT;
interrupted sync retries, sync errors remain failures and cancellation waits
for sync. The client requires finalizing and joined helper exit before success.
No Windows code, formatter implementation or additional authorization was added.

**Native qualification:** extend the existing offline QEMU recipe with
`--fat-helper --fat-bits 16|32`. Each filesystem passes ten complete client/helper
jobs on a 64-MiB emulated USB: missing formatter, bad label, invalid cluster,
changed disk sequence, formatter failure/cancellation, final-sync
failure/cancellation, interrupted-sync recovery and success. All four preflight
refusals hash the entire disk to prove no write occurred. Every case checks one
authorization launcher, ordered phases, joined exit, released device claim,
zero copied bytes and process/descriptor cleanup. Cancellation during final
sync also checks the retained exclusive whole-disk claim. The guest launcher
holds its exit briefly after the production helper result to test exit gating.
It is a root-only fixture stand-in, not a desktop polkit prompt qualification.

**Readback:** independently verify protective MBR, both GPT headers/tables and
their checksums, exact partition extent, FAT type, requested cluster size, hidden
sector offset, label, serial and FAT32 backup boot sector. Native `fsck.fat -n`
reports clean filesystems and `mdir` finds no files. FAT16's 2048-byte-cluster
fixture produces a 65,995,776-byte filesystem inside its 66,027,520-byte partition;
the 62-sector gap is permitted native track rounding. FAT32's 512-byte-cluster
fixture uses its entire 66,028,032-byte partition. The helper's reported bytes
match those independent BPB totals. No bootloader, mount/copy or boot claim is
part of these non-bootable jobs.

**Checks:** both FAT sets and the existing eleven-job GPT/exFAT regression pass
normally and with ASan/UBSan plus leak detection: 31 jobs per build, 62 total.
The preparation-process suite passes 44 rows per build, including the two new
FAT protocol boundary cases and unchanged legacy operations. The existing
non-bootable exFAT Widgets subset passes 16 rows per build (including test setup
and cleanup), covering selection, completion, failures, cancellation and
preflight refusal. No optional tests were skipped in these focused suites.
The full normal Linux build passes; Python/shell syntax and scoped whitespace
checks pass. Existing unrelated CRLF whitespace reports in `src/parser.c`
remain outside this checkpoint.

The first sanitizer FAT16 run caught a fixture race: the worker's sync marker
can become visible before Qt delivers its queued phase notification. The test
now observes both before cancelling; its rerun and the FAT32/exFAT sanitizer
runs pass. This did not require a production workaround. Small failure logs
are retained alongside the passing evidence.

Reproduction is in [the VM guide](../linux/tests/vm/README.md#non-bootable-gptfat16-and-fat32-helper-qualification-cp16f).
Disposable disks, copied partitions, kernels and guest staging trees are removed;
logs, manifests, hashes and the scoped source patch remain in parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16f-*`. Both VM build flags return to OFF. No physical
USB, source ISO, host installation or Windows customization qualification was
used. **Next: CP16g, expose these qualified GPT/FAT16 and FAT32 jobs in Qt with
shared Rufus filesystem defaults, preflight, confirmation and progress.** The
current non-bootable GUI remains GPT/exFAT until that bounded checkpoint.

## CP16g — Non-bootable GPT/FAT16 and FAT32 in Qt (2026-09-24)

**Scope:** expose CP16f's qualified format jobs through the existing Widgets
creation controller. Non bootable now offers FAT16, FAT32 and exFAT according to
native geometry. Source comparison uses Win32 SetFileSystemAndClusterSize and
its existing/manual filesystem selection, plus InitProgressBar in `src/ui.c`.
Reuse the shared allowed-filesystem, cluster/default and label algorithms. The
first available native format carries Default; a supported existing format or
manual choice takes precedence for selection. FAT16 ends at 4 GiB, FAT32 at
2 TiB, and metadata/cluster-count checks remove unusable choices. The user's
plain FAT32 naming decision remains in force at every capacity. GPT is still
the only qualified non-bootable layout and NTFS is not offered in this mode yet.

**Creation:** use the explicit non-bootable request flag for source-free
preflight, progress and status instead of identifying that workflow by exFAT.
The worker plans the GPT extent, checks FAT options and the configured mkfs.fat
executable before destructive confirmation, then repeats those checks before
authorization. The path comes from the same CMake provider as the helper.
Confirmation names the filesystem, normalized label and cluster size without
an Image field. Source, Syslinux, enhanced Windows installation and customization
preferences do not enter the format request, even with a Windows ISO retained
in the other boot-selection mode. FAT keeps its generated volume serial.

**Progress/completion:** use the original five filesystem steps for FAT16/FAT32
and ten for exFAT, with no copy/customization slots. Before final sync completes,
small FAT formats reach 10/11 (59577/65535); FAT32 at 32 GiB and above uses the
original analog-format weighting and reaches 99% (64879/65535). The CLI provides
no intermediate formatting callbacks, so progress advances at phase boundaries.
Full READY still requires successful sync/cleanup, the confirmed partition
extent, zero copied bytes and helper exit. FAT's native track-rounding tail is
permitted; exFAT still requires its exact full volume length. Failed/cancelled
jobs stay below full completion without a success notification.

**Tests:** add 23 functional write-Widgets rows and nine window rows. Extend the
existing format lifecycle cases across FAT16/FAT32/exFAT for one helper launch,
confirmation, normalized labels, retained images/settings, result-before-exit
waiting, success/unplug, denied authorization, sync/cleanup failures, wrong
layout, omitted finalizing, cancellation during formatting/final sync, and a
provider disappearing before confirmation or authorization. Two creation cases
retain a generated Windows ISO and verify it is excluded from the request. A
64-GiB FAT32 case checks the large-format weighting by simulating capacity; it
does not allocate a 64-GiB file. Window cases cover the filesystem ordering,
Default marker, existing formats, unsupported NTFS fallback, manual choices and
capacity boundaries. The earlier exFAT limits/selection tests are retained.

Normal and ASan/UBSan runs with leak detection pass format-options (35),
preparation-process (44), image-analysis Widgets (46), window (66), scaled-window
(3), and the complete write-Widgets suite (178 passed, two optional skips).
Qt totals include fixture setup/cleanup. The skips are the existing opt-in
read-only real Windows/Alpine ISO selection cases whose environment variables
were unset; every new case ran. These are private UDisks/D-Bus, regular-file and
protocol-child tests: they assert no target-file changes. CP16f remains the
actual native helper/device/readback qualification. No extra Windows
customization test, physical USB or host polkit operation was used.

The full normal Linux build and scoped whitespace checks pass. Focused and full
runs found no production regression. The tests run outside the ptrace/socket
sandbox for private D-Bus and LeakSanitizer. A rendered offscreen form was
inspected and retained as parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16g-nonbootable.png`;
it shows the short device-count footer, empty idle READY, disabled SELECT and
editable formatting controls. Logs, source baseline/patch and hashes remain in
`cp16g-*`. Temporary regular files and generated ISO fixtures are automatically
removed; both VM build flags remain OFF.

**Next: CP16h, source-free GPT/NTFS preparation without UEFI:NTFS, followed by Qt
exposure after native completion/readback qualification.** Non-bootable MBR/SFD
layouts remain separate steps.

## CP16h — Non-bootable GPT/NTFS backend (2026-09-24)

**Scope:** `format-ntfs-device-v1` adds an explicit source-free NTFS job through
the existing authorized helper. It rejects file targets, image sources,
Syslinux/Windows/enhanced boot options and caller-selected volume serials.
The native formatter generates its own serial. Geometry and provider checks
precede partition writes. The layout contains one GPT data partition; it
reserves no UEFI:NTFS extent and never materializes or writes the boot payload.
No mount support or source-tree checks are needed for a format-only job.

**Reuse:** adapt the existing NTFS preparation routine and partition formatter;
no new formatting implementation, provider layer or Windows changes. NTFS keeps
the exclusive whole-disk claim while mkntfs runs and during metadata readback.
The optional boot-partition descriptor is opened/rechecked only for bootable
requests. Incompatible combinations of the request mode and boot-partition
layout are refused before accessing the device. Bootable NTFS keeps its existing
embedded payload, second partition, bootloader phase and image-extraction path.
Non-bootable NTFS instead uses the existing final whole-disk sync/recheck and
requires finalizing plus helper exit before the client reports success.

**Native tests:** extend the existing guarded, offline 64-MiB QEMU fixture with
`--ntfs-helper`. Ten non-bootable jobs cover missing formatter, invalid label,
invalid cluster, changed disk sequence, formatter failure/cancellation,
final-sync failure/cancellation, interrupted-sync retry and success. Four
preflight refusals verify the entire disk is unchanged. The formatter wrapper
checks the retained exclusive claim before all six write attempts; cancellation
also verifies the claim while the formatter/final sync is blocked. Every job
checks one authorization launcher, phase order, zero copied bytes, joined exit,
released claim and process/descriptor cleanup. The launcher is a guest-only
stand-in, not a real desktop polkit prompt test.

Before those jobs, one existing bootable NTFS request checks its original
four-phase preparation contract and verifies the complete written UEFI:NTFS
payload byte-for-byte against the repository resource. The new jobs subsequently
replace its two-partition layout with one data partition. Two direct adapter
checks refuse bootable/non-bootable layout mismatches before device access.
Independent host inspection checks both GPT copies/checksums and the exact
single partition, then NTFS 3.1 metadata, primary/backup boot sectors, 4096-byte
clusters, hidden-sector offset, native serial, Unicode label and clean flags.
`ntfsck -n` succeeds. The final volume occupies all 66,027,520 bytes of its
partition at offset 1,048,576. This is formatting/readback and boot-payload
regression coverage, not an OS boot or new Windows customization qualification.

Both normal and ASan/UBSan guest runs with leak detection pass all eleven jobs
(22 total), using installed ntfsprogs-plus 1.0.0-3. The first normal attempt
exposed a missing `/tmp` directory in the minimal fixture, needed by Qt's
existing bootable embedded-payload temporary file. Adding that standard guest
directory resolved it; no production workaround was introduced. Keep the small
failed-run evidence alongside the successful retry.

The preparation-process suite passes 45 rows per build, including the added
NTFS format protocol boundaries and preserved legacy request semantics. The
complete write-Widgets regression passes 178 rows per build, with the same two
opt-in real Windows/Alpine ISO selection skips; all enabled cases run normally
and with sanitizers. Qt totals include setup/cleanup. The full normal Linux
build and Python/shell syntax/scoped whitespace checks pass. Qt tests use
private D-Bus and regular files outside the ptrace/socket sandbox; no host
physical USB or polkit operation is performed.

Reproduction is in [the VM guide](../linux/tests/vm/README.md#non-bootable-gptntfs-helper-qualification-cp16h).
Disposable disks, copied partitions, kernels and guest trees are removed even
on failure. Logs, manifests, provider versions, source baseline/patch and hashes
remain in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16h-*`. Both VM build flags return to
OFF. **Next: CP16i, non-bootable GPT/NTFS in Qt**, including payload-free cluster
geometry and the original non-image NTFS progress allocation. The current GUI
still offers FAT16/FAT32/exFAT in Non bootable; MBR/SFD remain later checkpoints.

### CP16j — non-bootable MBR table backend (2026-09-24)

Generalized the existing Linux MBR API to `MBR_IMAGE_OPTIONS/RESULT`,
`PlanMbrImageLayout`, `CreateMbrImage`, `CheckMbrImage` and `PrepareMbrTarget`.
The explicit `syslinux` field selects the old active FAT16/FAT32 contract;
all previous callers set it explicitly. The native Syslinux installer rejects
layouts that do not select Syslinux. No compatibility wrapper hierarchy or
Windows source edits were needed.

Source comparison: `drive.c:CreatePartition` uses inactive non-bootable data
partitions with type 0x0e for FAT16, 0x0c for FAT32 and 0x07 for NTFS/exFAT.
`format.c:WriteMBR` calls `write_zero_mbr`, whose original payload clears the
first 446 bytes, including the disk signature. Linux reuses that exact payload
and the existing Syslinux payload, preserving the partition table and 55-AA
marker. Both modes reuse common Rufus placement/track/cluster arithmetic,
libfdisk creation and existing descriptor/cancellation/sync/readback handling.
Table-only creation rejects GPT. Explicit preparation clears the bounded
primary/backup GPT and new-partition-prefix ranges before creating the table.
Readback never repairs damaged metadata.

Extended the existing regular-file MBR/clearing matrices for all four
non-bootable filesystems. Independent sfdisk JSON/verification and raw readback
check payload bytes, zero/nonzero disk signature, active flag, type, exact
extent and empty unused entries. Geometry includes the 2-TiB boundary without
allocating/opening large images, filesystem-specific maximum layout cluster
sizes and invalid sector/track/cluster inputs. Syslinux rejects NTFS/exFAT.
FAT readback additionally rejects the opposite boot mode for the same extent.
Failure injection covers descriptor refusal, pre-write/cancellation checks,
changed capacity, table/boot-code write failures, partial/interrupted I/O,
corrupt code/signature/active/type/extent/marker, stale GPT refusal, clearing
failures, final clearing readback and sync failure/interruption. Descriptor
position/flags/counts and bytes outside the authorized ranges are checked.

All twelve MBR CTest suites pass normally and with ASan/UBSan/leak detection:
560 planner/writer/checker calls per build (372 new non-bootable calls and 188
existing Syslinux regressions). This is partition-table/clearing qualification,
not native filesystem formatting or boot qualification. Callers must still
validate the selected formatter's geometry and qualify complete device jobs.
The largest actual image is about 129 MiB; every fixture is removed on exit.

The full normal Linux build and selected sanitizer build pass. Both existing
MBR guest executables also compile against the generalized interface, without
running a VM or creating a guest disk. Normal regressions pass: format options
36 rows, ISO write checks 119 rows, write-Widgets 190 rows (the same two optional
real-ISO selection skips), and shared partition-layout tests. Qt counts include
setup/cleanup. The Widgets fixture uses private D-Bus and regular files; no
physical USB or real authorization is used. No Windows customization or
installation qualification was added.

Python syntax and scoped whitespace checks pass. Logs, baseline, source hashes
and the scoped patch remain in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16j-*`; temporary
fixture media and edit scripts are removed. Both VM build flags are OFF.
**Next: CP16k, source-free non-bootable MBR/FAT16 and FAT32 device-helper jobs**,
with native guest readback before Qt exposure. MBR/NTFS, MBR/exFAT and SFD remain
separate later steps. The current Non bootable GUI stays GPT-only.

### CP16o — SFD whole-device preparation (2026-09-25)

Resumed this checkpoint after the user's full Windows-parity decision, which
supersedes the SFD deferral recorded in CP17a. Added the grouped feature backlog
and persistent scope instruction: all Windows features remain targets, with no
fixed implementation order. Existing Linux differences and the single Windows
customization qualification limit remain unchanged.

Compared `src/rufus.c:SetPartitionSchemeAndTargetSystem`,
`src/drive.c:CreatePartition` and `src/format.c:ClearMBRGPT`: SFD is a
non-bootable layout with the filesystem at byte zero and no new partition table.
The native layout returns the entire capacity without MBR/GPT, track or cluster
rounding. It requires nonempty, sector-aligned media and currently supports
512-byte sectors; each filesystem must validate its own geometry separately.
There is no inherited 2-TiB MBR limit or artificial 2-MiB partition-layout minimum.
The larger bound is tested by planning only, without allocating a large image.

Preparation reuses the MBR descriptor/identity checks and clearing implementation,
with the first 8 MiB and last 1 MiB bounded to the actual capacity and no overlap.
Unlike an MBR job it adds no partition-prefix clearing beyond those disk ranges
and creates no table. Preserve descriptor flags/position and sync after every
attempted write, including failure/cancellation; verify cleared regions after
sync. Tail failures are fatal, retaining the existing documented Linux choice
instead of Windows's warning-and-continue behavior. This is metadata preparation,
not a secure erase or removal of all signatures anywhere on the disk.

The new SFD suite passes 42 planning/preparation cases and two native FAT32
formats normally and under ASan/UBSan/leak detection. It covers small/overlapping
ranges, odd sector counts, planning beyond 2 TiB, invalid geometry/descriptors,
capacity changes, cancellation, interrupted/partial/zero writes, readback failure
and corruption in both clearing regions, sync failure and retained-descriptor
path replacement. Rejected requests preserve the target; valid clearing preserves
all middle data. No libfdisk table-writing call occurs. Native FAT32 formatting
on exact-size files follows stale GPT removal; independent BPB/backup checks,
fsck.fat and mtools confirm offset zero, no hidden sectors, expected volume ID/
label, capacity and no actual partition entries. sfdisk may report an empty DOS
label from the FAT 55-AA marker; the initial return-code-only assertion was
corrected after checking that behavior against a native mkfs.fat output.

All nine focused CTest suites pass normally and under sanitizers: SFD, six
existing MBR preparation variants, GPT creation and FAT32 formatting. After
removing the inherited minimum, the expanded SFD suite was rerun in both builds.
The full normal build and selected sanitizer probes pass, using Ninja default
parallelism. No Windows source, helper protocol or GUI behavior changed.

No physical USB, real polkit, filesystem mounts, VM boot or additional Windows
customization qualification was performed. Tests delete their temporary files;
no new large fixtures are retained. Both VM build flags remain OFF. Logs, scoped
source patch/baseline and hashes remain in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16o-*`.
**Next SFD checkpoint: CP16p**, whole-device formatter handoff, stale kernel
partition removal, exclusive reacquisition and final native readback inside one
authorized job; keep SFD unavailable in Qt until qualified. FAT16/NTFS/exFAT SFD
and the independent CP17b mounted-target work remain in scope.


### CP16p — SFD/FAT32 native block handoff (2026-09-25)

Added an explicit SFD layout to PrepareDeviceTarget, gated to non-bootable
FAT32. The caller first clears old disk metadata through CP16o's PrepareSfdTarget.
The handoff requires offset zero/exact disk capacity, refreshes the kernel
partition table and refuses any remaining children before opening a retained
non-exclusive whole-disk descriptor. Stock mkfs.fat then obtains its own O_EXCL
access through that descriptor. The parent reacquires exclusive access without
an extra launcher/authorization, rechecks disk identity/sequence/capacity/use,
and verifies the resulting FAT32 volume and empty MBR entry area. Mount/copy
and other SFD filesystems remain gated. Existing MBR/GPT snapshot/readback paths
retain their behavior; the native formatter itself required no new code.

Normal and ASan/UBSan/leak-detection runs pass all 13 SFD handoff cases on a real
QEMU USB block device, plus bootable/NTFS request refusals and a 4096-byte-sector
refusal with unchanged host image hash. Cases cover uncleared GPT/kernel children,
wrong extent/cluster, busy old partition, cancellation, formatter failure, sync
failure, competing claim on reacquisition, corrupted BPB/nested MBR entries after
formatter readback, and success. Actual stale GPT children are present before
format; successful handoff removes them. Descriptor counts, final claim and
unsupported mount behavior are checked. The formatter wrapper independently
checks that the disk claim was released. No competing claim is bypassed.

Independent host readback passes native fsck.fat/mtools and BPB/backup/label/ID,
zero hidden-sector and empty partition-entry checks. The whole 64-MiB target
contains 67,092,480 filesystem bytes after native sub-track rounding, starting
at byte zero. Normal and sanitizer shared MBR/GPT handoff regressions also pass
all 13 cases, including full-volume writes and mount/sync cleanup. Guest runs
use Linux 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts with CPU emulation because /dev/kvm is unavailable
in this environment. No sanitizer diagnostics were reported. The full normal
build and selected sanitizer guest targets pass with Ninja's default parallelism.

The guest uses a private UDisks fixture with real Linux block ioctls/claim behavior.
No host devices, mounts, polkit prompts, GUI flow or extra Windows customization
qualification are involved; this is not yet the complete source-free helper job.
The recipe removes generated USB images, copied volumes, kernels and guest trees;
logs, manifests, commands and readback hashes remain under parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp16p-*`. Both VM build flags return to OFF. Reproduction
instructions are in [the VM guide](../linux/tests/vm/README.md#sfdfat32-native-device-handoff-cp16p).
**Next: CP16q**, connect the SFD/FAT32 preflight and source-free helper operation,
verify one launch through failure/cancellation/final sync, then expose the Qt
choice in a separate checkpoint. Other SFD filesystems remain in scope.

and sanitizer builds pass with Ninja's default parallelism.

Guests use Linux 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts under CPU emulation, private UDisks fixture
properties and a guest-only pkexec stand-in. These exercise the real helper and
native block operations, not a real polkit dialog or physical USB. No further
Windows customization qualification was performed. No Windows source changed.
The GUI still offers only qualified MBR/GPT choices; SFD selection/confirmation
and Windows-default parity are **CP16r**. Other SFD filesystems remain in scope.

also rejects bootable SFD, uncleared GPT children and shifted/shortened extents.
The native whole-device formatter fails without changing media when our exclusive
claim remains held, proving why this path needs the existing handoff. On success
it formats the full 64-MiB volume at byte zero. Each job checks one launcher,
ordered phases, client waiting for helper exit and descriptor/claim/child cleanup.

The injected-entry test modifies both exFAT boot regions and recomputes their
checksums. It explicitly verifies that ordinary volume readback still succeeds,
then requires the independent SFD empty-entry check to reject the result. This
avoids attributing a checksum failure to partition validation. Independent host
readback verifies full extent, zero partition offset, matching boot regions and
checksums, empty partition entries, FAT/heap/cluster geometry and Unicode label,
then runs fsck.exfat/dump.exfat. Disk/source hashes and native tool hashes are
retained in manifests/results.

Normal MBR/exFAT regression passes thirteen complete helper jobs. The direct
GPT exFAT regression passes nineteen block/claim cases plus refusal of 4096-byte
logical sectors, retaining expected-device/capacity/offset checks, read-only and
wrong-target refusals, metadata checks, claim handoff and sync. New SFD creation
remains qualified only for 512-byte logical sectors. No new sector support is
implied by the shared adapter.

Normal host tests pass 84 native exFAT file-format cases, 16 provider preflight
cases and 17 native cluster-policy cases. The existing file tests already cover
zero partition offset and empty partition entries. The protocol suite adds an
exFAT SFD round trip and source/options/serial rejection. Its first run exposed a
stale reset expectation: unlike bootable FAT/NTFS operations, ordinary exFAT
requests already decode as non-bootable formatting. The test now preserves that
contract; the corrected 55-test suite passes. Five additional Qt controller rows
check a result held before exit, GPT-shaped/shortened results, sync failure and

### CP16x — exFAT SFD in the Qt workflow (2026-09-25)

Enabled the qualified exFAT SFD route by removing its temporary cluster-filter
gate and including exFAT when checking SFD availability. The existing switch
still limits formats to the four implemented filesystems. There are no backend,
protocol, formatter, privilege-flow or Windows source changes. Non-bootable SFD
now offers FAT16/FAT32/NTFS/exFAT where native whole-device geometry permits.
Shared Rufus filesystem order/defaults and remembered explicit choices still
apply. ExFAT uses the original FAT-style label normalization and its own progress
allocation, just as the existing GPT/MBR exFAT UI does.

Geometry tests check the 16-MiB whole-volume minimum, the 256-MiB and 32-GiB
default-cluster boundaries on both sides, 2 TiB and the final sector below the
shared 256-TiB limit. Every advertised cluster is checked against native exFAT
geometry at offset zero and full device size. Sub-minimum, unaligned, 256-TiB,
bootable and Syslinux misuse are rejected. Oversized clusters that cannot fit
native metadata remain unavailable. These arithmetic/discovery cases allocate
no corresponding large disk and do not establish hardware compatibility at
those sizes.

The native-filesystem selection cases now cover NTFS and exFAT together: eighteen
rows exercise defaults, cluster labels/values, explicit SFD after the large-device
GPT default, and restoration of the manual filesystem preference after a
FAT16-only target. Existing FAT16/FAT32 selection checks account for exFAT in the
list. Nine additional GUI job rows cover exFAT result-before-exit waiting,
incorrect extents, sync failure, missing finalization, cancellation during format
and finalization, the minimum whole volume and a large target. Confirmation has
SFD/exFAT, the normalized label and Cancel as default; the request has no source
or boot options and lets the native formatter generate its serial. One launcher,
whole-device extent, progress 61439 before helper exit, full green READY after
exit and a single completion notification preserved after unplugging are checked.
The shared SFD job data now names each filesystem and expected progress directly.

Normal full Qt tests pass 337 cases, with the two existing opt-in real-ISO skips.
Format-options and normal/scaled window suites also pass. The captured exFAT SFD
screen was inspected: Super Floppy Disk, BIOS or UEFI, exFAT, 128 kilobytes
(Default), START and empty idle READY fit correctly. Final sanitizer results are
recorded below. Builds use Ninja's default parallelism and both VM flags remain

USB, real polkit prompt, large image or Windows customization test is needed.

## CP17b1 — mounted-target metadata checks (2026-09-25)

Audited Windows dismount/locking, Linux UDisks acquisition, preparation preflight
and the authorized helper's early private-mount-namespace setup. Added the shared
read-only `ListUDisksTargetMounts` candidate check and kept mounted creation
refused through `CheckUDisksTargetUse`. The list is published only after every
member passes; errors clear any previous output. New checks reject protected
child volumes, stale/missing targets, ambiguous mounted siblings, unknown mount
state, invalid mountpoint bytes and unknown mounted-volume flags or device IDs.
Source-device, swap, encrypted/active-crypto, RAID and physical-volume refusals
are retained. Candidates are UDisks object paths, with one entry per filesystem
regardless of the number of reported mountpoints.

The new component suite passes 61 cases including Qt setup/cleanup. It covers
unmounted, SFD/whole-device, partitioned and multiple-mountpoint snapshots;
partition-table membership without a drive association; irrelevant other-device
mounts; stale identities; mount metadata errors; and dangerous members before
or after an otherwise eligible mounted member. Every failure leaves an empty
candidate list. A private D-Bus functional case checks decoded `aay` MountPoints
from a real ObjectManager reply and verifies that DD still refuses the mounted
target with zero OpenDevice requests. Its regular-file device fixture remains
unchanged; no real device is opened.

All four selected normal CTest suites pass: mount metadata 61 cases, target
acquisition 51, discovery 46 and raw-write/ISO/non-bootable Widgets 337 with the
two existing optional real-ISO skips. Normal full build passes with default
Ninja parallelism. Sanitizer results are recorded below. No Windows source,
helper privilege flow, protocol, GUI controls or formatter changed. VM options
remain OFF; no large fixture or Windows customization qualification was run.

This is metadata qualification, not proof that a filesystem can be unmounted.
Native mount/source ancestry, sysfs holders, swap, busy mounts, cancellation,
service/identity changes and both mount namespaces must be qualified next before
unmounting is enabled. In particular, source st_dev does not directly identify
a backing block device for FUSE/layered filesystems. The port plan records this
and the single-authorization constraint for both helper jobs and DD. Do not
expose the new candidate API as an unchecked unmount permission.

Compact evidence is retained under parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp17b1-*`:
baseline, scoped patch, hashes, build and test logs. No large artifacts were
created. Changes remain local and uncommitted.

Final ASan/UBSan/leak-detection build and the same four CTest suites pass:
**495 passed, 2 existing optional skips** in each build, with no sanitizer
diagnostics. Full GUI runtime was about 74 seconds normally and 125 seconds
under sanitizers, within the existing timeout. Checkpoint diff/added-line
whitespace reviewed. No physical USB or host mount was touched.


## CP17b2 — native mounted-target backend (2026-09-25)

Added a small native adapter using the system libmount parser and ordinary
`umount2`. No Windows, formatter, protocol or GUI changes. The adapter checks the
kernel disk/partition inventory, holders/slaves, retained source and swap, mount
IDs, known system/executable/current-directory filesystems and disk sequence.
It rejects unknown, nested/aliased and unsupported layouts and revalidates all
remaining mounts before each operation. A pinned trusted parent and statx
identity check precede NOFOLLOW unmount; no force/lazy flag, retry, recursive
cleanup or privilege request is used. Partial completion remains explicit on
failure/cancellation. The header and plan state caller obligations and the
synchronous syscall's cancellation limit.

The new `target_mounts.py` guest recipe passes **27 native cases in both normal
and ASan/UBSan/leak-detection builds**, using kernel 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts and TCG.
Actual kernel checks include open-file EBUSY, target source file, active swap,
DM partition holders and layered devices, nested/bind/system mounts, current
directory protection, partial cancellation and successful two-volume unmount.
Read-only retained disk descriptors coexist with mounted filesystems; a fresh
exclusive whole-disk claim must succeed after complete cleanup. The retained
independent memory source remains readable. Independent host fsck.fat passes
for both partitions after each completed guest recipe.

The private-namespace case proves that a second mount copy keeps O_EXCL busy
after the original mount is removed, even when the original namespace's native
inventory is empty. The child unmounts its copy and exits before the claim can
succeed. This supports the planned helper namespace reordering instead of merely
relaxing UDisks's mounted-target refusal. Test-only wrappers inject malformed or
unavailable mountinfo, unsupported filesystem data, unmount failure and a cancel
after the first syscall. Disk/mount identity mismatch and untrusted parents
refuse before any unmount call.

The expanded fixture initially failed because no udev creates `/dev/mapper`
aliases in this minimal guest; using its devtmpfs mapper node fixed the fixture.
All completed and failed guest disks/trees were removed after logs were retained.
Final evidence: `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp17b2-native-qualified/` and
`cp17b2-native-sanitizers/`, plus baseline/build logs, scoped patch and hashes.
The earlier runs remain as compact logs only. No host USB/mounts or new Windows
customization qualification. No real authorization claim: the native backend
runs already privileged in the guest and is not integrated with creation yet.

CP17b3 must match UDisks candidates, protect authenticated caller paths, resolve
namespace lifetime within one authorized job, then qualify exclusive acquisition
and helper cancellation before mounted creation is enabled. FUSE/NTFS-3G targets
and unresolved FUSE/overlay/loop/multi-device source backing remain refused and
in scope for later support. Native mountpoint parents must currently be trusted.

Final normal and sanitizer full builds pass with default Ninja parallelism and
both VM build flags restored OFF. The existing 61 UDisks candidate checks pass
in both builds. The sandboxed host sanitizer run passed all assertions but its
final leak check could not inspect the process under the sandbox's ptrace
restriction; repeating this read-only test outside the sandbox passed with
leak detection enabled. The native VM sanitizer run passed without that issue.
No repeated full GUI qualification was needed: this checkpoint's native adapter
is not linked into the GUI/helper execution path. Free space remains about
116 GiB in the project filesystem and 14 GiB in `/tmp`.


## CP17b3 — worker mount-namespace lifetime (2026-09-25)

The preparation helper now isolates its worker after source validation and
exclusive target acquisition, before writes. Native mount inventory uses
`/proc/thread-self/mountinfo`. Other Qt threads keep the original namespace;
worker children inherit the private one. The descriptor table stays shared for
the helper lifetime. Namespace errors use the existing job error/cleanup path.
No protocol, Windows, GUI or authorization flow change. Mounted creation remains
refused pending CP17b4 candidate matching, caller-path protection and integration.

Qualification passed normally and with ASan/UBSan/leak detection, using kernel
6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts and TCG for disposable guest devices:

- **31 native mount cases** per build: the previous 27 plus worker unshare
  failure, propagation failure, cancellation before isolation, and successful
  QThread isolation with QProcess and posix_spawn child inheritance. The guest
  starts with shared propagation. The main thread must not see the worker mount,
  while O_EXCL remains busy until worker cleanup. Independent host fsck passes
  on both FAT16 volumes after each recipe.
- **Five production Syslinux helper jobs** per build: missing/incompatible
  installer inputs, installer cancellation, and known/unknown image version
  success. Independent file readback, FAT metadata/fsck and MBR boot pass; the
  boot marker is `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK` and the backing digest stays unchanged during
  boot. The sanitizer helper uses the already qualified normal native installer.
- **14 SFD FAT32 client/helper jobs** per build: includes new unshare/propagation
  errors before writes with an unchanged entire-disk digest, plus existing
  preflight, cancellation, final-sync and success checks. Each job uses one
  launcher and waits for helper/descendant exit and descriptor cleanup.
  Independent whole-volume readback passes. The normal recipe's final console
  label still said 12 because it was running before the count label was fixed;
  its serial log and results contain all 14 validated cases. Labels now derive
  from the actual validated reports. NTFS/exFAT recipes inherit the new failure
  cases but were not rerun for this namespace checkpoint.
- **Four host CTest suites** per build: `rufus_prepare_process` (55 Qt cases),
  `rufus_prepare_helper`, `rufus_prepare_fat16_helper`, and `rufus_udisks_mounts`
  (61 Qt cases). All pass. The sanitizer host suite ran outside the sandbox to
  permit LeakSanitizer's process inspection. No sanitizer diagnostics.

Final full builds pass with default Ninja parallelism and VM test flags restored
OFF in both builds. Scoped changes and added-line whitespace reviewed. No host
USB/mount was touched, and no Windows customization test was added. No real
polkit prompt qualification is claimed; guest launchers simulate authorization.

## CP17b4 — exact mount matching and retained caller home (2026-09-25)

Added `MatchUDisksTargetMounts` beside the existing shared candidate check. It
requires disk number/sequence and exact one-to-one device/mountpoint agreement
with a freshly checked native inventory, independent of ordering. Raw path bytes
are compared directly. Stale, missing/extra, duplicated or aliased mounts fail;
existing source, protected-member and device-eligibility checks still apply.
The function takes a supplied UDisks snapshot; helper service-owner/freshness and
original source/device validation remain integration obligations.

Added libc account lookup and O_PATH/CLOEXEC retention of the authenticated
caller's home. Unknown/invalid accounts, non-directory homes and cancellation
fail. The lookup ignores HOME and follows account-home symlinks to protect the
actual filesystem. The existing native source backing check now also checks a
retained directory, including before every unmount. Target-backed or unresolved
homes fail without attempting an unmount. The caller retains/closes the home
descriptor for the complete job; omission is only for isolated native tests.
This checkpoint does not connect automatic unmounting to creation or change the
GUI, protocol, authorization flow or Windows code.

Validation passed normally and with ASan/UBSan/leak detection:

- **85 Qt metadata cases** per build (61 existing plus 24 matching cases):
  empty/whole-disk/partitioned targets, reordered native inventory, non-UTF-8 path
  bytes, disk/sequence mismatch, missing/extra mounts, wrong/swapped paths,
  duplicate device/ID/path/object entries, aliases, and protected/source/stale
  metadata. No host block descriptor or mount is opened.
- **44 native guest cases** per build (31 existing plus 13 caller-home cases),
  on kernel 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts under TCG. Real files-only NSS handles account
  resolution, invalid/absent UID and malformed/missing/file homes, cancellation,
  and buffer growth past 16 KiB. Native checks cover target-backed/unresolved
  homes, invalid/wrong-type descriptors and symlink retargeting while an original
  descriptor is retained. A misleading HOME does not change the selected home.
  Refusals clear results and make zero unmount calls. An independent tmpfs home
  and source coexist with successful two-volume unmount; both resulting FAT16
  volumes pass independent host fsck. Existing namespace/child inheritance,
  source/system/holder/swap/busy/cancellation cases all pass unchanged.

The first two guest runs exposed a fixture ordering error: the independent-home
test ran before its tmpfs mount existed, and the native check correctly refused
the unresolved rootfs. Moving that test after tmpfs setup fixed the fixture; no
production check was weakened. Failed-run logs and disk/image checksums remain,
but their disks and guest trees were removed. Final successful guest evidence is
in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp17b4-native-qualified/` and
`cp17b4-native-sanitizers-qualified/`; their large artifacts were also removed.

Normal and sanitizer full builds pass with default Ninja parallelism and VM test
flags restored OFF. The host sanitizer test ran outside the sandbox for final
LeakSanitizer inspection. No sanitizer diagnostics, host USB/mount changes or
Windows customization qualification. No extra full creation/boot or GUI suite
was needed: new checks remain isolated and the original source logic is covered
by the native regression suite. Compact `cp17b4-*` evidence includes baseline,
scoped patch/hashes, build logs and detailed host results. Changes remain local
and uncommitted. Next is CP17b5 complete preparation-helper integration before
Qt exposes mounted creation; mounted DD remains a separate required integration.


## CP17b5 — preparation-helper unmount integration (2026-09-25)

The preparation target now uses fresh UDisks eligibility, authenticated caller
home retention, original source checks and a validated read-only disk descriptor
to qualify mounted acquisition. It matches the native inventory before unmount,
uses the existing bounded native operation, and reports the actual unmount count
even on failure/cancellation. After unmount, a five-second metadata polling
deadline allows UDisks notifications to settle; each D-Bus call retains its own
existing timeout and can outlast the polling deadline. Source/disk identity and
service state are rechecked before exclusive acquisition, worker mount isolation
and any preparation writes. No unmount retry, force/lazy detach or remount.
The retained home closes with the target during job cleanup.

The root worker supplies the already authenticated UID and retained source to
the existing target object. CMake links its existing source-validation library;
no new protocol, privilege mechanism, Windows code or GUI control. The original
unmounted path retains its source support without the new mounted-layout/home
restrictions. Qt still refuses mounted targets, and DD remains unchanged.

  Independent host readback, partition-table checks, filesystem geometry and

- **Five production Syslinux jobs** per build retain missing/incompatible input,
