## CP17b7a — native mounted DD operation (2026-09-26)

**Scope:** `WriteRawDevice` retains and checks a caller-owned source, reuses raw
eligibility from `RawWritePlan`, acquires the existing preparation target in
acquisition-only `Table::Raw` mode, calls the unchanged raw writer, and rechecks
the target before returning. It closes the source, target and caller-home
references before return. No new copy loop, formatter, installer, authorization
or GUI behavior. Native root execution is explicit; the caller must supply an
authenticated non-root UID and confirmed identities. Only 512-byte target sectors
are qualified for this new operation; existing unmounted DD support is unchanged.

**Functional qualification:** `mbr.py --mounted-raw` runs the existing five
Syslinux helper cases to create a bootable initial disk, then 14 native DD jobs
on its mounted FAT32 partition. The raw source is a caller-owned 64-MiB copy of
the disk on independent tmpfs. Cases: changed source, wrong source owner, missing
boot marker, WIM signature, partial sector, oversize, wrong disk sequence, actual
busy mount, cancellation before work, after unmount and after 1 MiB copied,
injected fsync failure, injected readback mismatch, and complete success.

Both normal and ASan/UBSan/leak-detection guests pass all 14 cases. Refusals
compare whole-disk hashes and make no writes; cancellation after unmount also
preserves the disk. Every raw progress callback checks the retained exclusive
claim. Copy cancellation flushes its 1 MiB; flush failure reports EIO and retains
`sync_error`; readback corruption reports EBADMSG after verifying 63 MiB. Success
copies/verifies all 64 MiB and independently matches the original disk hash.
Every case releases descriptors and allows a fresh exclusive claim. Independent
MBR/FAT/file readback, fsck and BIOS boot pass on the final raw-written disk.

## CP17b7b — mounted DD helper/client operation (2026-09-26)

**Scope:** add `raw-write-device-v1` to the existing helper and process client.
The nine-field request carries device/source identities without formatting,
filesystem or customization options. DD remains device-only. Existing polkit
policy, fixed executable/arguments and one-request pipe lifecycle are reused.
The helper calls `WriteRawDevice`, without adding a formatter or copy loop.

Raw copy/sync/verify byte progress has distinct frames because native raw phase
IDs overlap with ISO operation IDs. Result frames preserve the raw phase,
written/verified counters, flush error and started/possibly-written state. The
client rejects skipped phases, backward/oversized/changing counters, mixed ISO
frames, incomplete readback and success before clean helper exit. A worker that
exits without reporting counters must retain possible media changes, including
when cancellation also occurred; zero counters alone cannot prove no writes.
The server keeps that conservative state, and the raw result transports it.

**Host tests:** the new protocol fixture redirects only its own QProcess launch
to an ordinary Python child; production launch paths are unchanged. It exercises
request schema/required keys, success, refusal, unknown write state, cancellation,
destruction, denied/dismissed authorization, flush failure, backward/changing/
oversized progress, missing/duplicate sync, premature verification, ISO frames,
false unchanged-media claims, short counters, wrong phase, absent/extra results
and wrong exit status. Successful results are held before child exit to prove
completion waits. Every case permits one launch only.

Normal and ASan/UBSan/leak-detection runs pass **26 raw protocol cases**, **55
preparation process cases**, **352 Widgets cases with 2 existing optional skips**,
and the actual ordinary-file preparation helper suite (GPT/FAT32 readback,
request rejection, EOF cancellation, child reaping, flush failure and recovery).
The optional skips are real Windows/Alpine ISO selection with no corresponding
environment variables supplied. These add no Windows customization qualification.
The broad host suite ran first; focused protocol/preparation suites were repeated
after adding the possible-write-state field. A final server fallback adjustment
preserves possible writes even when cancellation coincides with a missing worker
result; focused protocol/actual-helper regressions cover the final build.

**Functional tests:** `mbr.py --mounted-raw-helper` first runs the five existing
Syslinux helper jobs, then four mounted DD jobs through `PrepareImageProcess`,
a guest-only pkexec stand-in and the production helper. The existing FAT32
partition is mounted, while a caller-owned 64-MiB raw source and caller home live
on independent tmpfs. Results in both normal and sanitizer guests:

- Changed source: ESTALE, no unmount or writes.
- Actual busy mount: EBUSY, no unmount or writes.
- EOF cancellation after native unmount: ECANCELED, no writes.
- Successful mounted DD: all 64 MiB written and verified, source/disk equality.

Each job counts one authorization launcher, simulates delayed UDisks mount
notifications, holds launcher exit after the helper result, and checks descriptor,
child and exclusive-claim cleanup. The final disk passes independent MBR/FAT/file
readback, fsck and BIOS boot. This is simulated root-helper qualification with a
private D-Bus fixture, not physical USB, desktop automount or real polkit prompts.
Initial guests passed; both were repeated with the final seven-field raw result.
The later server fallback ordering change affects missing results on cancellation;
the successful guest workflows retain the same behavior. No new native unmount
or copy logic is introduced, so CP17b7a's native failure matrix was not repeated.

```sh
  --kernel 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts --accel tcg --mounted-raw-helper \
```

## CP17c — existing-multiple-partitions confirmation (2026-09-26)

**Windows reference:** `src/rufus.c` shows MSG094/MSG093 immediately after the
ordinary erase confirmation when `SelectedDrive.nPartitions > 1`. The count in
`GetDrivePartitionData` (`src/drive.c`) includes MBR extended containers but
excludes unused entries, Rufus type 0xea, recognized type 0xef Rufus FAT boot
partitions, GPT EFI/MSR, and GPT partitions named exactly UEFI:NTFS. The default
IDNO button in `IDD_NOTIFICATION` (`src/rufus.rc`) becomes Cancel for MB_OKCANCEL.

Qt shares one additional warning across unmounted DD, mounted DD, ISO,
non-bootable partitioned formatting and SFD. It follows the ordinary confirmation,
defaults to Cancel, and authorizes only after acceptance. Device preflight returns
the fresh count rather than relying on discovery-time content metadata. If a
previously single-partition target becomes multi-partitioned at the next check,
creation stops before authorization and asks the user to start again. The raw
post-authorization check also enforces this condition. No helper schema or native
write operation changed.

Linux obtains partition types/names and FAT labels through UDisks. When MBR EFI
filesystem/label metadata cannot establish a Rufus boot partition, it counts the
partition conservatively. This can add a warning but avoids a privileged raw read
before confirmation. The dialog retains the original text, substituting Linux
for Windows. Both differences are recorded in the support guide and plan.

format paths. They assert no launch/open/write before both confirmations and at
most one authorization after acceptance. Existing single-layout and empty-device
workflows remain covered by the full regression suite.

to `selectMounts`' existing accepted filesystem list. It retains the direct
kernel identity requirement, source/home/system protections, alias/nesting
refusals, stale-mount checks, normal unmount flags and exclusive acquisition.
No new mapping layer, daemon lookup, public API, helper route or Windows code.
Anonymous FUSE and source-name-only backing are not accepted. See CP17e1 in the
port plan for the pinned kernel source references and remaining scope.

- Full normal Linux build and three existing regression suites:

  source-only identity refusal still pass. Eighteen real NTFS cases add nine for

  mount, system alias, stale plan, cancellation and successful unmount/readback.

  exit. Remounting verifies the 4096-byte marker written before unmount; a final

  zero fixes in both runs; `fsck.fat -n` checks the second partition. Recipes

  `2026.7.7-1.1` x86_64_v3 pair, unpacked only into each guest. libfuse2, mkntfs,
  libmount and package hashes are recorded. No host driver installation,

## CP17e2 — complete helper jobs from mounted NTFS-3G (2026-09-27)

Extended the existing MBR/helper guest; no production or Windows source changes.
The recipe unpacks the same matching NTFS-3G/library packages only inside its
disposable guest and loads the real FUSE module. It runs the actual Qt helper
client, production helper and native block/mount APIs against controlled UDisks
metadata. A guest-only pkexec stand-in counts launches and holds launcher exit
after the helper result to check completion ordering.

Fourteen new jobs cover seven cases for each of `ntfs-3g` and `lowntfs-3g`:

- Changed source (`ESTALE`), a retained busy directory (`EBUSY`), caller home on
  the target (`EBUSY`) and mismatched UDisks mount path (`ESTALE`) refuse without
  unmounting or writing. Whole-disk hashes remain equal.
- EOF cancellation after native unmount, while UDisks still reports the mount,
  returns `ECANCELED` before writes, with the whole disk unchanged.
- A read/write NTFS mount is replaced by a non-bootable MBR/FAT32 volume through
  the existing formatter job, with direct FAT32 identification readback.
- Another read/write NTFS mount is replaced by the complete generated bootable
  image through DD. All source bytes are written and verified; the whole-disk
  hash equals the retained source. Both successful jobs require final sync,
  cleanup and helper/launcher exit before client completion.

Every new job has exactly one launcher, no UDisks authorization/unmount call,
released exclusive claims, and no leaked descriptors or descendants. Test-owned
desktop NTFS daemons exit normally after unmount. They are not adopted or killed
by the creation helper. Mountinfo, stat and statfs establish genuine `fuseblk`
and the partition's kernel dev_t.

The first run caught `EBUSY` on the read/write format case while the test polled
the FUSE path with `stat()`. Such path walks can themselves keep an unmount busy.
The fixture now observes `/proc/thread-self/mountinfo` during the job, without
walking that path. Initial stat/statfs identity checks still run before creation.
The normal rerun passes unchanged production code; no retry, forced unmount or
relaxed protection was added to the product. The failed run's compact log remains.

The first sanitizer guest reached the final DD job without sanitizer diagnostics
but exceeded the recipe's old 180-second outer deadline. This mode adds 14 jobs
to the existing ten, so its outer deadline is now 300 seconds. Per-job deadlines
and assertions remain unchanged; the timeout log is retained with the evidence.

## CP18a — standalone GPT/NTFS helper completion (2026-09-27)

Windows reference: `src/rufus.c:SetBootOptions` exposes UEFI:NTFS in advanced
mode; `SetPartitionSchemeAndTargetSystem` permits MBR/GPT and UEFI, preferring
GPT when no previous selection applies. Shared `GetAllowedFileSystems` permits
NTFS/exFAT and `GetExtraPartitions` requests the embedded UEFI:NTFS partition.
`src/drive.c:CreatePartition` writes that payload; `src/format.c:FormatThread`
does not extract an ISO for this boot choice. The port plan records these limits.

The Linux helper already accepts `prepare-ntfs-device-v1` without a source and
performs the GPT, native NTFS format and embedded payload copy/readback. This
change runs its existing `finalizeDevice` operation afterward, and the client
expects the additional finalizing phase for source-free NTFS. ISO-backed jobs
retain their existing extraction/finalization path. No new request fields,
operation type, backend, resource, layout implementation or Windows edits.

The existing `mbr.py --uefi-ntfs-helper` fixture runs the 12 non-bootable NTFS
regressions, then four source-free bootable jobs. The first three use the existing
test-only format probe, extended to leave boot-payload fsync alone so faults
occur at finalization. The last uses the production helper:

- Final disk sync failure yields `EIO`, preserves the error in `syncError` and
  ends FAILED, despite a complete boot-payload copy/readback.
- EOF cancellation during final sync flushes before exit and ends CANCELLED.
- An interrupted final sync is retried successfully.
- Ordinary creation ends COMPLETE only after checking, partitioning, formatting,
  bootloader, finalizing and helper/launcher exit.

All four check one guest authorization launcher, retained/released disk claims,
zero copied ISO bytes, full byte-for-byte payload readback, no temporary mounts,
and no leaked descriptors or descendants. The client remains active while the
launcher deliberately lingers after the helper result. Both output partitions
are independently checked after shutdown: GPT header/table copies, extents,
names/attributes/CRCs; NTFS boot copies, label, cluster size, clean volume flags
and `ntfsck -n`; and exact equality with `res/uefi/uefi-ntfs.img`.

Normal build and normal guest pass all 16 jobs. Five existing CTest suites pass:
`rufus_prepare_process` (60 Qt cases), `rufus_raw_helper_process` (27),
`rufus_format_options` (41), `rufus_prepare_helper` and `rufus_uefi_ntfs`.
The first full build hit a GCC 16 internal compiler error in Qt's qtextstream.h
while compiling the unrelated Windows setup test. Retrying completed the full
build without a workaround or parallelism cap.

in approximately 51 and 87 seconds under TCG. The final production helper hashes

## CP18c — standalone MBR UEFI:NTFS layout/payload (2026-09-28)

This checkpoint qualifies the native file operations before CP18d connects the
complete device/helper job. Windows reference: `drive.c:CreatePartition` makes
active `0x07` NTFS/exFAT data and an inactive `0xEF` trailing partition; MBR tail
placement uses the full disk end. `format.c:WriteMBR` clears boot code and the
disk signature for forced UEFI without clearing the main partition's active
byte. The Linux implementation reuses shared Rufus placement and the existing
libfdisk creator/checker. Metadata preparation clears both partition prefixes;
MBR and GPT share the existing retained-source, bounded payload writer and
table revalidation. Existing helper/Qt callers explicitly pass no MBR payload.
There are 86 net added production lines, with no Windows source edits.

Validation passed:

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build with default parallelism.
- Five new suites: 78 layout/create/readback calls and 29 preparation calls for
  each of NTFS and exFAT, plus 56 payload-copy cases across both filesystems.
  The same five suites pass under ASan/UBSan with leak detection enabled.

  flags, offsets, lengths, zero boot code/signature and unused entries. Exact
  file comparisons cover clearing boundaries and preservation outside the

  readback does not repair damaged tables. Descriptor flags/positions and counts

- Eighteen existing native suites pass: raw writing, GPT payload/layout, shared
  placement, format options, all six existing MBR layout/preparation pairs and
  SFD preparation/formatting. Three helper suites also pass: prepare process
  (62 Qt cases), FAT32 helper and FAT16 helper. Total: 26 normal suites.
- Eight sanitizer suites pass: the five new ones plus existing GPT payload,
  Syslinux MBR preparation and SFD preparation/formatting, with no diagnostics.

`fat32.c` and `partition_info.c` with test-only `read_data`, `contains_data` and
`write_data` functions over real, bounded FILE memory streams. It does not use
Windows FAKE_FD/HANDLE emulation, the Windows I/O module, a formatter or any
physical/virtual disk. The GUI/helper creation routes remain unchanged.

FAT16/FAT32 × keep-label configurations and failure at each of 16 write positions.
Successful cases preserve BPB fields except the original explicit label/drive-ID
changes, retain FSInfo allocation counters, contain the KERNEL.SYS filename and
expected boot signatures, and preserve all surrounding guard bytes. Every
injected write failure propagates and stops subsequent calls. This validates
the reused payload-writing functions, not the Windows `WritePBR` wrapper or a
complete Linux boot installation.

writer. It initially assumed the first 496 bytes of FAT32 FSInfo were preserved;

The initial output remains with the evidence to explain the correction.

to active `src/rufus.rc` entries and their existing files, totaling **400,604
bytes**. The kernel byte at `0x0d` is `0x01`, matching its bundled FORCELBA

## CP19b — native FreeDOS boot records on formatted files (2026-09-28)

Added `rufus_freedos_boot`, a small C adapter around the unchanged ms-sys FAT16,
FAT32 and physical-drive-ID routines. It reuses native formatter request/geometry
validation and accepts only retained writable regular files. FAT32 reserved
coverage, FSInfo/backup locations and backup BPB/signature are checked before
either record is written. Memory streams reserve a spare NUL byte and reject
out-of-range accesses; target I/O uses fixed prefixes and preserves fd position.
Partial changes are flushed after write failure/cancellation, with `sync_error`
retained separately. Success includes exact prefix readback and FAT validation.

`rufus_freedos_boot` passes **100 install/refusal/fault cases**, plus explicit
memory-overflow/end-bound guards and character-device rejection. Four formatted
fixtures cover FAT16/FAT32, selected/empty directory labels, 512/1024-byte
clusters and zero/nonzero partition offsets. Their largest sparse capacity is
128 MiB. Expected code comes from the original payload arrays, with independent
write offsets; every other prefix byte and the digest of all bytes outside the
prefix window must remain unchanged. The intervening FAT32 sectors are included
in this byte comparison. Root-directory and mtools readback confirm the volume
label is preserved despite the boot sector's original `NO NAME` replacement.
Distinct primary/backup FSInfo allocation hints also survive unchanged.

Fault coverage includes every original staged write (4 FAT16, 10 across both
FAT32 copies), primary/backup reads and writes, short I/O, EINTR retries, EOF,
readback corruption in either copy, partial writes, flush failure and combined
write/flush failure. Cancellation is checked before work, after staging, after
a partial write/primary record and after flush. Invalid options, extents,
descriptor flags, filesystem markers, BPB fields and backup geometry/signature
are rejected before target writes. File growth during flush fails final size
validation. Each invocation checks descriptor count, flags and position; no
mounts, child helpers or physical block devices are used by the adapter.

## CP19c1 — shared DOS locale policy/content (2026-09-28)

Extracted the original DOS tables, driver/code-page fallback policy and
CONFIG.SYS/AUTOEXEC.BAT content into `src/dos_locale_policy.c/.h`. The original
Windows wrapper calls the shared selector/writers and retains its keyboard and
OEM-code-page query bodies byte-for-byte. Host queries, path handling, file
opening/closing and logs stay in that wrapper. Linux CMake compiles the same
shared C module, without Qt or a platform callback interface.

The writers emit explicit CRLF on binary FILE streams, including the original
31-byte OEM `0xcd` border, menu default/timeout and DOS path separators. Windows
opens them in binary mode to avoid double CR translation. Both the FreeDOS and
MS-DOS branches are shared; the unknown-code-page fallback to driver-default
850 remains distinct from upgrading a supported requested 850 to 858.

`dos_locale_reference.c` freezes the pre-extraction tables and SetDOSLocale
writer, with its copyright intact. Test-only host/CRT shims supply explicit DOS
keyboard/code-page values; they do not implement Windows host discovery. The
reference uses release-mode assertions and native LF output, translated to
CRLF in the comparison to account for the original Windows text-mode CRT.
Only defined original output is compared; missing-description behavior and
invalid arguments have separate fixed expectations.

`rufus_dos_locale` passes **468 byte comparisons**, plus explicit driver/fallback
and missing-label cases, null-argument/static-string-lifetime checks, immediate
stream errors and buffered failures at close. The input domain comes from the
frozen original tables, not the new implementation. Tests independently check
US/437 CONFIG omission, the five-second default, original MS/FreeDOS driver
order, selected-vs-fallback 850/858 behavior, CRLF, OEM border and existence of
every referenced FreeDOS keyboard/EGA resource. `/dev/full` simulates failed
writes without touching a disk; a CONFIG failure prevents AUTOEXEC creation.

Four byte-comparison cases intentionally change the original `ega12` command
to `ega12.cpx` (CP 30003, 30029, 30030, 58335), matching the bundled payload.
Driver-supported keyboard IDs missing a description now display the canonical
ID; unknown code-page descriptions are `Unknown`. This prevents assertions/NULL
formatting while leaving driver/code-page fallback selection intact. The Windows

## CP19c2 — shared FreeDOS payloads and kernel FAT attributes (2026-09-28)

Added one ordered manifest for all 27 bundled files, their Windows resource IDs,
root/LOCALE destinations and the original five copy milestones. `ExtractFreeDOS`
uses that manifest for its existing Windows I/O; Linux CMake embeds the same
resource files, and `CopyFreeDosFiles` uses the common descriptor table. Tests
compare the manifest with independent original filename/order/milestone
expectations and active `rufus.rc` entries. The kernel's FORCELBA byte remains
unchanged and no payload binary is copied into a new source location.

The native component accepts an empty, exclusively borrowed directory on kernel
FAT. It uses exclusive creation beneath retained directory descriptors, writes
and verifies all bytes after file sync, and sets/verifies hidden/system bits on
COMMAND.COM and KERNEL.SYS through actual Linux FAT attribute ioctls. Other bits
are preserved. It flushes files and both directories on errors/cancellation,
retains a separate sync error, and leaves partial output marked incomplete.
No mount, privilege request, boot record or locale/startup file is produced by
this component. The preceding sixth progress slot belongs to its future caller.

`CheckEmptyTargetDirectory` is the existing ISO extractor guard moved unchanged
to `target_io` (only linkage/name changed); its ISO caller now uses that shared
implementation. The existing extractor's 229 functional cases cover the move.
Normal and ASan/UBSan/leak tests pass **31 FreeDOS copy cases**, including short
I/O, EINTR, full/zero/partial writes, readback failure/corruption, attribute
get/set/mismatch failures, close failures, first/second/final-directory sync
failures, combined copy/sync errors, cancellation and nonempty/linked/hidden
entries. Borrowed fd position/flags and descriptor counts remain intact. These
component tests simulate FAT ioctls; native qualification below uses the kernel.

The small guest recipe runs the same adapter with real FAT ioctls on newly
formatted 16 MiB FAT16 and 64 MiB FAT32 USB volumes. It uses no host block-device
attachment, networking or host mount/privilege request. Both native runs report
27 files, 400,604 bytes, two attribute sets, 29 successful file/directory syncs,
and milestones after files 5, 11, 17, 23 and 27. After successful private unmount
and guest exit, host-side `mtype` compares every byte with the original resource,
`mattrib` confirms H/S only on the two root files, and `fsck.fat -n` passes both
volumes. This qualifies payload copying/attributes on kernel FAT, not a FreeDOS
boot or the eventual helper/Qt creation route.

It creates CONFIG before AUTOEXEC and only AUTOEXEC for US/437. Startup files
have ordinary attributes and add no progress slots. The shared content and
original Windows code are unchanged. Neither the helper nor GUI enables FreeDOS.

`rufus_freedos_startup` has **64 cases** on disposable directories:

  content oracle, including CRLF/OEM bytes, requested 850 upgrading to 858,

  fallbacks and CP19c1's documented EGA12 filename correction.

  memory-stream close errors, short and interrupted I/O, zero/partial/failed
  writes, readback EOF/errors/mismatch, close failure, each file/root sync

  and dangling links, and hard links for either startup name under both menu and
  US/437 selections. Either existing name refuses the operation before writing;
  an entry appearing after preflight is refused by exclusive creation. Outside

- Two combined workflows copy all 27 payloads and then startup files, compare

  the five original payload-copy milestones. No startup progress is added.

All tests check retained descriptors/positions, no descriptor leak, operation

FAT type is supplied by the existing test shim here; CP19c2's real FAT16/FAT32

not new kernel-FAT tests, helper authorization tests or FreeDOS boot qualification.
No physical USB, ISO copy, disk image or Windows customization test is used.

no Windows file changes, and no new creation route is exposed. Existing callers
now spell out their previous bootstrap choice, including the Syslinux-only
installer guard and guest probes.

Eight functional suites reuse the existing disposable-file MBR/clearing tests:
Rufus and Windows 7 × FAT16/FAT32 × create/readback and prepare/readback.
Each bootstrap/filesystem pair has **81 MBR calls and 30 preparation calls**,
for **444 calls across the four pairs**. They check:

- Exact original payload bytes, active/type fields, disk signature, reserved
  bytes, unused entries and sfdisk's independent table verification. The Windows
  7 header's commented disk-signature array is excluded from the payload reader.

  geometry bounds, descriptor position/flags and no changes outside sector zero.

  rejected before preparation clears old metadata, verified by whole-file hashes.
- Replacing stale GPT metadata within existing clear ranges; partial writes,
  interrupted/short I/O, sync/read failures, cancellation and a replaced pathname.

## CP19d2b — complete FreeDOS device-helper path (2026-09-29)

The temporary FreeDOS rejection is replaced by the assembled production route.
It reuses native MBR preparation/formatter handoff, original ms-sys boot records,
private kernel FAT mounts, original payload resources and shared DOS startup
writers. Both ISO extraction and FreeDOS copying use the same finalization
operation, which preserves an earlier file-sync error. The manual DOS settings
stay frozen in the existing one-helper request. No Windows code changes occur
in this checkpoint.

**Native qualification:** four 64-MiB virtual USB variants pass: FAT16/FAT32 ×
Rufus/Windows 7 MBR. Each runs six jobs, for **24 scenarios**:

- Wrong disk sequence is refused before writes; whole-disk hashes stay equal.
- Mount failure reports EIO and cleans up without copying.
- EOF cancellation while writing COMMAND.COM reports ECANCELED, flushes partial
  output, unmounts and releases the disk; one copy step has been reported.
- Final syncfs failure reports EIO with `syncError=EIO`, even after all six copy
  steps. Successful copying cannot hide a failed flush.
- Unmount failure reports EBUSY with `cleanupError=EBUSY`. The helper does not
  lazily detach; namespace exit releases the mount. The guest confirms device
  availability and then removes the one empty failed-mount directory.
- Success has all seven phases, exactly six discrete copy steps, no continuous
  copy-count frames, nonzero payload/startup counts, and clean sync/cleanup.
  The real process client waits through the test launcher's delayed exit.

All cases use one launcher call per job and check device claims, mountpoints,
process descriptors and remaining children. The guest uses Linux
6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts, native mkfs.fat 4.2 and kernel vfat, QEMU TCG and a private
D-Bus UDisks fixture. The authorization launcher is a guest-only stand-in; this
establishes one-helper ownership, not an additional desktop polkit prompt test.
No host block devices, host mounts, KVM setup or Windows customization tests are
involved.

Independent host readback checks original MBR bytes, active partition/type/
extents, original PBR bytes and FAT32 backup equality; all 27 bundled resources
and their hidden/system attributes; exact startup bytes against the frozen
Windows DOS writer oracle; and filesystem consistency with read-only fsck.
Rufus-MBR runs select RO/852 (401,073 copied bytes including CONFIG/AUTOEXEC);
Windows-7-MBR runs select US/437 and assert CONFIG.SYS is absent. The file inventory
has no extra payloads. The only accepted fsck diagnostic is the original writer's
NO NAME BPB versus preserved RUFUS TEST directory label, with exact expected
warning text; all other repairs/errors fail the check.

**Build and component checks:** the full normal Debug build passes, with Ninja's
default parallelism. Eighteen selected normal suites pass: eight preparation/
FreeDOS component and process suites, eight Rufus/Windows 7 FAT16/FAT32 MBR suites,
original boot-record tests and raw-helper process regressions. Six suites pass
ASan/UBSan with leak detection: boot records on formatted files (100 cases),
FreeDOS requests, format options, preparation process and FAT16/FAT32 helper
regressions. Sanitizers run outside the ptrace sandbox. The native VM runs use
the normal build; they are not sanitizer or firmware-boot runs.

## CP19d2c — helper-created FreeDOS media boots under BIOS (2026-09-29)

Two representative end-to-end configurations pass:

| Filesystem / MBR | Explicit startup | BIOS result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FAT32 / original Rufus | RO/852 | Original language menu reaches the selected keyboard driver, then C:\>; VER and ECHO execute. |
| FAT16 / original Windows 7 | US/437 | Startup confirms US-English/437 with no CONFIG.SYS, then C:\>; VER and ECHO execute. |

Each final recipe run first passes CP19d2b's six real helper/process cases, then
independently verifies the completed media and boots it. The 64-MiB virtual USB
is the only guest disk. The BIOS stage has **no directly supplied kernel/initrd,
added DOS program or edited startup file**. A separate Linux creation guest runs
the same production helper, native FAT formatter and controlled UDisks metadata
as before; its test-only authorization launcher remains one launch per job.
No host block device, mount or real privilege prompt is involved.

`linux/tests/vm/freedos_boot.py` reuses the existing QMP keyboard/VGA helpers.
It waits for the FreeCOM prompt and validates the expected startup choice. It
then types VER and requires the command, a following FreeCOM version response
and a new prompt in order, preventing the startup banner from satisfying the
command check. ECHO must produce `RUFUSDOSOK` as its own output line, distinct
from the typed command. QEMU quits cleanly only after confirmation. Timeouts and
failures capture available evidence, terminate/wait for QEMU and let the outer
recipe remove the guest disks/trees. The boot uses snapshot mode and checks the
full backing-image SHA-256 afterward.

The observed environment is QEMU 11.1.1 with TCG and SeaBIOS identifying itself
as Arch Linux 1.17.0-2-2. The BIOS payload hash is
`b7dea28b1ab93d43f427232f5f6ab07c828fd97765d9b1daaf1b1712b39946e2`.
The bundled shell reports FreeCOM 0.86 / WATCOMC / XMS_Swap. RO startup reports
KEYBRD2.SYS:RO [852]; US startup reports US-English keyboard/codepage [437].
The recorded firmware, commands, unchanged disk hashes, VGA text and PNG
screenshots make those observations reviewable.

```sh

  --kernel 6.18.52-1-cachyos-lts --accel tcg --freedos-helper --freedos-boot \
  --fat-bits 16 --freedos-win7 /tmp/rufus-freedos-bios-fat16
```

## CP20a — standalone Syslinux source audit and native probe (2026-09-29)

[The reuse audit](linux-syslinux-standalone.md) traces Windows's advanced v4/v6
choices, FAT/NTFS eligibility, original MBR/loader resources, optional v6 module
download, no-config output and two actual copy updates within a three-slot
allocation. It identifies the existing v6 native installer and checked FAT
adapter as the implementation foundation. v4's matching provider and v6 NTFS
remain required work; upstream extlinux is an NTFS candidate, not yet qualified.

`linux/probes/syslinux/test_standalone.py`. It creates empty 64-MiB MBR/FAT16 and
FAT32 regular files using existing partition/format probes, then invokes the
unchanged native installer. It does not create a fake ISO or pass fabricated
image metadata into the production adapter. Independent checks cover:

- Exactly `ldlinux.sys` and `ldlinux.c32`, no configuration or kernel; native
  loader size (69632 bytes), original companion equality and R/H/S attributes.

  and disk signature, and unchanged bytes outside the chosen partition. The
  known primary/backup boot-code difference is normalized only on a throwaway

- SeaBIOS USB boot to `SYSLINUX 6.04 ... 6.04-pre1`, the expected no-configuration
  warning and `boot:` prompt. QEMU snapshot mode leaves each disk hash unchanged.
- Temporary installer configuration cleanup and removal of all media/temporary
  trees after exporting compact evidence.

The direct evidence run and its registered CTest both pass two BIOS boots, using
QEMU 11.1.1/TCG and SeaBIOS Arch Linux 1.17.0-2-2. The inspected screenshot shows
the expected bare prompt. No operating-system handoff, standalone production
helper route, actual privilege prompt, physical USB or Windows validation is
claimed. No new Windows customization test was run.

The full normal CMake/Ninja build passes with default parallelism. **Seven
selected CTest suites pass**: native selection, FAT16 installer adapter, FAT32
installer adapter, the new standalone probe, packed fields, shared filesystem
policy and shared progress policy. The existing file adapters each exercise
34 cases. Production GUI, helper and native-installer SHA-256 hashes remain
identical to the checkpoint baseline. No production C/C++ source was changed,
so there was no additional sanitizer/GUI qualification for this audit.

Two early probe expectations were corrected before the final runs: mtools groups
attribute flags as `SHR`, and the no-config boot warning is `WARNING: No

## CP20b — explicit standalone v6 in the shared FAT installer adapter

Completed 2026-09-29. The image-only API is renamed to `NativeSyslinuxRequest` /
`InstallNativeSyslinux`. Its default is still `BT_IMAGE`; only explicit
`BT_SYSLINUX_V6` permits a source-free job. That selection uses the qualified
embedded 6.04-pre1 provider and requires every ISO/source field to be null.
Images retain their source/configuration/module eligibility and identity rechecks.
Shared geometry and companion hash checks no longer require an ISO report.

The source-free preflight checks the fresh root using existing libfat sector
access and FAT entries: end marker first, or a volume label and then end marker.
It rejects populated/deleted roots rather than traversing arbitrary directories
or introducing a second filesystem reader. Both modes use the existing target
validation, supervised command runner, exact loader/ADV/VBR reconstruction,
companion/FAT-chain readback, sync and private-directory cleanup. The native
installer, original Rufus algorithms/resources and Windows code are unchanged.
Net production growth is 72 lines including comments; the helper and guest-test
callers only change API names. No helper protocol or Qt selector is enabled.

Validation:

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build with default parallelism passes. The native
  installer SHA-256 matches CP20a; GUI/helper binaries relink against the updated
  adapter. Existing dependency-header warnings remain.
- Nine selected normal suites pass: native selection, both image adapters, both
  standalone adapters, standalone BIOS probe, packed-field checks and the two
  image scan/version suites. The final expanded standalone matrices were rerun
  after adding unlabeled/deleted-file cases. There are **43 image + 46 standalone
  cases per FAT variant**, or **178 adapter cases** in total.
- Unsupported versions/selections/geometry, wrong source mode and each individual
  missing/extra source field fail before command launch. Prelaunch failures check
  whole-target SHA-256 equality. Existing boot files, configuration, directories,
  long filenames and deleted-file entries are rejected for standalone; labeled
  and unlabeled fresh roots succeed. FAT16 also covers 64-KiB clusters.
- The common fault matrix exercises cancellation before/during/after the command,
  descriptor access/flags/position, subreaper ownership, missing/failing/no-op
  tools, target changes, loader/VBR/BPB/backup corruption, damaged FAT chains,
  wrong companion bytes, read/sync failures and failed private-dir cleanup.
  Every case checks child reaping, descriptor counts and temporary-directory
  cleanup. Image jobs still check source identity/content and immutable analysis.
- The unchanged source probe passes **39 layouts, eight faults, one symlink and
  two UDF views**. This retains the unknown-version/module compatibility boundary
  and source-specific config/backup rules after separating common checks.
- Six ASan/UBSan suites with leak detection pass, including all 178 adapter cases,
  native selection and packed fields. Instrumented adapters call the normal
  pinned native installer/mtools; the upstream installer itself is not claimed
  to be sanitizer-qualified. Tests run outside the ptrace sandbox for LeakSanitizer.
- The checked standalone adapter creates the two-file FAT16/FAT32 output, then
  independent readback checks the module, loader size/attributes, filesystem,
  BPB/backup, original MBR and outside-volume bytes. QEMU/SeaBIOS snapshot USB
  boots reach `WARNING: No configuration file found` and `boot:` without a source
  ISO, configuration, kernel or OS. A separate evidence run retains screenshots,
  text, firmware identities and adapter results; the FAT32 screenshot was inspected.
  Backing hashes are unchanged after boot; all media and copied firmware are removed.

During test development, the new no-label probe initially assigned to a C array;
that test-only compile error was corrected. One manual source-probe invocation
incorrectly passed bsdtar for its UDF formatter; the final run uses the configured
private mkisofs. Initial and final logs are retained. Neither issue required a

lines pass the whitespace check.

Reproduction (reuse the configured dependency paths):

```sh

ctest --test-dir /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --output-on-failure \
  -R '^(rufus_syslinux_native_selection|rufus_syslinux_fat(16|32)(_standalone)?_install|rufus_syslinux_standalone_probe|rufus_syslinux_packed_fields|rufus_syslinux_scan_image|rufus_syslinux_image)$'

ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 \

python3 linux/probes/syslinux/test_standalone.py \
  /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build/syslinux/rufus-syslinux \
```

Completed 2026-09-29. The advanced Boot selection now offers **Syslinux 6.04**,
matching Windows's major/minor display while keeping the qualified 6.04-pre1
provider. The existing selection/controller/format path supplies MBR/BIOS,
FAT16/FAT32 eligibility, existing/manual filesystem preferences and the original

unplugging. Production growth is 31 net lines including comments in five files.

Validation and boundaries:

- The full normal CMake/Ninja build passes with default parallelism. New code
  introduces no compiler warnings; existing bundled libcdio/wimlib declarations
  still produce their existing pedantic warnings.
- Ten normal CTest suites pass: format options, prepare process, FreeDOS and
  Syslinux requests, FAT16/FAT32 helpers, image-mode dialog, main window, scaled
  main window, and the full Widgets write suite. The eight Qt suites total 788
  passing results. The full write suite has 516 passes and two skips for optional
  real Windows/Alpine ISO inputs; these are read-only image selection checks.
- The corresponding eight Qt suites also pass ASan/UBSan/leak checks: seven
  CTest suites plus the full Widgets executable under the extended test limit.
  That full run reports 516 passes, zero failures, the same two optional-input
  skips and a clean exit/leak check. The final sanitized executable also includes
  the screenshot layout-event flush. Instrumented native GUI/controller libraries
  are tested; the protocol fixture does not run a native installer.
- Focused coverage passes 28 functional cases (plus test setup/teardown): source
  isolation and retained DD/Linux/Windows selection for both bare BIOS loaders,
  capacity restrictions, FAT16/FAT32/large FAT32 success, missing/disappearing
  formatter/native tools, confirmation cancellation, unplugging, helper refusal,
  sync/cleanup/layout/phase errors and cancellation during formatting,
  installation/copy/finalization. Reuses the existing private D-Bus, device
  metadata and protocol child; it never opens a real device or runs the native
  installer. Invalid preparation launches zero helpers; creation launches one.
- Successful cases freeze the request, check the original Syslinux MBR choice,
  receive zero extraction bytes, verify both discrete progress positions, and
  hold the helper alive after its result to prove READY/notification cannot
  happen early. Completion then shows full READY and stays successful on unplug.
- Progress assertions use independent Windows values: ordinary FAT copy steps
  46810/51491, first finalization 60853; large FAT32 steps 62913/63568,
  first finalization 64879, on Rufus's 65535-unit scale. Final exit reaches 65535.
- Normal and 2× scaled selection/installation/READY screenshots are retained.
  The test lets Qt process the pending layout update after hiding Windows image
  options before capturing selection. Native device/install/BIOS qualification
  remains CP20c's unchanged helper/installer evidence; this checkpoint does not
  repeat VM boots, real desktop authorization or physical USB testing.

Reproduction (private D-Bus needs socket permissions; LeakSanitizer cannot run
under the ptrace sandbox):

```sh
cmake --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build
ctest --test-dir /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --output-on-failure \
  -R '^rufus_(raw_write_widgets|window|window_scaled|format_options|syslinux_request|freedos_request|prepare_process|prepare_helper|prepare_fat16_helper|image_mode_dialog)$'
cmake --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-sanitizers --target test_raw_write_widgets \
  test_rufus_window test_format_options test_syslinux_request test_freedos_request \
  test_prepare_image_process test_image_mode_dialog
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 \
ctest --test-dir /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-sanitizers --output-on-failure \
  -R '^rufus_(window|window_scaled|format_options|syslinux_request|freedos_request|prepare_process|image_mode_dialog)$'
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 360s \
  /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-sanitizers/test_raw_write_widgets
```

The first focused invocation could not create its private D-Bus socket inside the
sandbox and failed during fixture setup; it passed outside the sandbox. An initial
sanitizer selection included the unbuilt image-mode-dialog executable; that target
was built separately. The full sanitizer Widgets run reached the existing
180-second CTest timeout late in the suite without reporting a sanitizer error;
the bounded standalone rerun allows 360 seconds so it can finish its leak check.
Its interrupted 21-MB temporary directory was verified and removed, and no test
D-Bus/helper processes remained. Initial logs are retained rather than hidden.
No additional Windows customization qualification was run. Temporary file fixtures
remove themselves; no large disk, ISO tree, guest root or firmware copy was made.
Parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp20d-*` retains logs, screenshots, baseline/scoped
diff and source/binary hashes. Work remains local and uncommitted.

**Next: CP20e**, verify/build a matching native Syslinux 4.07 provider through
CMake, then extend the existing path only after payload/installer qualification.
Syslinux v6 NTFS remains required; investigate upstream extlinux separately.


## CP20e — native Syslinux 4.07 build, runner and bare BIOS qualification

Completed 2026-09-29. The optional `RUFUS_SYSLINUX4_UPSTREAM` path builds
`rufus-syslinux4` through the same native CMake recipe as v6. It compiles nine
unmodified upstream C files and uses original `bin2c.pl` to embed the v4 loader
and VBR; it needs no v6 companion or separate `syslxrw.c`. Both payloads are
SHA-256 pinned and compared byte for byte with Rufus's `ldlinux_v4` resources.
Generated files and install component are separate, so enabling v4 preserves
the existing v6 binary exactly. No application runtime C/C++ implementation or
Windows source is modified. The application still refuses v4 requests.

The [official archive](https://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/utils/boot/syslinux/4.xx/syslinux-4.07.tar.xz)
SHA-256 is `8e228c34b8a98166a4d42bf0c8ad0ff767ea9ff38dc03b6543248944be6e1887`,
checked against that directory's HTTPS checksum list; its PGP signature was not
authenticated. All 2279 extracted files compare unchanged with the archive after
building. Provenance, payload hashes and source limits are in
[the native build notice](../linux/syslinux/README.md#candidate-syslinux-407-provider--cp20e).

Validation passed:

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build with default parallelism. A separate v4-only
  configuration/build succeeds without the v6 source/target. No upstream Make
  or BIOS recompilation occurs. Original upstream packed-member compiler
  warnings remain visible; `_DEFAULT_SOURCE=1` handles glibc's deprecated
  `_BSD_SOURCE` spelling without patching source.
- Six normal suites: `rufus_syslinux4_command`, `rufus_syslinux4_package`,
  `rufus_syslinux_package`, `rufus_syslinux_standalone_probe`,
  `rufus_syslinux_packed_fields`, and `rufus_syslinux_request`.
  The final v4 package and v6 standalone probes were rerun after adding the
  v4 4096-byte-sector refusal case; both package suites were also rerun after
  adding the non-x86 configure refusal. All pass.
- The existing runner passes 21 process cases (including refusal before
  spawning, failures/signals, orphan writers, cancellation, timeout, unrelated
  children, environment/descriptor constraints and final fsync errors/retry)
  plus three real v4 installer cases. Those native cases cover success,
  retained-descriptor writes after pathname replacement, and cancellation
  inside mcopy. All children are reaped before fsync, descriptors/offset/flags
  are preserved, and no surviving descendants are left. The same 24 cases
  pass ASan/UBSan/leak checks on our runner, using the normal native executable.
- A staged `Syslinux4Runtime` package has exactly the executable, original
  COPYING and build/provenance notice, with 0755/0644 permissions, no symlinks,
  setuid bits or privileged service. Staged bytes match the built executable.
  Altering either copied payload makes CMake fail; original source is untouched.
- Each of FAT16 and FAT32 installs to a disposable 64-MiB whole-disk MBR image,
  using original Rufus MBR/format probes and the existing regular-file runner.
  Independent readback verifies exactly one boot file, its 37888-byte padded
  length and read-only/hidden/system attributes, BPB/backup preservation,
  original active MBR and unchanged prefix/trailing gap. FAT16 fsck is clean;
  FAT32 normalizes the expected primary/backup VBR difference only in a separate
  check copy. No configuration, kernel, companion or OS is created.
- Both build-tree and staged installs boot as snapshot virtual USBs under
  SeaBIOS/TCG to `SYSLINUX 4.07`, its expected `ERROR: No configuration file found`
  and `boot:` prompt. The FAT32 screenshot was inspected. Backing-image SHA-256
  stays unchanged. This is a bare-loader boot, not an OS or physical-firmware
  qualification. The tests use SeaBIOS Arch Linux 1.17.0-2-2, dosfstools 4.2,
  host GCC 16.2.1 and existing mtools. No guest Linux or root access is needed.
- The native v4 installer refuses a valid 4096-byte-sector FAT16 image before
  writing; its full hash remains unchanged. Application geometry must retain
  the existing 512-byte sector and unsigned-32-bit offset guards.

Sanitizer coverage is deliberately stated at the runner boundary: the unmodified
upstream installer retains typed unaligned accesses and exit-time allocations,
as already recorded for v6. 4.07 also has broken non-x86 accessor branches in
`libinstaller/syslxint.h` (invalid pointer arguments and word assembly), found
by source review. CMake now rejects that target architecture; a configure test verifies the
refusal. Those branches require fixes before non-x86-host qualification. No
suppression, fully sanitized upstream claim or new portability claim is made.
The checked adapter's exact patched-loader/VBR comparison, native block devices,
helper protocol/progress and GUI exposure remain later checkpoints. Windows
customizations, real USBs and desktop polkit prompts are not tested here.

Reproduction, using the existing configured builds/dependencies:

```sh
cmake -S linux -B /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build \
  -DRUFUS_SYSLINUX4_UPSTREAM=/path/to/syslinux-4.07
cmake --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build
ctest --test-dir /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build --output-on-failure \
  -R '^rufus_(syslinux4_command|syslinux4_package|syslinux_package|syslinux_standalone_probe|syslinux_packed_fields|syslinux_request)$'
cmake -S linux -B /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-sanitizers \
  -DRUFUS_SYSLINUX4_UPSTREAM=/path/to/syslinux-4.07
cmake --build /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-sanitizers --target syslinux_command_probe
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 \
python3 linux/probes/syslinux/test_command.py \
  /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-sanitizers/syslinux_command_probe \
  /tmp/rufus-linux-qt6-build/syslinux/rufus-syslinux4 /path/to/syslinux-4.07 --major 4
```

LeakSanitizer runs outside the ptrace sandbox. Parent
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp20e-*` retains build/test logs, source/payload/binary
manifests, scoped diff and `cp20e-v4-bios/fat16` / `fat32` screenshots/results.
Tests remove all disposable media, volume copies, staging trees, copied firmware
and temporary build trees. The 4.07 archive (about 4.4 MiB) and source (about
23 MiB) remain as the dependency for subsequent integration and corresponding
source, not disposable test media. Nothing is installed on the host. Changes
remain local and uncommitted.

**Next: CP20f**, reuse the checked adapter for explicit standalone v4 payload
selection and exact readback, with focused failure coverage for both versions.
Keep image inference unchanged; helper/native-device and Qt work follow later.

## CP20i — extlinux on kernel NTFS and NTFS-3G

Completed 2026-09-29. The standalone probe CMake builds eight unchanged upstream
extlinux C files and the existing hash-pinned 6.04-pre1 payloads. Supplying modern
glibc's `sys/sysmacros.h` at compilation resolves the old implicit `major/minor`
declarations; upstream source and the production build remain untouched. New
probe targets disappear with `BUILD_TESTING=OFF` and have no install rules.

The [reproduction recipe](../linux/probes/syslinux/README.md#ntfs-extlinux-investigation--cp20i)
uses two 64-MiB USB disks with 4096-byte clusters, Linux 7.2.7-arch1-1's new
`ntfs` driver and the retained NTFS-3G 2026.7.7 packages inside an offline TCG
guest. Existing MBR/NTFS formatter probes create the data layout; this experiment
alone overlays Rufus's original Syslinux MBR and active bit. Production still
refuses this bootable NTFS combination.

Final observations and checks:

- Both native installer processes succeed using inherited `/proc/self/fd/3`
  partition access. Filesystem magic and mount/partition identity are asserted.
  Competing partition and whole-disk `O_EXCL` opens fail `EBUSY` before and after
  installation. The mount owns the claim, matching the existing helper lifecycle.
- Kernel NTFS maps through FIEMAP. NTFS-3G refuses FIEMAP (`EOPNOTSUPP`) and maps
  through the unchanged FIGETBSZ/FIBMAP fallback. All 136 mapped loader sectors
  match raw partition reads on each driver.
- Both have a 69632-byte loader/ADV with SHA-256
  `52bbc70c76395cd579e73df912d53333aaa9feac7cc4cdd284eb4e8ea12df17e` and the
  pinned 122656-byte companion. After unmount, both remount read-only through
  the kernel NTFS driver with matching loader hashes. Independent 7-Zip reads
  recover the same files from the actual Syslinux volumes.
- MBR, BPB, backup boot sector and bytes outside the partition are preserved.
  Both unchanged disks boot under SeaBIOS to `SYSLINUX 6.04`, the expected missing
  configuration warning and `boot:` prompt. Snapshot boots preserve backing
  hashes; both video-text captures and the kernel-driver screenshot were
  inspected. The fallback screenshot preceded the VGA repaint and is discarded;
  its video-text prompt is retained. This is bare-loader boot,
  not OS handoff or physical-firmware qualification.
- ntfsprogs-plus 1.0.0-3's `ntfsinfo` rejects the original boot-sector jump. The
  [audit](linux-syslinux-ntfs.md#ntfsprogs-plus-checker-incompatibility) traces the
  restriction to upstream `ntfsck_verify_boot_sector`. Normalizing only the first
  three bytes in a disposable readback copy allows clean volume metadata to be
  inspected. The copy is restored before 7-Zip reads; actual guest/BIOS media
  remains unchanged. This is explicitly not a successful strict-checker result.
- Existing `rufus_syslinux_native_command` and `rufus_syslinux_native_fat`

## CP20j — checked Syslinux v6 NTFS installation

Completed 2026-09-29. Adds `InstallNativeSyslinuxNtfs` and extracts the existing
payload comparison into a common FAT/NTFS verifier using the original Rufus
patcher. The fixed upstream extlinux executable still does the installation.
Neither helper requests nor GUI filesystem eligibility is expanded here.

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build passes, without a parallelism override.

  (52.2 s): source-backed FAT16/FAT32 and standalone v4/v6 on each FAT type.
- `rufus_format_options`, `rufus_syslinux_request` and
  `rufus_syslinux_packed_fields` pass. NTFS helper requests remain rejected.
- `syslinux_ntfs.py --adapter` runs **48 cases per driver**, both normally and
  under ASan/UBSan with leak detection: 96 passed cases per build, no sanitizer
  report. Linux 7.2.7-arch1-1, NTFS-3G 2026.7.7, 512-byte sectors, 4096-byte
  clusters, two 64-MiB disposable USB disks, offline QEMU TCG/SeaBIOS.
- The matrix tests rejected identities/geometry/nonempty roots, missing/failed
  providers, cancellation before/during/after the child, filesystem/device sync
  failures and EINTR, cache invalidation failure, read errors, changed device
  sequence/read-only mounts, damaged VBR/BPB/backup/loader/ADV/companion,
  symlinks/directories/hardlinks, malformed FIEMAP responses, FIEMAP I/O errors,
  FIBMAP holes/out-of-range blocks and successful mapping through each API.
  It checks expected started/sync states, no leaked descriptors/children, and
  preserved borrowed fd flags/position. Invalid FIEMAP never falls back.
- Both completed media per build unmount, remount read-only, match independent
  7-Zip file hashes and boot to the Syslinux 6.04 prompt. MBR, BPB, backup VBR,
  prefix/trailing guards and snapshot backing hashes are preserved. Guest hashes
  must match the USB-serial-associated image's independent readback.
  All four VGA text-buffer captures show the expected prompt. Two PNG captures
  showed a stale display refresh and were discarded; the other two were inspected.
- Python compilation and shell syntax checks pass.

The executable qualification found two adapter issues before completion: final
FIEMAP extents may end at the non-aligned file length (round only that final
extent, as upstream does); raw block-device cached pages can remain stale after
filesystem/device flushes (discard clean raw pages before readback). Keeping the
full repeated-install matrix exercises the latter, rather than bypassing the
raw comparison. Early diagnostics show the mismatch and the subsequent pass.

Fixture corrections: NTFS-3G's synthetic permissions already allow writing and
do not support the unnecessary chmod attempted by a fault injector; modify
permissions only when required. Match disks by USB serial, not enumeration
order, and compare guest hashes with host readback. Build the sanitized formatter
fixture before the sanitizer recipe. Earlier debug attempts are superseded by
`cp20j-qualified` and `cp20j-asan`; their compact logs remain for diagnosis.

The ntfsprogs-plus `EB 58 90` jump restriction remains recorded. Metadata checking
normalizes only a disposable copy's jump; real readback/boots use original
Syslinux bytes. No upstream sanitizer-clean claim, physical device, host mount,
provider installation or Windows customization test is involved. Windows file
attributes and the production helper's full creation lifecycle are not yet
qualified by this adapter checkpoint.

Artifacts: parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp20j-qualified/`, `cp20j-asan/`,

## CP20q — NTFS Syslinux with UEFI:NTFS and dual firmware boot (2026-09-29)

The explicit `prepare-ntfs-syslinux-uefi-device-v1` request reuses the existing
UEFI:NTFS flag, layout and payload writer. Shared `GetExtraPartitions` must match
the request; missing/unnecessary partitions are refused before writes. The
existing x64 EFI check rejects malformed fallback loaders. The helper preserves
the Syslinux MBR/disk signature when writing the original embedded payload,
then uses CP20p's NTFS extraction/installation/cleanup lifecycle. Qt eligibility
remains unchanged.

Validation:

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build and selected sanitizer helper/client/probe builds
  pass. Normal layout, UEFI:NTFS writer, format-options, ISO preflight and Syslinux
  request suites: **11/11**, 142.96 s. Protocol: **1/1**, 3.46 s. Normal/scaled
  Widgets: **2/2**, 1.04 s. Selected ASan/UBSan/LSan suites: **5/5**, 42.45 s.
- The generated ISO contains the existing Syslinux/config fixture plus a small
  x64 EFI application built by the VM-only `uefi_handoff_fixture` CMake target.
  A separate OVMF smoke check first verified that application itself. It needs
  no kernel, initramfs or OS installation on the resulting USB.
- Complete native helper matrices pass **30 kernel NTFS and 29 NTFS-3G jobs per
  build**, normally and under ASan/UBSan/LSan: **118 dual-firmware image jobs**.
  New cases cover an omitted required partition, an unnecessary partition on a
  BIOS-only image, malformed EFI, and payload failure, cancellation and failed
  flushing. Existing source/version/config, copy/installer, attribute/readback,
  mount/cleanup and source-change cases remain in the matrix.
- Every job checks one authorization, phase/counter rules, source preservation,
  release of device claims, descriptors/descendants and completion after helper
  exit. The Syslinux fixture now explicitly acknowledges the held launcher;
  it no longer depends on a short sleep to observe the result-before-exit state.
- Independent readback checks the exact embedded UEFI:NTFS payload, both MBR
  entries, original Syslinux code and random disk signature, NTFS BPB/backup,
  file attributes, nine copied/generated files and unused-space preservation.
  For the 64-MiB fixture the main partition starts at 1048576 and spans 64962560
  bytes; UEFI:NTFS starts at 66028032 and spans 1064448 bytes.
- Each of the **four outputs boots under both BIOS and x64 OVMF**. BIOS follows
  the copied Syslinux configuration to `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK`; UEFI displays the
  original UEFI:NTFS banner and executes the copied application, which reports
  `RUFUS_SYSLINUX_UEFI_OK` and the expected QEMU exit status. Snapshot boots leave
  the backing-disk hash unchanged. This is not Secure Boot qualification.
- The BIOS-only image regression also passes **25 kernel NTFS jobs and one
  configured BIOS boot**, retaining its one-partition layout. Total successful
  final runs: **143 helper jobs and nine firmware boots**.

Earlier attempts exposed fixture issues: missing `/tmp` for materializing the
embedded payload; no udev-style link for the second partition; and a readback
check that incorrectly expected zeroes in an untouched inter-partition gap.
The gap contained the seed's original `S` bytes, consistent with Rufus's bounded
metadata clearing. A sanitizer attempt missed the launcher's short exit delay;
explicit acknowledgement now makes that check deterministic. One fully booted
fallback run failed its final input-hash check because the guest test binary
was rebuilt concurrently; it was repeated successfully with unchanged inputs.
No production condition or policy was weakened to accommodate these failures.

Successful evidence is in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/`:
`cp20q-uefi-kernel-final/`, `cp20q-uefi-fuse-verified/`,
`cp20q-uefi-kernel-asan-final/`, `cp20q-uefi-fuse-asan-final/` and
`cp20q-bios-regression/`. These retain manifests, preflight results, serial logs,

baseline/diff and source hashes. Failed attempts retain diagnostic evidence too.
All disposable disks, source trees/ISOs, copied kernels/initramfs and OVMF copies
are removed on success and failure. Source releases and user files are preserved.

Kernel 7.2.7-arch1-1, QEMU TCG, 512-byte sectors and 4-KiB clusters were used.

Next: CP20r, Qt NTFS image selection and lifecycle integration as recorded in

## CP20r — Qt NTFS Syslinux image integration (2026-09-29)

Qt now offers NTFS for qualified Syslinux images. Selection reuses the Windows
`GetAllowedFileSystems`, `GetPreferredFileSystem` and `GetExtraPartitions` rules;
cluster choices reserve the same optional UEFI:NTFS space as the confirmed job.
FAT remains preferred where compatible, while an image requiring NTFS retains
the native MBR/Syslinux route. The ISO-recommended/DD dialog is unchanged.

The source-backed UEFI:NTFS flag is explicitly distinguished from standalone
UEFI:NTFS throughout image preflight, confirmation, progress and completion.
The image remains retained, unknown versions still require matching payloads,
and the shared progress implementation uses NTFS's 16% preparation/81% copy/3%
finalization allocation. At half-copy the operation text is 50.0%, the overall
bar is 37027/65535 (56.5%), and the first finalization slot is 64224 (98%). READY
requires the complete copied tree, matching layout, clean protocol result and
helper exit. No production helper, extractor, bootloader payload, mount path or
Windows source was changed in this checkpoint.

A missing-formatter test exposed that ISO preflight had left this check to the
helper, although source-free jobs already checked it before authorization. The
existing formatter check now serves both paths, initially and after confirmation.
The privileged helper still performs its own checks. DD bypasses format/installer
preflight as before.

Validation uses the existing private D-Bus and regular-file USB fixtures, real
ISO analysis/preflight and a child process implementing the helper protocol.
It checks known and compatible-unknown sources, mismatched modules, load/reload,
MBR/GPT and FAT/NTFS switching, small-target limits, immutable requests, missing
installer/formatter before and after confirmation, BIOS-only layout, required
EFI partition, confirmation cancellation, copy percentages, authorization denial,
short copy, wrong layout, sync/cleanup failures, cancellation during formatting,
bootloader/copy/finalization, result-before-exit and unplug after successful READY.
The large-file selection case injects only Rufus's size classification; it does
not allocate or qualify another multi-gigabyte image.

Results and limits:

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build and selected sanitizer builds pass without any
  parallelism override. Compiler warnings are from existing libcdio/wimlib C
  headers included by C++; there is no new adapter warning.
- Normal shared policy, geometry, Syslinux selection/request, ISO preflight,
  helper protocol and normal/scaled window suites: **11/11**, 11.45 s.
- Final complete functional Widgets suite: **593 passed, zero failed, two
  skipped**, 132.01 s. The optional read-only Windows/Alpine real-ISO cases were
  not supplied their environment paths; generated ISO cases all ran.
- Selected ASan/UBSan/LSan component/protocol suites: **4/4**, 15.43 s.
- Targeted functional Widgets: **47/47** at 150% scaling, 14.42 s;
  **69/69** under sanitizers including standalone preflight regressions, 28.98 s.

No native media writes/firmware boots were repeated: CP20p/q qualify the unchanged

## CP21a — GRUB2 reuse audit and executable probe (2026-09-29)

The [reuse audit](linux-grub2-reuse.md) traces Windows boot selection, filesystem
eligibility, MBR/SBR/PBR writes, payload provenance, version/cache/download
handling and standalone content. The result is to reuse Rufus's original GRUB2
MBR and selected `core.img` through a small bounded adapter. A host `grub-install`
would generate a different core/module installation, whereas these existing
payloads already carry Rufus's version, prefix and patches. No production source,
main build, Windows source or Qt option changes in this checkpoint.

A separate CMake probe compiles the unchanged `src/ms-sys/br.c` and supplies
ordinary bounded stdio callbacks for `write_grub2_mbr`. It places the unchanged
core at byte 512, matching `WriteSBR`. Existing partition/formatter probes create
64-MiB FAT16 and FAT32 regular files, with seeded metadata and embedding gaps.
The complete before/after comparison permits changes only to the original
432-byte MBR payload, boot signature and core range. Disk ID, partition entry,
remaining gap and formatted volume must survive. Payload hashes, the MBR array's
agreement with `boot.img`, BIOS workaround, first-sector pointer and core block
list are checked independently.

SeaBIOS boots each file as an emulated USB disk. GRUB's actual `set` output must
report `(hd0,msdos1)/boot/grub` and `hd0,msdos1`; a directory command must find the
known marker on each filesystem. Snapshot boots must leave the backing hash
unchanged. Source hashes are checked again after testing.

Final results:

- Normal standalone CMake/Ninja build and boot CTest: **1/1**, 5.55 s. This
  contains **two bare BIOS boots and eight unchanged-target refusals**, covering
  empty/undersized payloads, payloads larger than the embedding gap and the
  63-sector old-BIOS layout, separately for each filesystem.
- ASan/UBSan/LSan build and the same boot CTest: **1/1**, 5.56 s, with another
  **two boots and eight refusals**. The original ms-sys routine and file harness
  are instrumented; the existing formatter/partition probes, native tools,
  firmware and prebuilt core are not. Leak detection is enabled without
  suppressions. The sanitizer run used the approved environment outside the
  sandbox so LSan could run; normal qualification needs no privileges.
- Existing shared GRUB image/inspection, format-policy and partition-layout
  suites: **4/4**, 0.12 s. Python syntax and scoped whitespace checks pass.
  Final probe builds have no compiler warnings. Ninja used default parallelism.

Two initial fixture failures are retained: QEMU first tried to place its snapshot
under sandbox-read-only `/var/tmp`, so its `TMPDIR` now points at the disposable
fixture directory; the prefix assertion first expected unquoted values, whereas
GRUB 2.14 prints quoted values. The corrected check also waits for the later
`root` line before inspecting the completed output. Neither fix changes payloads
or weakens a production rule.

The bare rescue prompt is expected: Windows's standalone GRUB2 option does not
supply `normal.mod`, a menu or an OS. These tests establish the original payload's
BIOS handoff and FAT directory reads, not a complete helper job, module/menu/OS
handoff, NTFS/ext support, UEFI, Secure Boot or physical firmware qualification.
The native formatter's PBR remains in this probe; Windows also writes standard
PBRs, which must be included in the next adapter rather than omitted because
GRUB does not use them. No host GRUB installation, mount, physical media write,
Windows build or additional Windows customization qualification was performed.

Evidence is in parent `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp21a-boot/` and
`cp21a-boot-asan/`, with text screens, QEMU commands, readback facts and hashes.
Build/CTest logs, initial failure diagnostics, the scoped baseline/diff and source
hashes are retained alongside them. Generated disks and QEMU snapshots are
removed on success and failure; no large fixture is retained or user ISO changed.

Next: CP21b, the bounded MBR/SBR/standard-PBR adapter on regular files, with
identity/bounds checks, partial-I/O, cancellation, flush and readback failures.
Then integrate the existing standalone helper lifecycle and advanced Qt option
in a separate checkpoint. Source-backed version/module selection remains later
work, as recorded in the plan and parity backlog.


## CP21b — production GRUB2 file adapters (2026-09-29)

The existing MBR writer now selects Rufus's original 432-byte GRUB2 array.
`WriteGrub2CoreImage` uses that writer's target/layout checks and transfer loop
to place immutable selected bytes at byte 512, without changing the rest of the
embedding gap or the partition. It checks bounds before writes, handles partial
I/O and cancellation, flushes written bytes even after failure, preserves the
first error plus any sync error, and verifies the payload and MBR before success.
The public core entry point currently rejects device requests.

The former `freedos_boot` adapter is renamed `fat_boot`, with an explicit standard
or FreeDOS choice. It calls the unchanged ms-sys FAT writers through the existing
bounded staging streams, validates the BPB and FAT32 backup, and retains its
flush/readback behavior. The existing FreeDOS helper explicitly selects the same
FreeDOS records. Standard device records remain gated for the helper checkpoint.
No original Windows source or payload, formatter, Qt behavior or authorization
flow changes. There is no new installer or second FAT I/O implementation.

Validation and results:

- Full normal CMake/Ninja build and selected sanitizer targets pass. Warnings
  come from existing upstream wimlib/libcdio code and headers; no new adapter
  warnings remain. Ninja used default parallelism.
- Normal GRUB2 FAT16/FAT32 MBR creation/preparation, FreeDOS and standard PBR
  suites: **six passed**. Both PBR suites run **102 install/refusal/fault cases**,
  plus memory bounds and non-file rejection. Independent expected bytes come
  from the original arrays; directory labels, BPBs, FSInfo hints, backups and
  all surrounding bytes are checked.
- The normal regression run passes **16/16**, 142.56 s. It includes the corrected
  core suite (**101 cases**), original FreeDOS records/request, Rufus/Windows 7
  bootstraps, Syslinux with NTFS/UEFI:NTFS, non-bootable FAT, UEFI:NTFS copying,
  SFD preparation, FAT16/FAT32 helper jobs and shared format/layout policies.
  Together these runs cover **22 distinct passing normal suites**.
- ASan/UBSan/LSan GRUB2 MBR, core, standard PBR and FreeDOS suites: **7/7**,
  105.94 s. Leak detection remains enabled without suppressions; the approved
  run outside the sandbox allows LSan to operate. Upstream native tools and
  firmware are not instrumented.
- The reusable firmware probe now has a native mode. Production MBR/core and
  standard PBR adapters generate 64-MiB FAT16/FAT32 images, then **two normal

The core cases cover empty/undersized/oversized inputs, exact-gap fit, multiple
buffer chunks, invalid options/descriptor flags/size/sectors/code/identity,

including a later chunk, and capacity changes. Complete-file comparisons assert

and sanitizer build/test logs, detailed assertions, boot screens/manifests and

## CP21f — original NTFS PBR on formatted files (2026-09-29)

The new adapter reuses `ms-sys/ntfs.c:write_ntfs_br` and the existing native

writes/reads back exactly 4,136 bytes on the borrowed partition descriptor.
The last-sector backup remains unchanged, matching Windows's `WritePBR` call.
The in-memory ms-sys callbacks moved from the FAT adapter into one shared C
file, without changing Rufus's original writers or introducing `FAKE_FD`.

The initial whole-file comparison caught an off-by-one test/adapter bound: the
test parser counted `0x54` in the C array's name as a byte. The array contains

record, and the run passes. No physical USB, host mount/install, helper job,
firmware boot, Windows build or additional Windows customization test was used.
Generated files were removed. NTFS GRUB2 stays disabled in Qt until the complete
helper and representative BIOS boot qualify.

The source-free `prepare-grub2-ntfs-device-v1` request now uses the existing

Snapshot boots leave the verified backing hash unchanged.

## CP21ac — GRUB ISO NTFS with UEFI:NTFS backend integration

2026-10-01. This is the bounded request/preflight/helper/regular-file checkpoint.
Native combined USB creation and both firmware boots remain the next checkpoint;
the Qt EFI-capable GRUB/NTFS gate is deliberately retained.

Production changes reuse existing code:

- `PrepareImageRequest` distinguishes a source-backed GRUB+UEFI:NTFS request
  from standalone UEFI:NTFS, retaining its ISO source. An explicit NTFS/MBR
  operation encodes the combined request; missing/incomplete sources,
  standalone/FAT/ext requests and customization options are rejected.

  GRUB NTFS bootstrap. Shared `GetExtraPartitions` policy still decides whether
  the ISO requires it; request/image disagreement is refused before writes.

  when UEFI:NTFS is requested, just as the combined Syslinux route does. A
  vendor-only loader, invalid EFI subsystem, read error or cancellation fails.
- The existing helper uses the confirmed dual-partition layout for the retained
  GRUB core, original NTFS boot-record adapter and full embedded UEFI:NTFS image.
  There is one bootloader phase, followed by the existing mount/extract/finalize
  sequence. A payload write/sync error stops before copying. No new formatter,
  mount provider, raw writer, installer or job abstraction is added.

requires both the original payload banner and application serial marker. All

through pacman, leaving hwinfo 26.0-1.1 in place. The installed libntfs now needs
libhd.so.26 and has no missing dependencies. No package pin, ABI alias or Rufus
production change was introduced.
