## CP23c — bounded native parallel checksum pipeline (2026-10-18)

Revalidate CP23b as completed progress and audit the current Windows HashThread,
IndividualHashThread and SetThreadAffinity implementation. Windows uses three
64-KiB read buffers, one worker per requested algorithm and asynchronous reading.
The first Linux reader hashes algorithms sequentially in its read worker. Measure
that exact retained source and a native pipeline with the same unchanged digest
core, compiler and optimized flags before claiming a performance improvement.
No actual Windows executable is benchmarked or qualified here.

Replace only the native file reader's internals. One pread thread feeds three
64-KiB slots; three or four algorithm workers each retain their own context and
consume every slot in source order. A slot remains immutable until all consumers
release it. Fast algorithms can proceed within that bounded queue while a slow
consumer applies backpressure. The calling RufusJob thread coordinates progress,
cancellation, final source checking and result publication. No Qt cancellation or
reporting query runs on a pthread reader/consumer. Completed byte counts mean all
algorithms have consumed those bytes; read-ahead alone is not progress. Short reads
are accumulated into the current slot; EINTR is retried and premature EOF fails.

Use monotonic condition waits with 50-ms cancellation polling. On failure/cancel,
wake every pipeline wait and join every successfully created reader/algorithm
thread before freeing buffers or returning. Treat partial allocation/mutex/
condition/attribute/thread setup as errno failures with empty results. Keep the
source descriptor and offset with the caller. Source dev/inode/size/mtime/ctime
must still match after all joins. Allocate the over-aligned contexts and buffers
with posix_memalign; total pipeline allocation stays below 256 KiB regardless of
image size, with a fixed maximum of five pthread workers. Join/teardown invariants
never allow a result or freed shared buffer while a worker remains outstanding.
The existing GUI source-close/QThread-join gate still follows the native pipeline.

The native scheduler honors the caller's Linux CPU affinity/cpuset instead of
installing Windows affinity-mask groups. A single-allowed-CPU run also passes.
Cooperative cleanup replaces Windows' forced thread termination: an in-flight
regular-file read must return before its reader can be joined. Full READY/results
remain gated during that cleanup. This preserves the port's completed-I/O contract
and avoids abandoning a thread with access to freed buffers or a closed source.
Algorithms, default/optional hashes, CPU detection, GUI/settings, helper and wire
protocol are unchanged; no additional dependency or physical target is involved.

Optimized standalone comparisons use GCC 16.2.1, -O2/-DNDEBUG, the same probe/core/
source adapters, generated nonzero RAM-backed files and three samples per size/
mode, alternating variant order. Each run independently verifies all requested
digests with hashlib and checks source inode/size/mtime/ctime. Median MiB/s:

| Input | Hashes | Retained serial | Native pipeline | Ratio |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 MiB | MD5/SHA1/SHA256 | 103.10 | 200.36 | 1.94x |
| 64 MiB | plus SHA512 | 80.49 | 209.53 | 2.60x |
| 256 MiB | MD5/SHA1/SHA256 | 112.45 | 220.09 | 1.96x |
| 256 MiB | plus SHA512 | 81.97 | 215.99 | 2.63x |

This quantifies the native algorithm/read pipeline on this shared x86-64 host,
without SHA instruction support, with warm memory-backed input and no-op progress
callbacks. It is not a Windows application, storage-device or complete desktop
throughput comparison. Both configured normal/sanitizer GUI/helper builds remain
Debug; optimized probes are separate compact evidence binaries.

Normal and ASan/UBSan/leak checks pass the retained-source and reader fault suites,
27 new startup/ownership/backpressure/cancellation cases, 100 independent digest/
stream cases, 14 GUI cases and three scaled GUI cases. Reader-fault fixture
counters/cancellation become atomic because pread now runs on a reader pthread;
assertions still check each short read, error, source mutation, offset and empty
failed result. Progress may coalesce, so assertion counts depend on scheduling.
The new test holds all algorithms, proves exactly three slots of read-ahead,
releases fast consumers while SHA256 is held, verifies bounded reuse with literal
independent digests, and cancels while the reader is blocked and consumers remain
held. Completion checks require all thread joins and destroyed resources. Inject
allocation, mutex, condition attributes/clock, each condition init, and each default/
extra algorithm or reader creation failure. Thread ownership is checked for
reporting/cancellation and source I/O; the source offset stays unchanged.

ThreadSanitizer also passes the 27 native lifecycle cases. They pass when confined
to one allowed CPU. QEMU's SHA-capable CPU executes the same 100 vector/stream

## CP28a — original Unix-compress/LZW retained-source reader (2026-10-18)

The read-only source foundation now accepts `.Z` (type 2). Extract the original
`decompress_uncompress.c` dictionary/bitstream body into `uncompress_core.inc`,
shared by Windows and the native adapter. Disabled-hook preprocessing is
identical to the captured original, including default allocations, width/CLEAR
alignment and original flags. Add the include to both Windows project inventories
and Automake distributions. The new native provider has no executable or library
runtime dependency. Existing gzip/XZ/BZIP2/LZMA bodies, writer, strict protocol,
helper, worker/controller and picker remain unchanged: eight production files
change, three are added and 719 prior production files are byte-identical.

The per-operation reader owns four zeroed buffers/tables plus its owner across
the C jump boundary. Retained `pread` batches short reads/EINTR, preserves the
caller's descriptor/offset and treats EOF before captured size as EIO. Output is
ordered in at most 64-KiB chunks, bounded before consumption, counted in actual
64-bit bytes, and published only after retained source identity and cancellation
checks. All allocation failures, consumer errors, cancellation and malformed
input release ownership and clear the result. The contract fixture measures five
allocations and a 526688-byte peak, including the owner. There is no expanded
intermediate image and no mutable global or thread-local decoder I/O.

Preserve original block/non-block dictionaries, KwKwK, width growth/alignment,
CLEAR, ignored 0x20/0x40 flags and the original lack of a lower-width header guard.
Unix compress consumes to EOF: no decoded-size promise, checksum or end marker
exists. Incomplete final-code bits are ignored; truncation can produce a valid
shorter stream and appended bytes may become codes. Report one member and zero
trailing bytes; never claim that all truncation/corruption is detectable.

Two concrete native corrections are intentional. The original final callback
can fail while its wrapper returns 196645 success bytes: only 196608 were accepted
with 64-KiB output buffers, or zero with Windows' default 256-KiB buffer. Native
consumer failures propagate their errno, including the final callback, instead
of publishing success. The original also increments saturated nine-bit streams
to ten bits: a valid 4096-literal zero stream silently becomes 3712 bytes. Native
initial and CLEAR resets retain nine bits at that dictionary limit, matching
current upstream ncompress's fixed decoder. Windows preprocessing remains exact.
The fixed decoder and native provider agree on all 24 pinned upstream vectors;
ten additional full-width nine-bit reference vectors and the silent-loss fixture
produce exact content. Legacy ncompress 4.2.4.6's long `-C` output does not round
trip even through its own decoder; use separately verified non-block fixtures.
The old encoder also loses three bytes in the sampled saturated nine-bit stream;
without a format size/checksum that loss cannot be inferred from the stored file.
Provider revisions, source SHA256/URLs and every observed result are retained.

The independent Python fixture encoder is test-only. GNU gzip and both pinned
ncompress decoders validate proper non-block fixtures at supported original
boundaries; fixed current ncompress validates saturated nine-bit fixtures. The
387-case corpus compares native bytes/hash/prefix/count with independent data and
the original wrapper at 64-/256-KiB input/output and gzip-dispatch entry. It covers
all 9..16 widths, block/non-block, saturation, CLEAR/group/refill boundaries,
KwKwK, flags, bad headers/codes, incomplete final bits, mutations/tails, explicit
limits and both native corrections. The retained-source test passes 37197 checks,
all five allocation failures, short/EINTR/early/late I/O, buffered/callback cancel,
final positive/negative consumer errors, identity changes and concurrent readers.
An independent gzip pass verifies all prefix/zero content. The actual native
count separately confirms 4294967808 decoded bytes, exact prefix and caller-bound
refusal, storing only encoded data; its large test uses count mode, not a native
full-output digest. Normal final source/corpus/large tests pass. The final ASan/UBSan source/corpus/large qualification also passes.

The initial 21-target regression set passes on both builds and covers admitted gzip/XZ/BZIP2/LZMA source,
writer, helper/protocol and all 96 analysis/99 focused Widgets results. The final
nine-bit correction is separately rebuilt and requalified on the three provider
and source targets; it cannot alter the unchanged other provider bodies. Record

The first broad build command named nonexistent test targets and stopped before
compilation; corrected target names build with Ninja default parallelism. Preserve

because its numeric parser omitted `HELD99`; the parser was corrected and the
full normal and sanitizer recipes then passed. Evidence and an independent
audit are in `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp29e`.

## CP30a/b — bundled Zstd source, frozen writer and strict helper (2026-10-18)

The original bundled Zstd decoder builds unchanged except for a Linux-only
guard around Windows CRT/libbb includes. The retained-source adapter bounds
input and output buffers, enforces the original 128-MiB window, preserves the
caller descriptor offset and validates all frames to EOF. Its independent CLI
corpus passes 46 vectors: known/unknown content size, checksum variants,
concatenated/empty/skippable frames, malformed/truncated/trailing data,
large-window refusal, short/EINTR/I/O/cancel/callback faults, and a real
`2^32 + 512` byte decoded count with EFBIG at `2^32`. Expanded output is never
stored; temporary compressed fixtures are removed.

The native Zstd writer test passes 118 geometry/frozen-plan/write/readback/fault
cases on owned regular files. The strict helper protocol passes; 51 simulated
helper jobs cover sector sizes, one claim, mounted protection, cancellation,
sync/cleanup, failure propagation and decoded readback. Normal focused
source/writer/helper regressions pass. The 13-target ASan/UBSan/leak focused
suite also passes as the ordinary user outside the sandbox because LeakSanitizer
cannot inspect local children inside it. Prior gzip/XZ/ZIP source and gzip/ZIP
writer/helper tests pass in the same runs. Both normal and sanitizer app/helper
targets link. The `zstd` CLI is used only as an independent test encoder, not
at runtime.

The CP29c 733-file production baseline now differs in eight existing files:
CP29e changed three and CP30 changes six, with CMake common to both sets.
Two new Zstd adapter files are added. The
remaining 725 baseline hashes are identical. Evidence is in
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp30ab`, including the scoped production delta and
normal/sanitizer CTest logs. No physical device or disposable guest block
device was touched. At CP30a/b, ordinary `.zst` picker/SELECT stayed gated until real guest
helper qualification, then full Qt confirmation/joined READY qualification.
The full Windows parity goal remains active.

The 37 vectors include a 1025-segment table, `2^32 + 512` logical-byte count,

## CP31b — frozen VTSI sparse writer and simulated helper (2026-10-18)

The native plan now freezes the logical zero-gap SHA256 and a separate ordered
extent-map SHA256. The VTSI packet requires both lowercase hashes; missing,
malformed or changed map hashes fail before any target claim. The writer
revalidates source and target identity, writes only aligned listed extents,
syncs after partial/complete writes, then compares the written extents against
the retained source. Gaps and bytes after the logical disk size remain exactly
as they were. Physical write/verify counters count segment data rather than
skipped logical bytes.

Twenty-six independent regular-file cases cover 512/4096/65536-byte target
sectors, unaligned refusal, same-size source substitution during preflight,
copy and verify, a same-logical/different-map mutation, short/EINTR/I/O faults,
dirty cancellation, sync, readback and target identity. Nineteen simulated
helper cases cover packet, claim, mounted protection, source ownership,
prewrite and dirty failures, close ordering and untouched gaps. The normal and
ASan/UBSan/leak focused CTest runs each pass 11/11 targets, including gzip
and Zstd writer/helper regressions and both VTSI and legacy helper packets.
Both GUI and helper binaries link. Sanitizer tests run as the ordinary user
outside the sandbox for LeakSanitizer's process inspection. No physical USB or
host block device was opened; temporary fixtures were removed. Logs are in
`.rufus-test-artifacts/cp31b`.

Real guest block-device sparse write/readback and ordinary Qt selection are
the next gates. Full Windows parity remains active.


## CP31c — VTSI real guest sparse write and client counters (2026-10-18)

The disposable 512-byte-sector QEMU USB guest builds VTSI images independently.
One job rejects a wrong frozen map hash before writes. A guarded helper then
writes two separated 64-KiB extents to the real guest block device while an
independent disk read confirms the intervening and trailing `0xa5` bytes stay
untouched. Its observed kernel claim covers two positioned writes, one sync,
two readbacks, 27 exclusive-claim checks and target close. The client reports
131,072 physical bytes written and verified for a 262,144-byte logical image.

That guest exposed a client protocol assumption: raw progress is a logical
disk position for VTSI, while result counters are physical segment bytes. The
client now keeps strict logical progress through the final sector and accepts
a successful VTSI result only when nonzero physical writes are fully verified.
Dense raw/compressed jobs retain their exact full-size counter checks. Normal
and ASan/UBSan/leak process suites each pass 8/8 gzip/XZ/BZIP2/LZMA/LZW/ZIP/
Zstd/VTSI targets, including sparse success, short verification, overcount and
incomplete logical-progress refusal.

A final VTSI image restores all 67,108,864 bootable bytes through the production
helper. Both normal and sanitizer guests pass the five seed and five mounted/
unmounted raw setup jobs, three VTSI cases, independent host disk/FAT-file
hashes and BIOS boot. The 64-MiB data file is renamed before appending VTSI
metadata, so the guest's caller tmpfs does not retain duplicate large images.
Both app/helper builds link; disposable virtual disks are removed after logs,
manifests and readback results are exported to `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp31c`.
No physical USB or host block device was opened.

Ordinary Qt `.vtsi` SELECT/confirmation/joined READY remains the next gate.
Full Windows parity remains active.

## CP34 — full FFU and preview 3 (2026-10-19)

The embedded FFU reader supports full single-store V1/V2 and V1-compressed
none/plain XPRESS (algorithm 0/1/3). It validates the security/image/store roots,
manifest dimensions, variable descriptors, source bounds and all SHA256 chunks
before output, including overwritten temporary GPT payloads. Repeated and
overlapping locations follow final write order; end-relative entries resolve
at the captured size; omitted blocks reconstruct as zero. Ordinary `.ffu`/`.FFU`
SELECT, frozen logical size/SHA256, confirmation and the existing native
writer/helper/readback/joined READY route are connected end to end.

The focused 61-case corpus passes in normal and ASan/UBSan/leak builds. It
covers V1/V2/compressed variants, 512/4096-sector metadata, extended roots,
multi-block/repeated/overwritten/end-relative maps, zero gaps, malformed roots,
descriptor bounds, unsupported methods, truncated files, integrity refusal
before output/target writes, XPRESS literal/extended match decoding, source
I/O/cancellation/consumer faults and native regular-file copy/readback. The
existing VHDX corpus also passes. LeakSanitizer needs execution outside the
restricted sandbox to inspect its own child processes; that rerun passes.

Independent Img2Ffu at `d0dda2b2e138dd0412018bc733e64d1a92c385b0` creates V1
and V2 FFUs from a synthetic 32-MiB GPT disk. The native reader reconstructs
both with the original raw SHA256. The encoder is retargeted from .NET 8 to
the installed .NET 10 only; its format code is unchanged. An independent
`dissect.util` XPRESS decoder also agrees on a paired/extended-match vector.
These tools remain test providers and add no production dependency.

One combined QEMU guest per build runs one seed and two ordinary FFU Qt jobs:
a 1-MiB XPRESS write with target tail preserved and a full 64-MiB bootable
uncompressed restore. Both guests pass actual kernel claim/write/readback,
one helper per job, held-99/joined 100% READY, independent host disk/FAT-file
hashes and BIOS boot. Existing helper fault matrices are reused and no raw
fault jobs are repeated. The guest FFUs carry the existing synthetic BIOS
fixture; the independent encoder examples separately cover GPT structure.
The single normal image-analysis/full raw-write Widgets regression gate is
recorded in `widgets-normal.log`.

Preview 3 packages the route as a native Arch/CachyOS package and generic
install archive. The package inspection checks exact binaries/policy,
dependencies, desktop entry, documentation, headless help/version and one
isolated native GUI launch. No host package is installed. Compact evidence is
in `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp34`; packages/checksums are in `build/releases`.
Disposable guest/oracle media and package staging are removed after export.
No physical USB or host block device is opened.

This preserves the captured disk layout rather than implementing DISM's
portable resizing/relocation. Other FFU codecs, partial/multi-store deployment,
unaligned captures, larger tables and catalog trust remain explicit parity
gaps. The support guide documents these bounds; device-image saving is next.
Format references are Microsoft's FFU image/integrity sections in Windows
Manufacturing Documentation 2019 (included with
[Img2Ffu](https://github.com/MobileTooling/img2ffu)), and
[MS-XCA plain LZ77 decompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-xca/34cb9ab9-5ce6-42d7-a518-107c1c7c65e7).

## CP35 — device image saving and preview 4 (2026-10-19)

One end-to-end batch adds the ordinary save-device action for fixed VHD,
dynamic VHDX and full uncompressed FFU. Windows `SaveImage` in `src/vhd.c`
uses the corresponding VHD footer, virtual-disk API and DISM capture routes.
Its ISO action uses oscdimg to create UDF from a mounted filesystem tree;
that export remains explicitly tracked for a separate implementation.

The Linux GUI stays unprivileged. The worker freezes the selected device and
kernel disk sequence, checks the destination filesystem against the source,
and requests `UDisks.Block.OpenDevice("r")` once with an exclusive read flag
and interactive authorization allowed. It keeps the returned read-only claim
through capture, native decoder/hash verification and a source consistency
reread. It then checks the selection again, closes the source, syncs/closes
and atomically publishes the private destination, syncs its directory and
joins the worker before full green READY. Existing output is retained until
commit. Cancellation while authorization is pending waits for the late reply
and closes its descriptor before becoming terminal. Sync/close/cleanup errors
remain failures, including an error after publication.

Boundaries are in `linux-support.md`: fixed VHD uses 512-byte sectors and the
2040-GiB limit; dynamic VHDX supports 512/4096-byte logical sectors up to
64 TiB, with zero blocks omitted; FFU emits every 128-KiB block in one
uncompressed V1 store and currently bounds capture to 128 GiB, a valid primary
GPT and printable nonempty ASCII partition names. The unsigned catalog template
retains Img2Ffu's MIT notice. No external encoder, DISM, Wine, .NET or Python
runtime is needed. Mounted sources, automatic unmount, read-only discovery,
additional FFU capture layouts, ISO export and remaining image operations stay
in the backlog.

### Consolidated qualification

- **29** focused cases in both normal and ASan/UBSan builds: all formats,
  512/4096-byte encoding, zero blocks, a partial final VHDX block, short/EINTR
  I/O, read/write/sync failures, capture/verification cancellation, source
  mutation, output corruption, invalid descriptor modes, malformed GPT,
  symlink refusal, changed/new destinations, overwrite preservation and
  directory-sync rollback/post-publication failure.
- Independent QEMU VHD/VHDX decoding, plus direct BAT reconstruction for 4-KiB
  VHDX because QEMU's VHDX driver rejects that logical sector size. Img2Ffu's
  independent reader verifies FFU metadata/payload hashes and reconstructs the
  manifest-sized disk; the test adapter bounds reads to that size to avoid
  the upstream stream's extra block and non-terminating EOF behavior.
- Combined normal and sanitizer USB guests: one bootable seed, real uid/gid
  1000 capture client with no direct raw-device access, one read-only D-Bus
  acquisition per operation, delayed-authorization cancellation and denial
  preserving an old backup, all three full 64-MiB captures, held completion,
  joined READY, claim release and post-success unplug stability. Independent
  exported-image readback covers every capture. One saved VHDX is restored
  through the existing production helper, with whole-disk and ten-file FAT
  readback and a BIOS boot. Existing writer fault evidence is reused.
- One relevant Qt gate: image-analysis Widgets, raw-write Widgets, window and
  enlarged-scale window. Two stale window expectations were corrected (About
  keyboard focus and setting discovery availability for the save picker),
  followed by focused passing window checks. The raw-write suite is run once.
- Native Arch/CachyOS and generic install packages are inspected without host
  installation: five executables, matching policy, dependencies, empty RPATH,
  desktop entry, docs/licenses, headless CLI and isolated offscreen launch.

Evidence: `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp35/checks.json`, compact logs/manifests and
package checksums. The first guest attempt exposed a missing caller in the
private test bus policy; the second passed capture/restore/boot but its input
audit detected a concurrent test-binary rebuild. Both diagnostics are retained;
the final guests use stable binaries. Disposable source/target/export media
and package staging are removed after evidence export. No physical USB or host
block device is opened by these tests. Actual desktop authorization UI,
physical media, Windows mounting and DISM deployment remain unqualified.

## CP36 — ISO export, automatic source unmount and preview 5 (2026-10-19)

One delivery batch completes filesystem ISO export and mounted-device saving.
Windows `IsoSaveImageThread` uses oscdimg with `-u2 -udfver102`, hidden-file
retention and no synthesized boot catalog. Linux uses unprivileged cdrtools
mkisofs, then replaces the ISO/UDF bridge recognition area with the UDF-only
VRS; UDF anchor, partition and file addresses stay unchanged. Native UDF
readback checks every directory/path, size and SHA256, followed by a complete
source manifest reread before the existing atomic destination publication.
Hidden files, empty directories, Unicode names, long paths and >4-GiB files
are retained; `ldlinux.sys` is not filtered as it is during media creation.
Links, special files, mixed mounts and invalid UTF-8 fail explicitly.

Mounted captures and ISO exports use one polkit `--save-device` source helper
through validation, ordinary unmount, read-only acquisition and cleanup. The
existing `--device` writing action remains distinct. Fresh frozen UDisks and
native inventories protect the caller home, output backing and system/layered
uses. Unix peer credentials and a job token bind the read-only descriptor to
the unprivileged caller. The helper accepts no output pathname. Raw capture
reacquires an exclusive handle; ISO privately mounts the whole filesystem or
first filesystem partition by offset. FAT/exFAT filenames use UTF-8, ext3/ext4
disable journal replay, and the preferred new kernel NTFS uses read-only mode.
Unavailable NTFS driver support uses one foreground read-only NTFS-3G process
with recovery disabled. Cleanup/close errors remain failures; READY waits for
source cleanup, helper exit, durable publication and worker exit. No automatic
remount or eject occurs.

### Consolidated qualification and delivery

- Normal and ASan/UBSan component batches reuse the 29 CP35 capture/transaction
  cases, add 24 source-protocol/FD/authorization cases and 14 ISO cases. The
  original ISO corpus fully encodes, decodes and hashes an actual >4-GiB file;
  the final focused 13-case run also covers running-encoder cancellation.
  Short I/O, copy/verification cancellation, symlink/FIFO refusal, missing or
  failed encoder, destination races and durable-publication faults are covered.
  Cancelling the encoder must reap it, retain the old backup and remove staging.
- One combined route in each build uses a uid/gid 1000 Qt client, six source
  authorizations for six jobs: mounted cancellation, mounted VHDX, busy ISO,
  private-unmount fault, FAT ISO and NTFS-3G ISO. Held helper exit verifies
  completion is joined. Kernel UDF loop mounts independently compare all FAT
  and NTFS export entries. The FUSE daemon must exit. One captured VHDX is
  independently decoded by QEMU, restored through the existing writer and
  checked by whole-disk/file readback and BIOS boot. Unchanged writer faults
  are reused. Only guarded disposable guest block devices are used.
- One relevant normal Qt gate covers image analysis, window, scaled window,
  raw-write Widgets and prepare-process behavior. A fixture binary rebuilt
  during the first raw suite caused a launch failure and a daemon cascade;
  passed prefix groups were retained and all remaining groups were resumed
  together (617 passed, one existing optional real-ISO skip). No second full
  raw suite was required.
- Preview 5 packages are built without host installation. Inspection checks
  five executables, both exact helper/policy argument matches, documentation,
  licenses, dependency resolution, empty RPATH, desktop metadata, headless
  CLI and one isolated GUI launch. cdrtools is an optional ISO-export provider.

Compact evidence: `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp36/checks.json`. Development guest
failures exposed missing fixture tools/modules/temp directory, a mountpoint
metatype registration and stale busy-source test assumptions. Those logs are
retained. The running-encoder test found and fixed a production wait loop that
continued after an inner wait had reaped the process. Final guest inputs stay
stable throughout their runs. Disposable images and package staging are removed.
Native new-kernel NTFS source mounts, ext/exFAT export, actual desktop polkit UI
and physical media have no new end-to-end qualification in this batch. The
support guide records bounds. Read-only discovery, remaining FFU layouts,
parent/log handling and the rest of Windows parity remain unfinished.

## CP37 — read-only device discovery and saving, preview 6 (2026-10-19)

Close read-only USB discovery and image saving as one delivery batch. Linux
previously removed these devices before the save action could see them.
Discovery now requires a known boolean UDisks ReadOnly property, retains that
capability on Device, and explicitly requests read access in the shared native
USB/identity checks. Write remains the default access for all existing target
checks. Save-specific snapshots and use checks permit read-only media without
relaxing protected/system, output/source backing, swap, layered-storage, holder,
mount alias or busy-source checks. No production code clears BLKROSET.

Known read-only changes keep the physical source ID and selection, publish the
capability immediately, and invalidate a pending or active creation job when
it becomes read-only. Unknown/invalidated state still discards eligibility.
The Device list marks `[Read-only]`, saving remains enabled and START explains
the save action; formatting controls stay disabled. Image selection stays
available. Capture uses the existing one UDisks read acquisition for unmounted
raw images or one source helper for mounted raw/ISO, with the same descriptor,
source consistency, transactional publication, cleanup and joined READY rules.

Windows references are `src/dev.c:GetDevices`, which opens physical devices
through the Windows read/write handle API during enumeration, and
`src/vhd.c:SaveImage` / `src/iso.c:IsoSaveImageThread` for saving. Linux uses
explicit source-versus-target access because UDisks supplies write protection
as discovery metadata and saving needs only read access. No native Windows
read-only-device UI comparison or physical switch qualification is claimed.

### One qualification batch

- Normal and ASan/UBSan batches run 24 source-protocol boundaries, 29 existing
  capture/transaction cases and the 86-row mount-policy suite. Read access is
  tested against default write refusal, child read-only mounts, kernel/UDisks
  matching, output-on-source refusal, protected/layered/swap/unknown states,
  malformed flags and zero metadata-only discovery opens.
- Focused discovery/controls tests cover known writable/read-only transitions
  without replacing the source, save availability, disabled creation controls,
  stale confirmation refusal and no authorization or write from an obsolete
  confirmation. The production discovery/access boundaries also pass under
  sanitizers. Unchanged ISO payload, >4-GiB and encoder-failure evidence from
  CP36 and the shared writer/helper fault matrix are reused.
- One combined normal and sanitizer guest route uses the real uid/gid 1000
  client and production UDisksClient discovery. The guarded guest sets both
  disk/partition kernel read-only flags, then captures VHD, mounted VHDX, ISO
  and GPT FFU. Each job checks source SHA256 and retained BLKROGET state.
  VHD/FFU use one UDisks read acquisition; mounted VHDX/ISO each use one helper
  and wait through a held helper exit. All four outputs undergo the existing
  complete native verification. Independent QEMU VHD/VHDX decoding and kernel
  UDF file readback cover the new acquisitions; CP35's independent Img2Ffu
  encoder qualification is retained. Metadata-based write preflight and a
  native write target with deliberately stale writable metadata both refuse.
  The fixture alone clears protection to prepare GPT and perform one saved
  VHDX restore; whole-disk/FAT-file readback and BIOS boot complete that route.
- One normal Qt gate covers prepare-process, image-analysis Widgets, window,
  scaled window, UDisks target, full raw-write Widgets and full discovery.
  Removing the old excluded-read-only fixture exposed an obsolete index in
  the initial-device window case; its 50 passing prefix rows are retained and
  the remaining window functions pass together after the fixture correction.
  Other suites are not repeated. Optional existing image/companion skips are
  retained in the compact evidence.
- Preview 6 packages are built and inspected without host installation: five
  executables, both helper/policy argument matches, dependency/RPATH/desktop
  checks, documentation/licenses, headless CLI and one isolated GUI launch.

Evidence: `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp37/checks.json`, compact component/Qt/guest
logs, manifests and package checksums. Stable input binaries are retained
through each guest run. Disposable disks, exported captures and package stages
are removed after evidence export. The encoders and source cleanup protocols
are unchanged; only their read-only admission is extended. Existing geometry
and source-class bounds still apply. Physical read-only media, actual desktop
authorization UI and Windows mounting/deployment remain unqualified.
Remaining FFU capture/deployment layouts, VHD/VHDX parent/log handling, other
image operations and every remaining parity work group stay in scope.

## CP38 — VHD/VHDX parents and VHDX log replay, preview 7 (2026-10-19)

Deliver portable parent chains and dirty-log reading as one image batch. Windows
Rufus delegates VHD/VHDX reading to `OpenVirtualDisk` and read-only
`AttachVirtualDisk` in `src/vhd.c:MountImage`. Linux extends the existing native
source provider, keeping the decoded SHA256, confirmed DD, one authorization,
verified writer and joined READY protocol.

A retained graph opens each ordinary parent read-only and checks UUID/linkage,
virtual size/sector geometry and VHD parent modification time. VHD MSB and VHDX
LSB sector bitmaps select child versus inherited sectors; explicit zero states
remain zero. Identity/path checks bracket decoding. The helper checks ownership
before reading parent bytes, keeps every descriptor until final cleanup, and
includes every parent backing in target protection before unmount and after
exclusive claim. Partial parent opens, fallback attempts and failure paths close
all descriptors. Native parent paths use portable relative Unicode locators;
Windows drive/volume/UNC relocation and locator repair remain unsupported.

VHDX version-0 logs are read once, validate CRC-32C/header/descriptor/data-sector
integrity, find the newest complete circular sequence and replay its descriptors
in order. A bounded interval overlay provides data, zero ranges, overwritten
updates and virtual extension before reading regions, metadata or BAT entries.
Original headers, logs and parent files are never repaired or changed. The
support guide records the 32-file chain and log/BAT/work budgets. This native
immutable-source choice avoids privileged writes to user images and stale-path
repair; it differs from the operating system virtual-disk attachment service.

### One qualification batch

- Normal and ASan/UBSan run 56 grouped parent/replay checks: fixed and sparse
  dynamic VHD parents, multiple levels/block geometries, Unicode/relative/name
  fallback, absent/stale/unsafe parents, cycles/depth, retained replacement and
  mutation, VHDX 512/4096-sector bitmaps/full/zero/inherited blocks, dirty parents,
  circular/gapped/overlapping log records, zero ranges, virtual extension and
  replayed BAT/metadata. Invalid CRC/GUID/tail/sequence/descriptor/truncation and
  unknown-version cases refuse before output. Native regular-file writes use
  the retained graph and verify target bytes/tail; cancellation and descriptor
  counts are checked. Source hashes, size, mtime/ctime and the caller offset stay
  unchanged. Independent QEMU repairs and decodes a disposable dirty-log copy;
  the original remains byte-for-byte dirty. The existing 47 VHD and 40 VHDX
  source/fault/QEMU/write checks also pass under both builds. Shared writer and
  helper failure matrices are reused rather than copied for each chain format.
- One combined normal and sanitizer guest route uses one bootable seed, then
  ordinary Qt SELECT/confirmation/helper jobs for a small VHD child and VHDX
  child, plus one full 64-MiB VHDX restore requiring both parent inheritance and
  log replay. Each job uses one helper, physical readback and held-99/joined
  READY. Parent/child bytes stay unchanged. Real root-helper refusal covers a
  root-owned parent and a parent on the selected target, with the entire disk
  unchanged. Host disk/FAT-file readback, clean filesystem checks and BIOS
  `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK` complete each build's representative restore.
- One Qt gate runs prepare-source/process, image-analysis Widgets, window,
  scaled window, UDisks mount/target/discovery and the full raw-write Widgets
  suite. Existing optional real-image/companion skips remain unchanged.
- Preview 7 generic/Arch packages are built and inspected without host
  installation: five executables, both helper/policy argument matches,
  documentation/licenses, desktop metadata, empty RPATH, library resolution,
  headless help/version and one isolated GUI launch. No QEMU or additional
  virtual-disk runtime is required by the application.

Evidence: `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp38/checks.json`, grouped vectors, Qt/component
logs, stable guest binary manifests, disk/file hashes and package checksums.
Initial guest fixture failures occurred after the parent-on-target refusal:
the test attempted an exclusive claim while its own parent-file mount remained
attached. Cleanup ordering was fixed before both successful final routes.
Final source review tightened invalid circular-log scan termination and added
cancellation; the focused normal/sanitizer corpus was rerun on those final
reader objects, reusing the already-qualified valid guest/writer path. No
additional whole restore or fault matrix was scheduled for that refusal-path
correction. Disposable media and package stages are removed after evidence

and all remaining full-parity work remain unqualified/in scope.

References: [MS-VHDX log replay](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-vhdx/0d588e33-23a6-4c71-b27f-87d97ac3e914),
[parent locators](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-vhdx/4f4449cf-af59-45da-9045-c4950b9438b2),

## CP39 — FFU codecs, descriptor runs and capture names, preview 8 (2026-10-19)

Deliver remaining standard FFU codecs and descriptor/capture restrictions as
one batch. Windows Rufus delegates application to DISM `/Apply-Ffu` and saving
to `/Capture-Ffu` (`src/format.c`, `src/vhd.c`). Linux keeps the existing native
full single-store reconstruction and verified DD writer, adding MS-XCA LZNT1
and Huffman-XPRESS alongside uncompressed/default/plain-XPRESS. No new external
runtime decoder or privilege route is introduced.

The bounded decoders check tables/chunks, input consumption, match history and
exact output sizes, including optional markers and legal alternate long-length
forms. Huffman tables renew at 64-KiB output boundaries; LZNT1's length/distance
split follows the current position in each 4-KiB chunk. Grouped compressed
payloads use one cached decode, capped at 16 MiB decoded, and each logical block
retains its own SHA256 entry. Multi-block beginning/end-relative runs, repeated
destinations and last-write ordering are validated before reconstruction.
Sparse gaps invalidate the cached decoded group before zeroing, so a subsequent
reference to that group cannot consume overwritten cache bytes. All decoded
chunks, including superseded data, are checked before logical output.

FFU capture now permits unnamed and valid Unicode GPT names. Its uncompressed
payload retains exact GPT bytes. Optional manifest names are omitted for empty
or non-ASCII names, retaining an ASCII manifest; INI controls and malformed
UTF-16 are refused. This changes descriptive metadata rather than renaming GPT
partitions. Existing read-only acquisition, frozen source consistency, output
verification and atomic publication remain unchanged. Capture retains the
current GPT/geometry/size limits; no optimized or signed FFU is generated.

### One qualification batch

- A grouped normal and ASan/UBSan corpus passes 91 codec, descriptor, source,
  native-write/tail and capture checks. It covers 1-KiB through 1-MiB decoded
  buffers, literal/match chunk boundaries, LZNT1 displacement transitions,
  optional/alternate Huffman encodings, malformed/truncated tables/tokens,
  cancellation, all five FFU compression identifiers, grouped/repeated/end-
  relative destinations, overlap ordering, cache gaps, corruption before output,
  allocation/range bounds and unnamed/Unicode captures. Independent upstream
  wimlib 1.14.5 compresses real-match Huffman buffers and decodes reference
  vectors. Dissect independently decodes LZNT1 vectors. Existing saving (29) and
  FFU mapping/XPRESS/source/writer (59) checks pass normally and sanitized.
- Independent Img2Ffu validates chunk hashes and fully decodes unnamed and
  Unicode GPT captures; output SHA256/size matches the original 8-MiB disks.
  The existing oracle and dependencies are test-only. An exploratory EOF-driven
  Python Huffman decoder loses an output byte on lookahead padding or interprets
  an optional end symbol as a match; the exact-size wimlib decoder is used for
  that comparison. No production behavior was changed to match the EOF oracle.
- One combined normal and sanitizer guest route uses one bootable seed and
  ordinary Qt SELECT/confirmation/helper jobs for grouped LZNT1 and Huffman
  inputs, including end-relative runs, physical readback, preserved target tail,
  one helper per job and held-99/joined READY. One full 64-MiB LZNT1 restore
  per build receives host disk/FAT-file readback, a filesystem check and BIOS
  `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK`. Existing writer/helper faults and CP35–CP37 source,
  cancellation, cleanup and publication evidence are reused.
- One Qt gate runs prepare-source/process, image-analysis Widgets, window,
  scaled window, UDisks mount/target/discovery and the full raw-write Widgets
  suite. The raw suite reached its 600-second infrastructure limit under
  concurrent guest/build load after 1,550 completed data rows. Those rows and
  the other eight passing suites are retained; the remaining 50 data rows run
  together (51 passed including init/cleanup, one optional skip). The union
  covers all 1,600 data rows, equivalent to 1,597 passes and five existing
  optional skips with init/cleanup counted once. No full raw suite is repeated.
- Preview 8 generic/Arch packages are built without host installation and
  checked for five executables, both exact helper/policy argument matches,
  documentation/licenses, desktop metadata, empty RPATH, dependency resolution,
  headless help/version and one isolated GUI launch.

Initial full-guest fixtures represented every byte as a Huffman literal. Those
disposable runs were stopped after their small codec jobs succeeded, to avoid
spending the batch on repeated literal decoding under Debug/TCG/sanitizers.
The replacement encodes uniform 64-KiB chunks with real distance-one Huffman
matches and keeps nonuniform chunks as literals. Exact decoding is checked by
both native and upstream decoders; the full representative restore uses LZNT1,
with both codecs receiving real-device small jobs under the shared writer; the component corpus retains full literal
boundary cases. Final guest inputs remain stable throughout their runs. Sanitizer timing also exposed per-byte history-copy overhead; bounded growing
nonoverlapping memcpy spans preserve forward match semantics and remove that
overhead. The final focused corpus was rerun after this optimization. The
final focused corpus also removes an unnecessary canonical-length restriction
from Huffman decoding, with independent alternate-form agreement.

Evidence: `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp39/checks.json`, grouped component/Qt logs,
independent oracle reports, stable guest manifests, disk/file hashes and package
checksums. Disposable media and package staging are removed after export.
Target-aware portable/optimized resizing, partial-update base validation,
multi-store selection/deployment, SFU, signer trust and additional capture
layouts remain explicit FFU work. Full Windows parity, actual desktop polkit
UI and physical-media/Windows-deployment qualification are not claimed.

References: [MS-XCA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-xca/a8b7cb0a-92a6-4187-a23b-5e14273b96f8),
[LZNT1 buffer headers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-xca/cba0fa15-bd62-4eda-8838-8fc7ab406df1),
[Huffman encoding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-xca/c7ec7ba9-ca8f-448f-bb85-027c1516db1c),
[upstream wimlib](https://wimlib.net/) and
[Img2Ffu](https://github.com/MobileTooling/img2ffu).

## CP40 — target-aware full FFU deployment, preview 9 (2026-10-20)

One delivery batch changes ordinary full FFU installation from captured-size DD
to final sparse deployment at the selected target capacity. Read-only logical
analysis still reconstructs captured-size zero gaps for the decoded digest.
The separate layout digest hashes the verified FFU metadata/payload hash table
and is frozen from SELECT through confirmation, helper preflight, copy and
verification. The existing JSON `layoutSha256` field is shared by VTSI and FFU;
other providers reject it. The internal field is now `imageLayoutSha256`.

The FFU reader retains beginning/end-relative descriptors until target capacity
is known. Final extent resolution preserves last-write order and clips partial
overlaps between the two block grids when the target capacity is not an FFU
block multiple. Omitted regions are untouched. All original metadata and decoded
payload chunks, including overwritten payloads, are authenticated against the
image's SHA256 table before any deployment callback. These are integrity checks,
not catalog signer authentication.

For a larger GPT target, validate both captured GPT header CRCs, current/alternate
locations, usable range, disk GUID, matching table dimensions and contents,
table CRC and partition bounds before writing. Move the backup table/header to
the new end and update both header geometry/CRCs and protective MBR length.
Partition entries and filesystem sizes stay unchanged. GPT patch ranges
supersede covered image ranges; physical write/readback counters count each
final byte once. Sector sizes must match the manifest and FFU blocks must be
sector aligned. GPT tables are bounded to 4096 entries of at most 1024 bytes.
The existing shared writer retains source/target identity, claim, cancellation,
fsync after partial failure, readback, cleanup and READY after helper exit.

Qualification is grouped in `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp40`:

- One independent Python serializer/deployment oracle supplies 60 cases per
  normal/sanitizer build: all supported FFU versions/codecs, equal/larger and
  non-block-aligned targets, deterministic overlapping begin/end maps, gap
  preservation, 512/4096-byte GPT relocation, invalid backup refusal, frozen
  layout refusal, equal-content/different-map substitution in preflight/copy/
  verification, partial writes, EINTR, cancellation, sync and readback faults.
- Existing FFU parser/integrity, codec/capture variants, image saving, shared
  dense writer and VTSI writer suites run as one five-suite component group.
  CP39's independent codec comparisons and the established source/acquisition/
  helper fault matrix are reused. LeakSanitizer needs local process inspection
  outside the sandbox; the final sanitizer route retains leak checking.
- A focused FFU helper protocol suite covers strict layout fields, sparse
  counters, progress bounds, failure/cancellation and helper-exit joining.
  One relevant nine-suite Qt regression gate includes the full raw writer
  widgets, source/process, analysis, window/scaling and device-service suites.
- One combined QEMU route per build uses disposable tmpfs media. It retains one
  seed job, ordinary LZNT1 and Huffman-XPRESS end-relative jobs, an 8-MiB GPT FFU
  deployed to 64 MiB with unchanged partition entries and relocated CRC-valid
  headers/tables, and one representative full 64-MiB grouped LZNT1 restore.
  Each ordinary job uses one helper and holds at 99 until helper/launcher exit.
  Host disk/FAT readback and one SeaBIOS `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK` complete the route.
  No repeated claim matrix or codec-specific full boot is added.
- Release output comprises the Preview 9 Arch/CachyOS package and generic TGZ,
  inspected without installing. Disposable guest disks and package extraction/
  staging directories are removed after compact evidence export.

Ordinary full-image larger-target deployment is the finish line for this batch.
Optimized partition/filesystem resizing, partial-update base validation and
deployment, multi-store selection/deployment, catalog signer trust and additional
capture layouts remain explicit FFU work. Real 4Kn hardware and complete Windows
parity remain unqualified. Audit correction: Windows Rufus's FFU picker and
`/Apply-Ffu /ApplyDrive /ImageFile` invocation do not expose DISM's separate
`/SFUFile` workflow; the speculative CP39 SFU item adds no Rufus parity requirement.

## CP41 — exact-sector FFU capture and adaptive sizing, preview 10 (2026-10-20)

One end-to-end batch removes the artificial 128-KiB device-size multiple and
128-GiB ceiling from FFU saving. The native reader now emits final map extents
and zero gaps at exact manifest capacity. Beginning/end grids can overlap at
sector boundaries inside chunks. Full mapped blocks must still fit the disk;
no out-of-range payload bytes are silently clipped or written.

The encoder reads all complete beginning-relative blocks, then reads one full
block anchored at the exact source end. The source hash and copy progress count
only previously unread bytes in that tail. Overlap contents participate in the
saved-image comparison and final source reread, retaining consistency detection.
A shared pure geometry planner supplies both output preflight and capture.
It chooses power-of-two chunks, normally starting at 128 KiB and increasing to
16 MiB, within the reader's 64-MiB descriptor/hash/map/payload-index budgets.
The current dense bound on x86-64 is 32 TiB minus 64 MiB. These large sizes are
qualified by arithmetic planning checks; no actual multi-terabyte capture is
claimed. Capture remains full uncompressed V1 with existing GPT/manifest bounds.

Qualification and evidence are grouped in `.rufus-test-artifacts/cp41`:

- One normal/sanitizer corpus provides 58 cases: all codecs across 512/4096-byte
  tails, exact logical hashes and equal-size target readback, actual captures
  reconstructed by an independent Python FFU decoder with every chunk hash
  checked, exact output-size planning, short I/O, cancellation, source mutation,
  large-size planner transitions and actual 2/4/8/16-MiB chunk decoding.
- One six-suite component group reuses image saving, FFU parser/integrity,
  codec/capture variants, CP40's target-aware deployment/substitution/fault
  cases, and shared dense/VTSI write qualification. Authorization, publication,
  source/claim and helper fault matrices are reused. Sanitizers retain address,
  undefined-behavior and leak checks with authorized local process inspection.
- One combined QEMU route per build captures an unmounted, kernel-read-only
  8-MiB-plus-1536-byte block source through `SaveDeviceImage`. The source's
  SHA256 and read-only state are checked. Ordinary Qt SELECT/confirmation/DD
  then installs the saved FFU on the 64-MiB target and verifies unchanged GPT
  entries with relocated headers/CRCs. The source backing hash remains exact.
  One full grouped LZNT1 FFU restore supplies independent disk/FAT readback and
  SeaBIOS `RUFUS_RAW_BOOT_OK`. Each Qt job uses one helper and holds at 99 until
  launcher exit. The unchanged save authorization/publication flow was already
  qualified in CP35/37; the new guest source tests native encoder geometry.
- One relevant nine-suite Qt regression gate runs after builds. Preview 10 is
  packaged as native Arch/CachyOS and generic TGZ output, inspected without
  host installation. Compact logs/manifests/checksums are exported and all
  disposable guest disks and packaging stages are removed.

Optimized FFU partition/filesystem resizing, partial-update base deployment,
multi-store handling, signer trust, remaining dense/manifest/capture restrictions,
real 4Kn hardware and the full Windows feature backlog remain active. This
checkpoint establishes its stated capture/geometry finish line only.

## CP47 — full and quick formatting, preview 16 (2026-10-20)

Enable the existing Quick format checkbox and freeze its choice with the job.
Match Windows's quick-only large-FAT32 rule and cleared/disabled DD checkbox,

only the selected volume under its own exclusive partition claim, then hands
off to the native formatter for metadata. Native NTFS full formatting
selects --full on ntfsprogs-plus or removes -Q for NTFS-3G's full default after
bounded capability checks. Unsupported quick-only tools fail before partitioning.
exFAT uses native -f with check-written/no-discard; ext3/ext4 disable lazy journal
initialization, including persistence. ext2 retains Windows's equivalent full/
quick behavior. Full format does not imply a whole-disk erase outside the volume.

Remove the 120-second absolute formatter deadline only for full jobs. Preserve
cancellation, TERM/KILL escalation, reaping, sync, metadata verification, one
authorization and READY after cleanup/helper exit. FAT stops on a zeroing/readback
I/O error instead of marking a bad cluster and hiding incomplete verification;
Windows's formatter can mark unusable clusters. This is a deliberate Linux
refusal. Independent bad-block/fake-capacity modes remain separate parity work.

creation; actual NTFS-3G full formatting and physical media are not newly qualified.

## CP51 — old-BIOS compatibility, preview 20 (2026-10-20)

Implement the original advanced checkbox through shared partition placement,
GUI cluster/filesystem selection, frozen strict requests and all helper MBR
option constructions. Default off; retain session preference while unsupported
modes clear/disable the effective option. BIOS-bootable MBR routes use twice the
track rounded up to cluster, plus an inactive final one-track 0xEA compatibility
partition unless UEFI:NTFS takes priority. Persistence precedes the final extra.
No new CHS cheat is invented; the Windows source also leaves its CHS-fix TODO.

Libfdisk's default first-LBA restriction otherwise rejects a start below 1 MiB.
For this mode set its sector grain and first LBA after creating the DOS label;
stored start/size still come from shared Rufus rules and independent readback.
Original GRUB2/GRUB4DOS gap checks remain. Linux refuses a too-large SBR before
writing, whereas Windows performs the same fit check in `WriteSBR` after format.
READY, claims, cancellation, sync, one authorization and source protection remain.

## CP53 — explicit FFU stores, preview 22 (2026-10-20)

V2 FFUs with multiple stores now offer an explicit store chooser. The list shows
one-based store numbers, capacities and source UEFI device paths. START stays
disabled until the chosen store passes complete analysis. The retained source
identity is checked again after choosing; cancellation or a changed source stops
selection. Confirmation identifies the store. The strict optional `store` field
freezes it through native preflight and the single authorized helper. Legacy
requests may omit it for a single-store image; multiple stores never default to
one. The native layout digest binds the chosen store even when two stores have
identical decoded content.

All store headers/descriptors are bounded and parsed in metadata order; payloads
follow all metadata. Metadata hashes authenticate the chooser, and every store's
payload hashes are checked before any logical output or target writes. Only the
selected store contributes writes, end-relative placement, GPT relocation and
partial-update base comparisons. Other stores' ranges are never applied to the
selected device. Existing sector/chunk/map/table bounds, source protection,
claims, sync/readback, cleanup and READY after helper/launcher exit remain.

Windows Rufus delegates FFU deployment to DISM with the selected physical drive.
This Linux route makes the store explicit for its one selected target. Source
UEFI device paths are displayed for identification; they are not resolved into
host devices or used to write additional disks. Automatic multi-target/UEFI-LUN
mapping, optimized partition/filesystem resizing and catalog signer trust remain
unqualified and pending. Full Windows parity remains active.

Qualification is one batch:

- One 25-case corpus per normal/sanitizer build covers three stores with distinct
  512/4096-byte sector geometries and exact capacities, logical reconstruction,
  equal/larger dirty targets, overwritten/repeated/end-relative runs, invalid or
  omitted choices, corruption in unselected payloads, inconsistent headers,
  selected-only partial base comparisons and frozen identity for identical stores.
  Eight native FFU suites and the existing FFU helper-process suite run together.
  Reuse the unchanged helper claim/sync/cleanup matrix.
- A cached independent Img2Ffu V2 encoder (commit d0dda2b2e138dd0412018bc733e64d1a92c385b0)
  emits two GPT stores. Both selected logical disks reconstruct exactly, including
  separate data and partition names. The sources and generated FFU are temporary.
- Focused chooser/Widgets cases cover either store, Cancel and a source changed
  while choosing. Strict protocol cases cover legacy omission, one-based bounds,
  exact integer types and refusing the field for other formats. Run one full
  nine-suite normal Qt gate and focused new Widgets cases under sanitizers.
- Each combined kernel-7.2.11-arch1-1 guest selects/writes both small stores through
  the ordinary SelectionController, checks independent kernel readback and untouched
  tails, then restores a full bootable image from store 2 in a separate container.
  Every job freezes the store before authorization, launches once, holds below
  READY until helper/launcher exit, syncs and reads back. One final independent FAT
  inspection and BIOS boot qualify the shared writer per build. The Qt Widgets
  dialog itself is covered by the focused desktop fixture.
- The initial native probe assumed every calloc had count 1; keep its byte budget
  while allowing bounded array allocations. The first guest fixture left its new
  image owned by root; pre-authorization ownership validation refused it. Chown the
  fixture to its simulated caller, retain the failure log and run the combined
  normal/sanitizer route. Neither correction weakens production checks.
- Inspect Preview 22 native/generic packages without installation, retain compact

the complete Windows feature backlog stay active.


## CP54 — FFU catalog signature policy, preview 23 (2026-10-20)

FFU input now validates a present catalog as a bounded PKCS#7 Microsoft CTL.
Unsigned catalogs remain accepted. Linux also retains its existing catalog-free
FFU input compatibility: these sources have no signer identity and receive the
same chunk-integrity checks as unsigned CTLs. Windows normally parses a CTL
even for unsigned input; keeping already-supported catalog-free images usable
is an explicit Linux compatibility difference. For a signed
catalog, the first cryptographically valid signer is selected; invalid signatures,
changed signed content and missing signer certificates refuse before logical
output, store listing or target writes. As Windows desktop DISM does, the reader
accepts test/self-signed and expired certificates and rejects its two known
production-chain SHA-1 thumbprints. It does not consult the host trust store,
fetch certificates, apply host clock/revocation policy or claim publisher trust.
A fixed public Microsoft Root Certificate Authority 2010 certificate lets an
included production intermediate reach the same root without host PKI state.

The policy was checked against the static FFU provider shipped in the user's
Windows 11 25H2 ISO. No Windows application was executed. Catalog signatures
cover the CTL contents; payload and metadata chunk hashes are still checked
separately. This preserves the observed desktop policy and does not add a new
requirement to match a CTL member to the FFU hash table. The entire catalog's
SHA-256 is additionally bound into the frozen Linux layout identity, so changing
to another valid catalog cannot retain the selected job's identity. Catalogs
are limited to 16 MiB. FFU saving continues to produce unsigned catalogs.

Qualification groups native normal/sanitizer signature and file-writer cases,
independent osslsigncode signing/verification, a genuine Windows production CAT
refusal, combined normal/sanitizer Qt guests, one Qt gate and inspected native/
generic packages. Each guest applies selected stores from signed FFUs, verifies
readback and source retention, then performs one full restore and BIOS boot.
Existing shared helper faults are reused. Evidence is in
`../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp54/`; disposable disks and package stages are removed.

Optimized partition/filesystem resizing and automatic multi-target/UEFI-LUN
mapping remain pending. Static format findings for the next resizing batch:
`[FullFlash] Optimized=True` identifies a single non-first `UseAllSpace=True`
partition. Windows shifts following begin-relative descriptors in 128-KiB units,
aligns the following partition to 1 MiB, updates GPT geometry and extends the
selected filesystem, with recovery metadata updated afterward. Implementation
must handle the filesystem and recovery consequences together; descriptor
relocation alone does not complete this behavior. Full Windows parity remains
active.


CP54 final evidence: 48 catalog cases pass in each normal/sanitizer build,
including a genuine production CAT, mixed production/test signer ordering,
invalid signatures, source substitution and file-writer prewrite refusals.
Nine existing FFU component/protocol suites per build retain their coverage.
The expired-certificate fixture uses explicit historical CA dates. A real mixed-
signer test exposed that `PKCS7_dup` sorts the signer SET; verification now copies
the selected original signer explicitly before inspecting its certificate chain.
Only catalog cases and combined guests were repeated for that correction.

The single full nine-suite Qt run passed all 1,621 widget assertions with five
existing optional skips, but CTest reached its 600-second wall-clock deadline
at shutdown. Only that widget executable was repeated, with a 900-second limit:
it passed the same assertions and exited successfully after 521.8 seconds.
The other eight Qt suites were not repeated. Both final guests match the current
binary hashes, apply two small selected stores and one 64-MiB bootable store,
verify ten restored FAT files independently, and boot successfully. Disposable
media is removed; compact manifests and transcripts record the exact scope.

and instance waiting, saved advanced panels and automatic/persistent session logs.
Ctrl+L/P and Alt+R/U retain their original roles. No device-write semantics or
helper protocol changes are introduced.

The focused normal and ASan/UBSan/LSan groups each pass 16 real cases, excluding
lifecycle hooks: startup, filename detection, INI key/value compatibility and
profile reset, full-session log retention/replacement, a real competing process
and wait/release, device units, ordinary/persistent logging, portable GUI and
remembered panels. Existing GUI tests now isolate settings/data paths so no
user profile is written. A full build also identified a historical GRUB fixture
missing newer unsupported-method stubs; its two representative FAT32/NTFS paths
pass after the fixture is completed. It cannot acquire host devices.

The batch gate is one established nine-suite Qt run. CP58 and earlier device
writer/helper/polkit/fault/cleanup/READY evidence is reused; no new device guests,
Windows execution or installation matrix is required. Commands and compact
results are under `../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp59/`, with `checks.json` as the final
receipt. Preview metadata changes from 27 to 28 are release-only; the Qt gate covers unchanged runtime behavior apart from the displayed version,
and the focused group covers the final startup/storage/logging sources. Native/TGZ package inspection
covers policy/helper paths, system libraries, docs, headless CLI and isolated GUI
startup with private settings/data/runtime storage. No host installation is done.

Localization, updates/download selection and the other unfinished groups remain
in the active full Windows parity goal.

## CP60 — UDF and ext data-format layouts, Preview 29 (2026-10-21)

The [filesystem batch](linux-filesystem-formatting.md) adds native UDF revisions
1.02/1.50/2.00/2.01 and non-bootable ext2/ext3 on MBR/GPT/SFD, preserving the
original advanced visibility, 256-MiB ext minimum and Default cluster choice.
One strict native-format operation reuses the existing authorized helper,
partition/claim/sync/cleanup pipeline and READY-after-exit gate. UDF also uses
the existing icon/extended-label and supplementary ZIP writers.

The grouped normal and ASan/UBSan/LSan component gates each pass 80 real cases
(15 new native/protocol cases, 54 format-policy cases and 11 desktop cases),
excluding lifecycle hooks. All nine filesystem/layout requests round-trip and
reject contradictory fields. Real file formats cover all four revisions,
Unicode/empty labels, full/quick behavior and bounded metadata corruption/refusal.
The first sanitizer run's assertions passed but LeakSanitizer could not work
inside the tracing sandbox; the authorized unprivileged run outside it passes
with leak detection enabled. Both records are retained.

One combined guest per build drives four ordinary Qt jobs on an owned 320-MiB
simulated USB: UDF/GPT/quick with icons and a Unicode ZIP overlay, UDF/SFD/full,
ext2/SFD/quick and ext3/MBR/full. Independent kernel mounts verify files,
labels/journal metadata and released claims. Every job checks one authorization,
held progress until helper exit and joined READY. The minimal fixture required
an independent archive backing mount, its usual `/dev/block` partition alias
and a readback parent directory; original failing logs remain in the receipt.
No production protection was weakened to accommodate those fixture omissions.

Existing shared fault/polkit/boot evidence is reused; these are non-bootable
formats, with no new bootloader or Windows execution/installation matrix.
The batch uses one established nine-suite full Qt gate. Commands, source/provider
hashes, transcripts, package checks and cleanup are recorded under
`../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp60/`, with `checks.json` as the final delivery receipt.
That gate passes 2,191 real cases and finds three old filesystem-list assertions.
Updating those expectations also identifies a selector omission: SFD eligibility
must consider UDF when the older filesystems do not fit a tiny device. The
affected normal/sanitizer group passes 14 cases, including UDF-only 2-MiB SFD
selection and refusal below the minimum, bringing covered Qt cases to 2,194.
The five pre-existing optional skips are retained. The completed 320-MiB guest
routes already satisfy the selector's earlier FAT branch and remain unchanged;
no full Qt or guest matrix is repeated for this selector correction.
Initial debug/guest gates use Preview 28 metadata; the final affected Qt group
and Release use 29. Native/TGZ inspection checks the final
provider path, policy/helper pair, runtime dependencies, docs, headless CLI and
isolated portable startup. No provider or application is installed on the host.

UDF 2.50/2.60 HD metadata partitions are not implemented by udftools 2.3 and
remain provider work. ReFS formatting, further sector/geometry cases, DOS
attribute/label discovery and the other backlog groups remain in the active
full Windows parity goal. Large owned guest media are removed after log export.


## CP61 — runtime UEFI validation and checksum maintenance, Preview 30 (2026-10-21)

The [runtime batch](linux-runtime-validation.md) shares Windows eligibility and
its session checkbox behavior, freezes the optional helper flag, streams source
MD5s before edits, repairs only explicitly changed entries, tracks generated
SWMs and actual Windows file replacements, preserves original EFI loaders and
installs the six unchanged bundled validators. Existing wrong source digests
remain wrong. Source backup/list/space checks precede target writes, and all
collector descriptors close before private-mount cleanup.

The five focused suites pass 203 real cases per normal and ASan/UBSan/LSan
build, excluding lifecycle hooks. One combined networkless guest per build
creates FAT16/FAT32/NTFS media through ordinary Qt, verifies independent
manifest/config/resource/original-loader bytes, checks one authorization and
held-exit/joined READY, and reacquires released claims. A direct-helper backup
conflict leaves the complete disk unchanged. Final NTFS media boots a bare EFI
marker through UEFI:NTFS and the validator; a one-byte damaged copy reports one
failure and never automatically chains to the original loader. No Windows
application or installation runs.

Initial fixture logs retain the missing raw-controller bus setup, corrected
MD5SUMS/generated-list expectations, absent second-partition udev alias, and
corruption controls that matched NTFS resident/stale data. Distinct nonresident
control data fixes the fixture. Production protections are unchanged. The
source-size progress hint can differ after config length changes, as in Windows.

One complete normal build precedes the established nine-suite Qt batch gate.
That run passes 2,193 real cases and retains five existing optional skips. Two
older legacy-GRUB rows fail: a cleanup target comparison and a following
analysis/UI timeout. Both pass immediately in the targeted normal and sanitizer
reruns without source changes. The cause is unestablished; the receipt preserves
the failing full run and both focused passes. Across those runs 2,195 distinct
Qt cases pass; this is not a wholly green single full-suite run.
The earlier unchanged shared helper fault/polkit and customization evidence is
reused. Debug/guest gates use Preview 29 metadata; Preview 30 changes only
release metadata. Native/TGZ inspection covers the matching helper/policy,
dependencies, CLI/isolated GUI startup, new guide and validator license/notice.
Commands, exact results, source/package hashes and cleanup are in
`../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp61/checks.json`. Temporary guest disks and package
stages are removed; user ISOs are preserved. Secure Boot/revocation and all
other unfinished Windows features remain in the active parity goal.

## CP62 — bundled Secure Boot checks and START warning, Preview 31 (2026-10-21)

One [Secure Boot batch](linux-secure-boot.md) implements bounded native PE digest,
certificate issuer, DBX, SSP, SBAT, Windows SVN and expert-certificate metadata
classification. Shared fallback text and seven original DBX resources retain
the Windows data; Windows source/project lists include the extracted header.
The original path classifies certificate metadata rather than authenticating
publishers or checking the actual firmware trust store, and Linux keeps that
boundary. Remote policy refresh remains a separate download/update backlog item.

Normal and ASan/UBSan/LSan groups each cover 206 real checks: 30 component cases,
174 existing image-analysis cases and two focused UI cases. Generated certificates
and PE fixtures exercise hash exclusions, classification/precedence and malformed
bounds/cycles. The actual analysis worker inspects an ISO containing a generated
certificate-bearing SBAT-revoked EFI fixture; the UI checks default Cancel, cancel/continue,
zero authorization before ordinary confirmation and unchanged target bytes.
Initial UI logs retain the deferred-dialog deletion assertion and the fixture's
missing EFI subsystem field. The fixed fixture uses the existing preflight;
no production guard is weakened. The original cancellation test wrapped the
reporting adapter's underlying function instead of the scan entry point; wrapping
the direct scan query fixes the test. Full image-analysis results are reused
after fixture-only changes; affected core/UI cases are rerun together.

One combined networkless guest per build exercises the new read-only analysis
through ordinary FAT16/FAT32/NTFS creation. Independent manifests/configs/resources/
original EFI readback, released claims, backup prewrite refusal, one authorization
and held-exit/joined READY pass. The final NTFS media boots the unchanged validator
to a bare native EFI marker; one damaged payload byte yields exactly one failure
and an unanswered continue prompt. No Windows execution/installation or host
block-device writes occur. The helper/write contract is unchanged, so its older
fault/polkit/customization evidence is reused.

A full normal build precedes one nine-suite Qt gate, after both guests and all
build work finish. It passes all 2,196 real cases and retains the five existing
optional skips. CP61's two legacy-GRUB rows do not recur; no source change was
made to those rows and the original failures remain documented. Native/TGZ inspection covers helper/policy paths, libraries,
CLI/isolated startup and the new guide. Debug/focused/guest/Qt metadata is Preview
30; only release metadata changes to 31. Exact commands/results, source/resource/
package hashes and cleanup are recorded in `../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp62/checks.json`.
Temporary media/stages are removed after evidence export. Broader chain/firmware,
remote policy updates and all remaining Windows features stay in the active goal.


## CP63 — remote policy refresh and atomic DBX cache, Preview 32 (2026-10-21)

One [policy update batch](linux-policy-updates.md) implements original session
SBAT/active/revoked list refresh, interval-selected DBX timestamp checks, one
download decision, normal/portable atomic caching, settings/manual/cancellation
controls and frozen next-selection policy. The shared bounded HTTP transport
also preserves the existing detached-signature download behavior. Remote
policy feeds use the original HTTPS/structural-validation boundary; cache
SHA-256 binds storage contents and does not authenticate publishers.

The native DBX envelope deliberately stores original bytes, architecture,
UTC timestamp and checksum in one atomic JSON file instead of Windows's raw
file and separate registry timestamp. Interrupted/failed replacement cannot
leave a mismatched pair. Owned regular-file reads, strict size/schema/DBX
validation and bundled fallback cover unusable cache entries. The shared
DBX URLs/timestamps and bundled resource bytes remain unchanged; only metadata
constness and its generator change for C++ reuse.

Normal and ASan/UBSan/LSan groups each pass 118 distinct real cases: 61 retained
signed-download, 30 Secure Boot component, 22 policy/update/cache, three window
and two selected creation-widget cases. Initial groups passed before the final
startup/absent-architecture fixes; only the affected 27 cases per build rerun.
Real loopback HTTP/TLS fixtures cover redirects, signed verification, malformed/
missing/chunked/oversized responses, one DBX choice, cache failure/corruption,
UTC time, offline retention and reentrant cancellation. Public HTTPS samples
record current text-list/GitHub metadata compatibility without execution.
The GUI exercises actual consent/settings and confirms that current image
reports remain frozen until reselection. No host settings inference, helper
protocol or device-write semantics change.

The full normal build and sanitizer guest-target build finish before their
respective tests; Ninja uses default parallelism. One combined networkless guest
per build passes FAT16/FAT32/NTFS creation, independent readback, one authorization,
released claims, held-exit/joined READY and prewrite backup refusal. The final
NTFS media boots a bare native EFI marker through the unchanged validator;
the damaged control reports one failure and waits at an unanswered prompt.
Both guest media trees are deleted after compact evidence export. No host media,
Windows execution or installation is used.

One nine-suite Qt gate passes 2,198 real cases, retains five existing optional
skips and fails one older keyboard-navigation assertion: enabling Settings puts
it between About and Log in the existing tab order. The test now checks Settings
focus explicitly. The entire 87-case window suite then passes normal and
sanitizer builds; no production behavior changes for this repair. Across the
gate and repair runs 2,199 distinct Qt cases pass. This is not a wholly green
single full-suite run, and the original failure/transcript is retained. No
second full gate or unchanged guest/fault matrix is run for a test expectation.

Debug/focused/guest/full-gate metadata is Preview 31; Release and repaired window
suites use revision 32. The metadata revision and obsolete keyboard expectation
are the only changes after the full gate. Native/TGZ inspection covers matching
helper/policy paths, dependencies, CLI, isolated portable startup, documentation
and licenses. Exact commands/results, source/resource/package hashes and cleanup
are in `../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp63/checks.json`. Package staging is removed.
Existing shared helper fault/polkit and agreed customization evidence is reused.
The complete Windows parity goal remains active, including application binary
updates, image download selection, localization and all other unresolved rows.

## CP70 — NTFS compression and indexing (Preview 39)

Delivered session Alt+N compression, saved Alt+Q indexing, strict frozen NTFS

fallback. [NTFS options](linux-ntfs-options.md) records original behavior,

changes, so the helper temporarily changes the private parent's directory
default around boot-file creation and always restores it before payload writes.
A required restoration failure fails the incomplete job. Ordinary NTFS creation
keeps the kernel provider; larger clusters continue uncompressed, as on Windows.

Each job verifies one authorization, joined full READY and released claims.
A missing required provider refuses before writes and preserves the disk hash.
Both guests then boot the original UEFI:NTFS/native EFI fixture.

optional skips, zero failures. Native/TGZ Preview39 packages were inspected,

`../.rufus-test-artifacts/cp70/checks.json`.
